A first decisive theorem would be log-convexity of the renewal sequence generated by irreducible bridges.  In exact tests through $n=23$ ($b_{23}=862{,}447{,}881$, extending the previously enumerated range), every inequality from $n=5$ holds, minimum ratio $1.00081$; a violation would mark a second curvature reversal in a sequence believed monotone-regular.

\section{Monotone transport in the length}

\begin{conjecture}[Bridge height rises in likelihood-ratio order]\label{af4}
For every $n\ge1$ the bridge height satisfies $H_n\le_{\mathrm{lr}}H_{n+1}$: for all $h_1<h_2$, $B(n,h_2)B(n+1,h_1)\le B(n,h_1)B(n+1,h_2)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Likelihood-ratio order is the strongest standard stochastic order: it asserts total positivity of order two for the full array $B(n,h)$, implies stochastic and hazard-rate dominance, and gives a single-crossing structure for the height laws that renewal and unfolding arguments could exploit.  The obstruction is that uniform reweighting across lengths need not preserve the geometric bias of an added step; no total-positivity statement appears in the bridge literature~\cite{HW62,DG19}.  Proposition~\ref{af:height} proves the top corner of the law at every length: the four leading diagonals are explicit polynomials and the two top adjacent cross-products are $2(n-1)(n+1)$ and $\tfrac43(n-2)(n-1)(n^2-n-3)$, positive always, so the conjectured order is a theorem where the array is thinnest.  A first decisive theorem would be TP${}_2$ of the full array in a strip of bounded height, where transfer matrices apply.  In exact integer tests of all cross-products, not only adjacent ones, for $n\le22$, every inequality holds; a counterexample would exhibit a height at which longer bridges become relatively rarer, breaking single-crossing.

\begin{conjecture}[Monotone coupling of the absolute endpoint]\label{af5}
For every $n\ge0$ there is a coupling of $U_n$ and $U_{n+2}$ under which $(|X_n|,|Y_n|)\le(|X_{n+2}|,|Y_{n+2}|)$ coordinatewise almost surely.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is the strongest of the transport laws: a single coupling forcing every increasing functional of the absolute endpoint to grow when two steps are added, in a model where even the growth of $\mathbf E[R_n^2]$ is a recorded open problem~\cite{MS93,BDGS12}.  The conjecture strictly implies that open monotonicity along each parity class, and much more: all upper-orthant probabilities and all increasing moments grow.  The parity shift respects bipartiteness, and the statement is distributional, since an individual walk can move inward over two steps.  Strassen's theorem makes each instance finitely decidable: the coupling exists if and only if every upper-set inequality holds, checked here by exact integer maximum flow.  A first decisive theorem would be the marginal law $|X_n|\le_{\mathrm{st}}|X_{n+2}|$.  In exact max-flow tests for every $n\le19$, the transport deficit is zero in all cases; a counterexample at some larger $n$ would exhibit an explicit increasing endpoint event whose probability falls with length, a finite-size reversal of excluded-volume swelling and a sharp datum about the open problem.

\begin{conjecture}[Monotone coupling of the span vector]\label{af6}
For every $n\ge0$ there is a coupling under which $(S_x,S_y)$ at length $n$ is coordinatewise dominated by $(S_x,S_y)$ at length $n+2$ almost surely.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Spans grow along any fixed path, but truncating a uniform $(n+2)$-step walk does not give a uniform $n$-step walk, so pathwise monotonicity does not transfer to the ensembles; the conjecture says the reweighting never overturns it, in the strongest product-order sense.  Every increasing functional of the bounding box, the area proxy $S_xS_y$, escape probabilities from rectangles, and mixed span moments would then grow monotonically along parity, providing monotone finite-volume approximants for the confinement and compression ensembles studied in~\cite{BBO25}.  Because spans are pathwise monotone, an extension-biased coupling corrected by local surgeries is a plausible mechanism, unlike for the endpoint.  A first decisive theorem would be stochastic growth of $\max(S_x,S_y)$.  In exact max-flow tests for every $n\le19$, all transport deficits vanish; a counterexample would locate a box size whose escape probability falls when two steps are added.

\begin{conjecture}[Span likelihood-ratio expansion]\label{af7}
For every $n\ge0$, $S_{x,n}\le_{\mathrm{lr}}S_{x,n+2}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Marginally, Conjecture~\ref{af6} gives only stochastic growth of $S_x$; this law upgrades it to likelihood-ratio order, total positivity of the span-count array on each parity class, controlling the odds of large against small spans and yielding single-crossing tail structure for confinement estimates.  Transfer matrices organize square-lattice walks by width, so the natural target is a positivity-preserving operator whose minors encode the order, the same structure conjectured for bridges in Conjecture~\ref{af4}.  The span-conjugate ensembles of~\cite{BBO25} give the nearest literature, with no ordering statements in the length.  A first decisive theorem would be TP${}_2$ for spans confined to a strip of width three.  In exact integer tests of all cross-products for $n\le19$, every inequality holds; a counterexample would give a span value whose relative odds fall with length, breaking the single-crossing picture.

\begin{conjecture}[Stochastic growth of the contact count]\label{af8}
For every $n\ge2$, $C_n\le_{\mathrm{st}}C_{n+1}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Extending a fixed walk cannot destroy contacts, but the uniform law at length $n+1$ reweights $n$-step prefixes by their atmospheres, and contact-rich walks have systematically smaller atmospheres if Conjecture~\ref{af12} is right, a selection bias working against the pathwise gain; the conjecture asserts the gain always wins at every tail threshold.  In particular, the normalized partition factor $Z_n(u)/c_n$ is then nondecreasing in $n$ for every $u\ge1$ and nonincreasing for $u\le1$, a monotonicity statement bearing on the attractive regime $u>1$, where even the existence of the limiting free energy remains open, in contrast to the repulsive regime settled by subadditivity.  The contact-scaling literature~\cite{BOS01} and the interacting-walk estimates of~\cite{BGJ20} study the marginals; no stochastic monotonicity in length appears there.  A first decisive theorem would be monotonicity of $\mathbf P(C_n\ge1)$.  In exact tail tests for all $n\le20$, every cross-multiplied inequality holds; a counterexample would exhibit a contact level whose tail probability falls with length, quantifying the atmosphere selection effect.

\section{Dependence laws at fixed length}

\begin{conjecture}[Negative quadrant dependence of the two spans]\label{af9}
For every $n\ge1$, $(S_x,S_y)$ is negatively quadrant dependent under $U_n$: $\mathbf P(S_x\ge a,S_y\ge b)\le\mathbf P(S_x\ge a)\,\mathbf P(S_y\ge b)$ for all $a,b$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A fixed step budget makes the two axes compete: horizontal extension consumes steps and room that vertical extension needs, and the conjecture asserts the competition at every joint tail, not merely in the covariance, which is $-2.283$ at $n=16$.  The retained negative control sharpens the claim: the same statement for $(|X_n|,|Y_n|)$ is false already at $n=3$, so the negative dependence is a property of accumulated geometry, not of symmetry or of the step budget alone.  The uniform self-avoiding measure has no known FKG or negative-association structure, so any proof would introduce a genuinely new correlation inequality; a natural route is a negative-lattice property of the bivariate span counts after a cumulative transform.  A first decisive theorem would be $\mathrm{Cov}(S_x,S_y)\le0$ for all $n$.  In exact tests of every upper-tail determinant through $n=21$, all signs are as conjectured; a counterexample would locate a scale at which two-axis extension becomes cooperative rather than competitive.

\begin{conjecture}[Positive quadrant dependence of radius and atmosphere]\label{af10}
For every $n\ge1$, $(R_n^2,A_n)$ is positively quadrant dependent under $U_n$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The atmosphere is a microscopic escape capacity and the radius a macroscopic extension observable; the conjecture couples them at every joint tail: walks that have travelled far are locally more extendable.  Through the identity $\mathbf E[A_n]=c_{n+1}/c_n$, the law ties endpoint geometry to the one-step coefficient ratio, and it would give a comparison principle for atmospheric sampling methods, whose attrition and weights are controlled by exactly this quantity~\cite{RJvR08,OP08}; the atmospheric-collapse computations of~\cite{AJvR09} point the same way qualitatively, with no formal correlation statement located anywhere.  Because $A_n$ is itself an extension count, the conjectured family of inequalities is equivalent to the average atmosphere inside radial upper sets dominating the global average, a formulation open to direct extension-counting attack.  A first decisive theorem would be $\mathrm{Cov}(R_n^2,A_n)\ge0$ for all $n$, the covariance being $+4.636$ at $n=16$.  In exact tests of every upper-tail determinant through $n=21$, all signs hold; a counterexample would exhibit a radius beyond which far endpoints are paradoxically more caged.

\begin{conjecture}[Negative quadrant dependence of radius and contacts]\label{af11}
For every $n\ge1$, $(R_n^2,C_n)$ is negatively quadrant dependent under $U_n$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Contacts reward folding, displacement requires extension, and the conjecture makes the opposition exact at every pair of thresholds.  Its weakest consequence is already the physically central sign: differentiating the interacting-walk expectation at the athermal point gives $\partial_\beta\mathbf E_\beta[R_n^2]\big|_{\beta=0}=\mathrm{Cov}(R_n^2,C_n)\le0$, so an infinitesimal attraction shrinks the mean-square displacement, the folklore mechanism of collapse~\cite{BOS01,BGJ20} for which no rigorous finite-$n$ sign result appears to be known.  The full quadrant law is far stronger, coupling every increasing function of radius negatively with every increasing function of contact number.  A natural strengthening to test first is whether the contact-conditioned radius laws fall in likelihood-ratio order, which would imply the quadrant law; the enumerated joint tables permit exactly that screening.  A first decisive theorem would be the covariance sign alone.  In exact tests of every upper-tail determinant through $n=21$, all signs hold; a counterexample would put a threshold pair at which attraction and extension cooperate, a genuine surprise for the collapse picture.

\begin{conjecture}[Negative quadrant dependence of contacts and atmosphere]\label{af12}
For every $n\ge1$, $(C_n,A_n)$ is negatively quadrant dependent under $U_n$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Contact-rich conformations are locally crowded, and the conjecture asserts that the crowding reaches the endpoint at every joint tail: attraction suppresses extendability.  Its covariance consequence, $\partial_\beta\mathbf E_\beta[A_n]\big|_{\beta=0}\le0$ with $\mathbf E_0[A_n]=c_{n+1}/c_n$, says that switching on attraction immediately lowers the expected number of legal extensions, the mechanism by which the collapse transition throttles growth ratios, seen qualitatively in the atmospheric-collapse study~\cite{AJvR09}.  Jointly with Conjecture~\ref{af8} the law forms a closed circuit: contacts grow with length, yet contact-rich prefixes are underrepresented among extendable walks, and the circuit would become a recursion scheme if both signs were theorems.  A first decisive theorem would be monotone decrease of $\mathbf E[A_n\mid C_n\ge m]$ in $m$ at fixed small $n$, an explicitly finite statement.  In exact tests of every upper-tail determinant through $n=21$, all signs hold; a counterexample would exhibit a contact level whose walks are locally freer, inverting the crowding heuristic.

\section{Phase and dimension laws}

\begin{conjecture}[The collapse trichotomy of partition curvature]\label{af13}
Let $K_n(u)=\log Z_{n+2}(u)-2\log Z_n(u)+\log Z_{n-2}(u)$ and let $u_\theta$ be the square-lattice collapse point, $u_\theta\approx1.9474$~\cite{BGJ20}.  Along either parity class: $n^2K_n(u)\to-11/8$ for $0<u<u_\theta$; $n^2K_n(u_\theta)\to-4/7$; and $n^{3/2}K_n(u)\to\sigma(u)$ with $\sigma(u)>0$ for $u>u_\theta$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This conjecture is a consolidation: each regime restates the standard prediction, and the new content is only the uniform sequence-level formulation.  In the swollen phase the constant is $-4(\gamma-1)$ with $\gamma=43/32$~\cite{Nie82}; at the collapse point it is $-4(\gamma_\theta-1)$ with the tricritical exponent $\gamma_\theta=8/7$ of Duplantier and Saleur~\cite{DS87}; and in the collapsed phase the positive $n^{-3/2}$ curvature is exactly the surface term $-s(u)\sqrt n$ in the collapsed scaling form of Owczarek, Prellberg, and Brak~\cite{OPB93}, proved in the partially directed model by Legrand and P\'etr\'elis~\cite{LP22}, and studied for radius-of-gyration laws in~\cite{LDVB26}.  What the trichotomy adds is a phase detector reading a single sequence: the discrete curvature of $\log Z_n$ changes sign and scaling exponent across the transition, with no radius or specific-heat observable.  The retained control is that the finite-size roots of $K_n$ oscillate strongly below $n\approx12$, so nothing monotone is claimed at finite length; the roots computed here through $n=19$ run $1.9843,2.1022,1.9697,2.0589,2.0016$ from $n=15$, consistent with slow drift toward $u_\theta$.  A first decisive theorem would be the swollen-phase clause for the strictly self-avoiding model, or the collapsed clause for any two-dimensional undirected ensemble.  A failure in any regime would force revision of the corresponding scaling form itself.

\begin{conjecture}[Self-avoidance survival rises with dimension]\label{af14}
For every $n\ge4$ and $d\ge2$, $q_{d+1,n}>q_{d,n}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A nonbacktracking walk fails to be self-avoiding only by closing a loop of length at least four, and added transverse directions dilute every such pattern; the conjecture asserts that the dilution is monotone at every finite length, not merely in the $1/d$ expansion of Fisher and Gaunt~\cite{FG64}.  For $n\le3$ survival is identically $1$, so $n=4$ is the first nontrivial length, and Proposition~\ref{af:nbw} proves the law for all $n\le7$ in closed form, in every dimension at once.  Since $q_{d,n}^{1/n}\to\mu_d/(2d-1)$, the full conjecture implies that the normalized connective constant $\mu_d/(2d-1)$ is nondecreasing in $d$, a normalized companion to the strict increase $\mu_{d+1}>\mu_d$ that follows from the edge-addition theorem of Grimmett and Li~\cite{GrL14}, and a cross-dimensional comparison that lace-expansion combinatorics~\cite{FvdH13} seems well suited to attack, pattern by pattern.  A first decisive theorem would be $n=8$, where six-cycles first interact.  In exact rational tests for all enumerated pairs, $d\le10$ at $n\le7$ and up to $n=14$ for $d=2,3$, every adjacent-dimension difference is positive, the smallest being $6.3\times10^{-4}$; a counterexample would exhibit a length at which raising the dimension makes self-trapping relatively likelier.

\begin{conjecture}[All radial moments fall with dimension]\label{af15}
For every $n\ge2$, every real $q>0$, and every $d\ge2$, $\mathbf E_{U_n^{(d+1)}}[|\omega_n|^q]<\mathbf E_{U_n^{(d)}}[|\omega_n|^q]$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Self-avoidance relaxes as the dimension grows, so excluded-volume swelling should weaken; the conjecture asserts the weakening in every positive radial moment at every finite length, comparing uniform ensembles of the same step number across dimensions.  The retained negative control forces this formulation: full stochastic dominance of the radial laws is false, the distributions crossing already at $(d,n)=(2,3)$, so a Mellin-order statement is the strongest available.  If the moments obey the standard scaling $\mathbf E[R_n^q]\sim A_{d,q}n^{q\nu_d}$, the conjecture is incompatible with $\nu_{d+1}>\nu_d$, giving conditional monotonicity of the metric exponents through their conjectured values $\nu_2=3/4$~\cite{Nie82} down to the mean-field $1/2$; no rigorous fixed-length cross-dimension comparison of displacement appears in the literature~\cite{MS93,BDGS12}.  Proposition~\ref{af:extreme} proves the extreme-order regime from the spanning-axes inequality, and Proposition~\ref{af:rad2} proves the length-two case for every dimension and every positive order, so the open content is bounded orders at longer lengths.  A first decisive theorem there would be the $q=2$ case at some fixed small $n$ for all $d$.  In exact and gridded tests across $d\le10$ and all enumerated lengths through $n=14$, every adjacent-dimension difference has the conjectured sign, the smallest gap $1.8\times10^{-4}$; a counterexample would give a moment order at which higher dimension swells the walk.

\part{Budgeted irreversibility and the spectral geometry of relaxation}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 19 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The nine conjectures below concern a single organizing question of non-equilibrium dynamics: when a relaxation process is allowed only a finite budget of irreversibility, how is that budget spectrally allocated?  They form four programmes.  A current-fluctuation law (Conjecture~\ref{ag1}) asserts that a reversible shortcut added to a driven ring at fixed activity strictly amplifies the standardized skewness of the winding current, against the mixing intuition, sharpening the cumulant inequalities of~\cite{WB22,Pta22} into a monotonicity law.  A frontier programme (Conjectures~\ref{ag2} to~\ref{ag6}) studies the linear diffusion $\dd X_t=-(S+A)X_t\,\dd t+\sqrt{2S}\,\dd W_t$ with fixed Gaussian steady state, whose entropy-production rate is the exact quadratic $\Sigma(A)=\operatorname{tr}(A^\top S^{-1}A)$~\cite{GL19}, and conjectures the complete architecture of the budgeted-gap frontier: nested mode recruitment ordered by the reversible spectrum, piecewise-convex arcs with downward marginal-gain resets, exact two-mode support at small budget, a rank-two extremizer for the oscillation frequency, and a pairwise formula for the cheapest exceptional point, the thermodynamic analogue of the nearest-defective-matrix problem~\cite{ABBO11}; the unlimited endpoint is the theorem of Leli\`evre, Nier, and Pavliotis~\cite{LNP13}, and the spectral-perturbation bound of~\cite{KOI24} and the dissipation--coherence decomposition of~\cite{NKI26} bound the same objects, so Conjecture~\ref{ag5} is closely related to the latter work.  A coherent-acceleration programme (Conjectures~\ref{ag7} and~\ref{ag8}) transfers the frontier architecture to primitive Lindblad dynamics with detailed balance, where a stationary Hamiltonian is a skew perturbation in the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal (GNS) geometry~\cite{Alicki76} and coherent gap enhancement is the theorem of Li and Lu~\cite{LiLu24}: sequential operator-mode recruitment under the commutator-accessibility constraint, and saturation of the classical envelope exactly on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-closed mode systems.  A preparation-geometry programme (Conjecture~\ref{ag9}) turns from rates to eigenvector geometry in the anomalous-relaxation setting of the Markovian Mpemba effect~\cite{LR17,KRHV19}: the measure of preparations that robustly cancel the slow mode should collapse in inverse proportion to the biorthogonal condition number as a Liouvillian exceptional point is approached, quantifying the antagonism between exceptional-point acceleration~\cite{ZXW25,CTH24} and robustness~\cite{MP26}.  The proved layer is three calibrations: Proposition~\ref{ag:pair} solves the two-mode frontier in closed form, identifies the second-slowest mode as the unique best infinitesimal partner of the slowest, and gives the exact pair costs used throughout; Proposition~\ref{ag:env} proves that the classical frontier is an upper envelope for every coherently driven detailed-balance Lindbladian and that the unital qubit attains it exactly; and Proposition~\ref{ag:basin} proves the basin-collapse law exactly in the qubit model, with the sphere prefactor equal to one.  Four negative findings are retained as controls, and they shape the part: the Markov analogues of the exceptional-point frontier laws were tested at optimizer level and discarded, since on a three-state ring the budgeted-gap frontier reaches its supremum only on the unidirectional boundary at infinite entropy production, on rings of four and five states the slow pair's real part continues to improve past the exceptional point rather than pinning, on the four-state instance the slow sector turns complex strictly before the frontier's plateau, and the fixed-trace pinning that motivated those claims is an artifact of three-state spectra; gap optimizers generically sit at defective matrices~\cite{BLO01} and at exceptional points of Liouvillians~\cite{ZWG23}, so only the budgeted, structure-revealing refinements below are claimed as new; and a proposed resonance criterion for entangling coherent acceleration was tested in exact second-order arithmetic and discarded, since in every nondegenerate product instance the best local Hamiltonian already attains the full optimum, the commutator structure forcing every entangling transition out of a simple product slow mode to carry a strictly larger spectral denominator than its local counterpart, while the claimed advantage appears only through slow-mode degeneracies outside the criterion's own hypotheses; and a proposed capacity principle equating the number of slow modes simultaneously cancellable by unitary preparation with the maximal rank of the tangent overlap map was refuted on a generic qutrit instance, where the slow coordinate's range over the fixed-spectrum orbit omits zero entirely, the spectral offset between the stationary state and the orbit dominating the orbit's fluctuation, so feasibility of Mpemba preparation on an orbit is an affine range condition invisible to the tangent geometry, constructive steering protocols~\cite{GMS26} notwithstanding, and Conjecture~\ref{ag9} carries that condition as an explicit hypothesis.  Conjectures~\ref{ag2}, \ref{ag3}, \ref{ag7}, and~\ref{ag8} assert laws for every dimension.

For a continuous-time generator $Q$ on a finite connected graph with stationary law $\pi$, the activity is $\kappa=\sum_i\pi_i\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}$ and the entropy-production rate is $\sigma=\tfrac12\sum_{i\ne j}(\pi_iq_{ij}-\pi_jq_{ji})\log(\pi_iq_{ij}/\pi_jq_{ji})$.  On the homogeneous $N$-ring with affinity $F$, rates $e^{\pm F/(2N)}$, the winding current $J_t$ has long-time cumulant rates $c_m$ obtained from the tilted generator, and $S_3=|c_3|/c_2^{3/2}$ is its standardized skewness.  For the linear diffusion above, $S=S^\top>0$ is diagonal with simple spectrum $s_1<\cdots<s_n$ after an orthogonal change of basis, $A^\top=-A$, the stationary covariance is the identity, $r(A)=\min_j\operatorname{Re}\lambda_j(S+A)$, $\Omega(A)=\max_j|\operatorname{Im}\lambda_j(S+A)|$, and the frontier is $r_*(\Sigma)=\sup\{r(A):\Sigma(A)\le\Sigma\}$ with $\Sigma(A)=\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}^2(1/s_i+1/s_j)$; since the real parts sum to $\operatorname{tr} S$, always $r(A)\le\bar s=\operatorname{tr} S/n$, and $\bar s$ is attained at finite budget~\cite{LNP13}.  A mode $i$ is \emph{active} for $A$ when the $i$th row of $A$ is nonzero.  For a primitive Lindblad dissipator $\mathcal D$ in detailed balance with respect to $\rho_*$, the operator $K=-\mathcal D$ is positive self-adjoint in the GNS inner product with eigenmodes $KF_j=s_jF_j$ on the traceless sector, a stationary Hamiltonian ($[H,\rho_*]=0$) acts as the skew-adjoint $\mathcal A_H=-i[H,\cdot\,]$ with matrix elements $a_{jk}(H)$ and coherent budget $\Sigma_H=\sum_{j<k}|a_{jk}(H)|^2(1/s_j+1/s_k)$, and $r_{\mathrm{OU}}$ denotes the frontier of the diagonal spectrum $\{s_j\}$.  For a density matrix $\rho_0$ with simple spectrum, $\mathcal O_{\rho_0}$ is its unitary orbit, the left Liouvillian eigenmodes $\ell_1,\ell_2,\ldots$ are ordered from slow to fast and split into real functionals, $T_\rho:K\mapsto(\langle\ell_\alpha,i[K,\rho]\rangle)_\alpha$ is the tangent overlap map with real rank $\operatorname{rank}T_\rho$, and for a family $\mathcal L(h)$ with simple slow eigenvalue the biorthogonal condition number is $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)=\|\ell_1(h)\|\,\|r_1(h)\|$ under $\langle\ell_1,r_1\rangle=1$; the $\eps$-robust basin on an orbit $\mathcal O$ is $\mathcal B_\eps(h)=\{\rho\in\mathcal O:|\langle\ell_1(h),\rho-\rho_*\rangle|\le\eps\}$ with the invariant orbit measure $\mu_\mathcal O$.

\begin{proposition}[Pair calibration for the frontier programme]\label{ag:pair}
(i) A perturbation supported on the pair $(i,j)$ leaves $\operatorname{span}\{e_i,e_j\}$ invariant with eigenvalues $\tfrac{s_i+s_j}2\pm\sqrt{(\tfrac{s_j-s_i}2)^2-a_{ij}^2}$; the block reaches its exceptional point at cost $\Sigma_{ij}^{\mathrm{EP}}=\tfrac{(s_j-s_i)^2}4(1/s_i+1/s_j)$ and generates frequency $\Omega_{ij}(\Sigma)=(\Sigma/(1/s_i+1/s_j)-(\tfrac{s_j-s_i}2)^2)_+^{1/2}$ at cost $\Sigma$.  (ii) The small-budget rate gain of coupling the slowest mode to mode $j$ is $\gamma_{1j}=s_1s_j/((s_j-s_1)(s_j+s_1))$ per unit entropy production, strictly decreasing in $s_j$: the second-slowest mode is the unique best infinitesimal partner.  (iii) For $n=2$ the frontier is
\[
r_*(\Sigma)=\frac{s_1+s_2}2-\sqrt{\Bigl(\frac{s_2-s_1}2\Bigr)^2-\frac{\Sigma}{1/s_1+1/s_2}}
\quad(\Sigma\le\Sigma_{12}^{\mathrm{EP}}),\qquad r_*(\Sigma)=\bar s\quad(\Sigma\ge\Sigma_{12}^{\mathrm{EP}}),
\]
continuous, strictly increasing and strictly convex on the arc, with marginal gain diverging at the threshold and resetting to zero beyond it; all laws of Conjectures~\ref{ag2} to~\ref{ag6} hold for $n=2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) is the characteristic polynomial of the $2\times2$ block, which is invariant because $A$ vanishes off the pair, together with the cost formula $\Sigma=a_{ij}^2(1/s_i+1/s_j)$.  For (ii), expanding the block eigenvalue gives $r=s_1+a^2/(s_j-s_1)+O(a^4)$ at cost $a^2(1/s_1+1/s_j)$, whence $\gamma_{1j}$; as a function of $s_j$, $s_j/(s_j^2-s_1^2)$ has derivative of the sign of $-(s_j^2+s_1^2)<0$.  For (iii), when $n=2$ the only skew matrices are the pair blocks, so the frontier is the substitution $a^2=\Sigma/(1/s_1+1/s_2)$ into (i); the arc is the composition of the strictly convex increasing map $\Sigma\mapsto-\sqrt{K-c\Sigma}$, its derivative $c/(2\sqrt{K-c\Sigma})$ diverges as $\Sigma\uparrow\Sigma^{\mathrm{EP}}_{12}$, and beyond the threshold both real parts equal $\bar s$, which no feasible $A$ can exceed.  Recruitment, convexity, two-mode support, the frequency formula, and the cheapest exceptional point are then all immediate for $n=2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Envelope calibration for the coherent programme]\label{ag:env}
(i) For every primitive detailed-balance dissipator with traceless-sector spectrum $\{s_j\}$ and every stationary Hamiltonian $H$,
\[
\operatorname{gap}(-\mathcal D-\mathcal A_H)\ \le\ r_{\mathrm{OU}}(\Sigma_H).
\]
(ii) For the unital qubit dissipator with Bloch decay rates $(s_1,s_2,s_3)$ and $H=\tfrac12\,h\cdot\sigma$, the traceless Liouvillian spectrum equals $-\operatorname{spec}(S+A(h))$ with $A(h)$ the cross-product matrix of $h$, every $3\times3$ skew matrix is realized, and the envelope is attained exactly.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
In the GNS inner product $K=-\mathcal D$ is positive self-adjoint on the traceless sector and $\mathcal A_H$ is skew-adjoint and real in a $K$-eigenbasis; the gap of $K+\mathcal A_H$ is the objective $r$ evaluated at the particular skew matrix $a(H)$, whose cost is $\Sigma_H$ by definition, and the frontier is the supremum over all skew matrices of that cost, which proves (i).  For (ii), on Bloch coordinates the dissipator acts as $\operatorname{diag}(s_1,s_2,s_3)$ and $-i[H,\cdot\,]$ acts as $r\mapsto h\times r$, an arbitrary antisymmetric matrix as $h$ ranges over $\R^3$, so the Liouvillian restricted to the traceless sector is conjugate to $-(S+A(h))$ and the relaxation problem coincides with the three-dimensional frontier problem.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Basin calibration for the preparation programme]\label{ag:basin}
Let $\mu$ be the uniform measure on the unit sphere of Bloch vectors and let the slow left functional of the family $B(h)=S+A(h)$, $S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,s_2,s_3)$, $A(h)$ the rotation block $a_{12}=-h$, be normalized by $\langle\ell_1,r_1\rangle=1$ with $\|r_1\|=1$, so $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)=\|\ell_1(h)\|$.  Then for every $0<\eps\le\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)$ and every $h$ below the exceptional point $h_c=(s_2-s_1)/2$,
\[
\mu\{x:|\langle\ell_1(h),x\rangle|\le\eps\}=\frac{\eps}{\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)},
\]
exactly, and $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)=\sqrt{h_c/2}\,(h_c-h)^{-1/2}(1+o(1))$ as $h\uparrow h_c$, so the basin measure collapses at the exact rate $\eps\sqrt{2(h_c-h)/h_c}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The functional $x\mapsto\langle\ell_1,x\rangle$ is linear, and by the Archimedes projection theorem the coordinate of a uniform point of $S^2$ along any unit direction is uniform on $[-1,1]$, so the band $|\langle\ell_1,x\rangle|\le\eps$ has measure $\min(1,\eps/\|\ell_1\|)$, and $\|\ell_1\|=\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}$ under the stated normalization.  For the divergence rate, write $d=h_c=(s_2-s_1)/2$ and $u=\sqrt{d^2-h^2}$; the slow eigenvalue of the block $\begin{pmatrix}s_1&-h\\h&s_2\end{pmatrix}$ has right eigenvector $r\propto(h,\,u-d)$ and left eigenvector $\ell\propto(h,\,d-u)$, so
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)=\frac{\|\ell\|\,\|r\|}{|\langle\ell,r\rangle|}=\frac{h^2+(d-u)^2}{h^2-(d-u)^2},
\]
and as $h\uparrow d$ one has $u=\sqrt{2d}\sqrt{d-h}\,(1+o(1))$, numerator $\to2d^2$, denominator $=(h-d+u)(h+d-u)=2d\,u\,(1+o(1))$, giving $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sqrt{d/2}\,(d-h)^{-1/2}(1+o(1))$.
\end{proof}

\section{A current-fluctuation law for equilibrium shortcuts}

\begin{conjecture}[Reversible shortcuts amplify winding skewness]\label{ag1}
For every even $N\ge4$ and affinity $F\ne0$, add to the homogeneous driven $N$-ring a reversible antipodal chord of strength $g$ carrying no winding increment, rescaling all rates to keep the activity fixed.  Then the standardized skewness $S_3(g)$ of the long-time winding current is strictly increasing in $g\ge0$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The chord carries no affinity and no counted current, and the mixing intuition says extra reversible pathways should Gaussianize the winding statistics; the conjecture asserts the exact opposite at every chord strength: the shortcut suppresses coherent winding progress faster than it suppresses the third cumulant, so the standardized non-Gaussianity strictly grows.  The standardized skewness uses the absolute third cumulant, $S_3=|c_3|/c_2^{3/2}$, and is therefore even in $F$: reflecting the ring sends $F\mapsto-F$ and the winding tilt $z\mapsto-z$, so the scaled cumulant generator obeys $\psi_{-F}(z)=\psi_F(-z)$, making the signed third cumulant odd in $F$ while the variance rate $c_2$ and hence $S_3$ stay invariant; the law is thus symmetric under affinity reversal, and the positive-affinity tests below cover both signs.  The nearest results are the skewness and kurtosis bounds of Wampler and Barato~\cite{WB22}, proved for unicyclic networks and known to fail multicyclic ones, and the steady-state cumulant bounds of~\cite{Pta22}; neither orders the effect of a topological perturbation.  The statement is one-dimensional in $g$ for each $(N,F)$, so it is unusually exposed: a single high-precision decrease refutes it.  A first decisive theorem would be the sign of $\dd S_3/\dd g$ at $g=0$ for all even $N$.  In tests with fourth-order tilted-cumulant differences across $N\le10$, affinities $0.5\le F\le12$, and chords through $g=50$, all $420$ sampled ratios exceeded one and every consecutive pair increased, the smallest ratio being $1.0000739$, at the smallest chord; a counterexample would exhibit a mixing pathway that Gaussianizes a driven current, locating the boundary of the amplification mechanism.

\section{The finite-budget frontier of linear diffusions}

\begin{conjecture}[Sequential spectral recruitment]\label{ag2}
For every diagonal $S$ with simple spectrum there are thresholds $0=\Sigma_0<\Sigma_1\le\Sigma_2\le\cdots$ and a choice of maximizer $A(\Sigma)$ of the frontier at every budget whose active-mode set is $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with $m$ nondecreasing in $\Sigma$: no mode is recruited before every slower mode.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The conjecture is a spectral water-filling law with a non-Hermitian twist: at small budget all resources go to the two slowest modes, by the exact quotient of Proposition~\ref{ag:pair}(ii), and the claim is that recruitment stays ordered by the reversible spectrum at every scale, so the optimizer's invariant subspace grows by one canonical direction at a time until the theorem of~\cite{LNP13} takes over at the ceiling.  The dissipation--coherence trade-offs of~\cite{NKI26} bound the same objects without addressing optimizer architecture.  A first decisive theorem would be ordered recruitment for $n=3$.  In global optimizations over spectra $(1,2,5)$, $(1,1.3,7)$, $(1,2,2.05)$, $(1,50,50.5)$, $(1,2,5,8)$, and $(1,2,3,7)$ across budgets spanning four orders of magnitude, every observed active set was an initial segment $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ with $m$ nondecreasing, including near-degenerate and widely split spectra; a counterexample would be a spectrum whose optimum skips a slow mode, which would overturn the marginal-return mechanism itself.

\begin{conjecture}[Convex arcs with marginal-gain resets]\label{ag3}
For simple $S$ the frontier $r_*(\Sigma)$ is continuous and piecewise real-analytic; on each maximal interval with constant active set it is convex; the one-sided marginal gain jumps only downward at arc boundaries; and $r_*$ reaches the ceiling $\bar s$ at a finite budget and is constant beyond.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Convex arcs mean increasing returns to irreversibility inside a fixed spectral architecture, the opposite of concave resource allocation: budget should be pushed into the currently active block all the way to its structural threshold, not spread smoothly.  Proposition~\ref{ag:pair}(iii) proves the extreme form for $n=2$, where the marginal gain diverges at the exceptional point and resets to zero, and the ceiling attainment at finite budget is the unconstrained theorem of~\cite{LNP13}; the conjecture asserts that this convex-then-reset geometry survives every recruitment in every dimension.  The nonsmooth-optimization literature knows that spectral-abscissa optimizers sit at defective matrices~\cite{BLO01}, which is where the resets live.  A first decisive theorem would be convexity of the first arc for $n=3$.  In fine-grid frontier computations for $(1,2,5)$ over fifty-two warm-started budgets, the discrete slopes increase monotonically within each of the two resolved arcs, from $0.69$ toward $4.9$ on the first and from $0.18$ toward $1.1$ on the second, with the only slope decreases at the recruitment threshold near $\Sigma\approx0.38$ and at the terminal entry into the ceiling, which is reached exactly, $8/3$ to $10^{-6}$, by budget $\Sigma\approx4.1$; a counterexample, a concave stretch inside an arc, would restore ordinary diminishing returns somewhere on the frontier.

\begin{conjecture}[Finite two-mode radius]\label{ag4}
For simple $S$ there exists $\Sigma_1>0$ such that for every $0<\Sigma<\Sigma_1$, every global maximizer of the frontier, up to sign and rotations inside exact degeneracies, is supported on the two slowest modes; $\Sigma_1$ is the first budget at which the two-mode branch collides or loses optimality to a branch containing mode three.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Proposition~\ref{ag:pair}(ii) proves that the second-slowest mode is the unique best infinitesimal partner, so the two-mode block wins at first order; the conjecture upgrades the perturbative selection to exact support on a whole interval, the base case of the recruitment law and the natural first proof target of the programme, accessible to analytic perturbation theory plus an isolation argument.  In global optimizations at spectra $(1,2,5)$ and budgets through $0.16$, the largest coupling outside the $(1,2)$ block was $2\times10^{-5}$, and for the widely split spectrum $(1,50,50.5)$ the two-mode support persists through budgets in the hundreds, consistent with the block's exceptional-point cost; a counterexample would be a spectrum where dense couplings beat the pair at arbitrarily small budget, contradicting the strict gap in the quotient $\gamma_{1j}$.

\begin{conjecture}[Rank-two oscillation extremizer]\label{ag5}
For every diagonal $S>0$ and budget $\Sigma$,
\[
\sup_{\Sigma(A)\le\Sigma}\Omega(A)=\max_{i<j}\ \Omega_{ij}(\Sigma),
\]
with $\Omega_{ij}$ the pair formula of Proposition~\ref{ag:pair}(i): no coupling of three or more modes generates a larger spectral frequency than the best single rotation block.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
For isotropic $S$ the statement is the equality case of the operator-norm--Frobenius-norm inequality for skew matrices; the anisotropic weighting $1/s_i+1/s_j$ and the detuning penalty $(s_j-s_i)/2$ break that argument, and the conjecture asserts the rank-two concentration survives.  This conjecture is the part's closest to prior work: the dissipation--coherence bound of~\cite{NKI26} constrains entropy production per oscillation period in the same family, and whether the envelope above is a saturated form of that bound cannot be settled from its abstract; the exact pairwise envelope and its attainment are proposed as the new content, recorded pending that paper's full text.  A first decisive theorem would be the $n=3$ case, a two-parameter reduction.  In adversarial optimizations over dense skew couplings at spectra $(1,2,5,8)$, $(1,1.1,1.2,1.3)$, $(1,2,50,51)$, and the five-mode $(1,3,3.2,9,10)$ across five budgets each, the adversarially optimized dense coupling coincided with the pair envelope to eight digits in every case; a counterexample would exhibit collective oscillation beating every pairwise rotation, a genuinely new non-normal mechanism.

\begin{conjecture}[Cheapest exceptional point is a pair]\label{ag6}
For simple $S$, the infimum of $\Sigma(A)$ over antisymmetric $A$ making $S+A$ defective equals $\min_{i<j}\Sigma_{ij}^{\mathrm{EP}}$, attained by the single block of Proposition~\ref{ag:pair}(i) on a minimizing pair.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is a thermodynamic Wilkinson problem: the distance to defectivity, classically measured in unweighted norms and characterized through coalescing pseudospectral components~\cite{ABBO11}, is here measured in entropy production over the stationarity-preserving antisymmetric perturbations, and the conjecture asserts that the cheapest route to an exceptional point is always the elementary two-mode one, computable from pairwise rates.  Exceptional points are often treated as delicate high-dimensional nonnormal phenomena~\cite{Heiss12}; a proof would make their minimal thermodynamic cost a two-body quantity.  The retained Markov control sharpens the claim's scope: the analogous exceptional-point frontier laws fail for jump processes, where current perturbations are not block-closed, so the pair structure is a genuinely linear-diffusive mechanism.  A first decisive theorem would be the $n=3$ case via the discriminant variety.  In adversarial minimizations of the eigenvalue separation at $90$, $97$, and $99.5$ percent of the predicted cost across four spectra, the optimizer converged onto the pair block itself, the minimal separation matching the block's own value $(s_j-s_i)\sqrt{1-\Sigma/\Sigma^{\mathrm{EP}}_{ij}}$ to six digits and vanishing to machine precision exactly at the predicted cost; a counterexample would be a genuinely collective cheapest defectivity.

\section{Coherent acceleration of dissipative quantum dynamics}

\begin{conjecture}[Recruitment under commutator accessibility]\label{ag7}
For a primitive detailed-balance dissipator with simple traceless spectrum, every small-budget maximizer of $\operatorname{gap}(-\mathcal D-\mathcal A_H)$ over stationary Hamiltonians of coherent budget $\Sigma_H$ concentrates, as $\Sigma_H\to0$, on the accessible direction maximizing the restricted quotient $\sum_{j>1}|a_{1j}(H)|^2/(s_j-s_1)$ over $\Sigma_H$; and there is a maximizing selection whose active dissipative modes are nested and nondecreasing in the budget, with changes only at spectral collisions or accessibility branch crossings.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Coherent gap enhancement is the theorem of Li and Lu~\cite{LiLu24}; the conjecture concerns the optimizer's architecture, which their variational framework does not address.  The new obstruction is algebraic: commutators with stationary Hamiltonians realize only a subspace of skew matrices, and coupling the slow mode may force side couplings elsewhere, wasting budget, so the selected partner is the accessible optimum of the same Rayleigh quotient that drives Conjecture~\ref{ag2}, not necessarily the second-slowest mode.  For maximally accessible dissipators, stationary state proportional to the identity, the constraint vanishes and the classical recruitment law applies verbatim through Proposition~\ref{ag:env}.  A first decisive theorem would be the perturbative selection statement, a finite-dimensional constrained Rayleigh problem.  In tests on a unital qutrit with an eight-rate Gell-Mann dissipator, the finite-budget optimizer aligned with the predicted accessible direction to cosine $1.0000$ and its leading matrix element coupled the two slowest eigenoperators, with the forced side couplings an order smaller; a counterexample would exhibit accessibility overturning sparse recruitment itself rather than merely redirecting it.

\begin{conjecture}[Envelope saturation is Lie-algebraic]\label{ag8}
For a primitive detailed-balance Lindbladian, the envelope of Proposition~\ref{ag:env} is attained on a nontrivial budget interval if and only if the dissipative eigenmodes active in the classical optimizer close under commutation into a direct sum of three-dimensional $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-type modules together with spectators, so that the unrestricted skew optimizer is realized by a Hamiltonian commutator.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Proposition~\ref{ag:env} makes the classical frontier an unconditional upper bound and shows the unital qubit attains it because the Bloch cross product realizes every rotation; the conjecture characterizes exactly when that saturation persists: the active operator modes must form the adjoint representation of an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, making the optimal rotation physically implementable by a stationary Hamiltonian.  The interval hypothesis is the safeguard against accidental coincidences: saturation at an isolated budget forces nothing, while saturation on a nontrivial interval pins the whole optimizer path inside the commutator image.  This is a sharp structural dichotomy, coherence saturates the classical bound precisely on quantum systems that look classical in the relevant sector, and it would give the first necessary-and-sufficient criterion in the coherent-acceleration literature~\cite{LiLu24,CRE26}.  A first decisive theorem would be necessity for a qutrit dissipator whose slow modes do not close.  The unital qubit equality is verified to machine precision, and the qutrit computations of Conjecture~\ref{ag7}, whose accessible optimum falls twenty-six percent below the unrestricted classical optimum, exhibit the conjectured strictness on a non-closing system; a counterexample would be saturation without closure, revealing an unforeseen exact-control mechanism.

\section{The geometry of anomalous relaxation}

\begin{conjecture}[Exceptional points collapse robust Mpemba basins]\label{ag9}
Let $\mathcal L(h)$ approach a second-order exceptional point $h_c$ in its slow sector from the diagonalizable side, normalize the slow eigenvectors by $\|r_1\|=1$ and $\langle\ell_1,r_1\rangle=1$ so that $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)=\|\ell_1(h)\|$ and the basin $\mathcal B_\eps(h)=\{\rho\in\mathcal O:|\langle\ell_1(h),\rho-\rho_*\rangle|\le\eps\}$ is fixed in scale, and suppose the slow functional vanishes transversally on the fixed smooth orbit $\mathcal O$, uniformly near the exceptional point: the tangential gradient of the unit-normalized slow functional is bounded above and below by positive constants along its zero set on $\mathcal O$, and that zero set is nonempty with hypersurface measure bounded below, uniformly for $h$ near $h_c$.  Then there are constants $0<c<C$ with
\[
c\,\frac{\eps}{\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)}\ \le\ \mu_\mathcal O(\mathcal B_\eps(h))\ \le\ C\,\frac{\eps}{\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}(h)}
\]
for all sufficiently small $\eps$ and all $h$ near $h_c$: the measure of preparations that robustly cancel the slow mode collapses in exact inverse proportion to the biorthogonal condition number.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Exceptional points maximize acceleration for exactly tuned preparations~\cite{ZXW25,CTH24}, eigenvector rotation can switch Mpemba behavior with spectra pinned~\cite{YZXM26}, and preparation noise is known to degrade the effect~\cite{MP26}; the conjecture quantifies the antagonism as a clean scaling law, the coarea mechanism being that biorthogonal normalization makes the slow functional's gradient on the orbit grow like $\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}$, so the $\eps$-slab thins in exact proportion.  Proposition~\ref{ag:basin} proves the law in the qubit model with prefactor one and identifies the divergence rate $(h_c-h)^{-1/2}$, so the basin closes like $\eps\sqrt{h_c-h}$; the open content is the general orbit, where the uniform-transversality hypothesis records exactly the remaining boundary, tangency of the limiting zero set to the orbit, at which the upper constant would fail.  A first decisive theorem would be the law for generic qutrit families.  In sphere samplings of the qubit model and of a four-dimensional companion, the product of basin fraction and condition number held constant within sampling error while the condition number grew fifty-fold toward the exceptional point, and the basin fraction was linear in $\eps$ throughout; a counterexample would exhibit robust exceptional-point Mpemba preparation, welcome news for experiments and fatal for the coarea picture.

\part{Inverse problems and design laws for multivariate extremes}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 19 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The thirteen conjectures below concern a single organizing question of extreme-value theory: how much of the dependence structure of rare events can be recovered from partial, thinned, or redesigned observation, and at what cost in stability.  They form five programmes.  A geometric programme (Conjectures~\ref{ah1} to~\ref{ah4}) studies the extremal coefficient $\theta_m(\Gamma)$ of the H\"usler--Reiss family~\cite{HR89,EH20} as a functional on variogram matrices: an isoperimetric recruitment staircase at fixed total variogram energy with a proved symmetry-breaking boundary, the regular simplex maximal for three variables and at weak dependence but strictly beaten below it by configurations carrying fewer active components, a pairwise closure law at weak dependence sharpening the consistency inequalities of Schlather and Tawn~\cite{ST02} into an asymptotic equivalence, a scale-elasticity bound of one half paired with entrywise monotonicity whose conjunction yields a dimension-free sparsification law for resistance variograms, strengthening the variogram-level guarantees of~\cite{EAR26} to the extremal coefficient itself, and a positive-curvature law at complete dependence whose convex-body shadow is the Wills functional~\cite{Vit96}.  A cluster-tomography programme (Conjectures~\ref{ah5} and~\ref{ah6}) turns the missing-data results for subsampled sequences~\cite{RT00,MF04,HS08} into an inverse theory: the Bernoulli-thinning response curve should identify the entire limiting cluster-size law through its generating function, and the two-parameter systematic-plus-Bernoulli response should identify the cluster support exactly up to the equivalence generated by its modular occupancy data.  A topological programme (Conjectures~\ref{ah7} and~\ref{ah8}) makes the topology of extreme directions an inferential target: a bottleneck-consistency law for persistent homology of intermediate-order angular samples at the rate $b(U(n/k))+(\log k/k)^{1/s}$, composing the diagram-estimation rates of~\cite{CGLM15} with a finite-threshold angular bias, and a leakage trichotomy locating exactly when hidden regular variation~\cite{Res08,MR11} is topologically visible after support filtering.  A tail-tomography programme (Conjectures~\ref{ah9} and~\ref{ah10}) quantifies the inverse problem of angular reconstruction from one-sided projection tails: a severe stability barrier, no H\"older inverse on measures and only a logarithmic modulus on H\"older classes, the analytic-kernel phenomenon of moment problems~\cite{Tal87} instantiated for the fractional transforms whose injectivity dichotomy is recorded in Proposition~\ref{ah:moment} following~\cite{MN21,CT19}, and a parameter-count identifiability threshold for $s$-atomic angular measures at exactly $m=sd-1$ generic fractional projections.  A design programme (Conjectures~\ref{ah11} to~\ref{ah13}) redesigns block maxima themselves: Poissonized block sizes should remove the universal $V^2/(2n)$ finite-block correction and the corresponding $n^{-1}$ estimator bias documented in the block-maxima second-order theory~\cite{BVZ19,DF19,BZ21}, factorial-cumulant matching should extend the removal to a full ladder of orders, and exact second-order cancellation in a Hall family~\cite{Hall82} should create a cusp at which threshold adaptation, whose logarithmic penalty away from the cusp is the theorem of Carpentier and Kim~\cite{CK15}, cannot be uniformly oracle-optimal, with critical window $|c|\asymp n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$.  The proved layer is four calibrations.  Proposition~\ref{ah:hr} gives the exact Gaussian-orthant formula for $\theta_m$ used throughout, proves the elasticity bound in the pairwise case, and proves that every collinear configuration has vanishing second curvature, the easy direction of Conjecture~\ref{ah4}.  Proposition~\ref{ah:thin} proves the cluster-level thinning algebra: the Bernoulli response formula, the systematic random-phase formula, the identifiability of the occupancy multisets from the joint response, the recovery of the entire difference multiset from occupancy data by M\"obius inversion, and the closure of occupancy equivalence under dilation.  Proposition~\ref{ah:moment} proves the integer--fractional injectivity dichotomy for the projection transforms, with an explicit two-atom versus three-atom pair invisible at $\alpha=2$ and separated at $\alpha=3/2$.  Proposition~\ref{ah:block} proves the exact Poissonization identity for Pareto seeds and constructs, for every order $r$, finitely supported non-Poisson integer block-size laws whose factorial cumulants match the Poisson law through order $r$, with the exact probability-generating-function identity showing that the finite-block error then falls to order $n^{-r}$.  Five negative findings are retained as controls, and they shape the part.  The deposited isoperimetry claim, that the regular simplex maximizes $\theta_m$ at fixed energy for every $m$, is refuted for $m\ge4$: the width identity of Proposition~\ref{ah:hr}(iv) makes configurations with fewer active components strictly better away from weak dependence, with exact orthant-probability instances at $m=4$, scale $0.12$, and $m=5$, scale $0.35$, where the four-active configuration beats the simplex by $3.5\times10^{-3}$ and is found by unrestricted optimization, so Conjecture~\ref{ah1} keeps the simplex law at three variables and states the recruitment staircase above.  A proposed modular reconstruction claim, that the occupancy multisets over all moduli determine a finite cluster support up to translation and reflection, is refuted: the six-mark pair $\{0,1,4,10,12,17\}$ and $\{0,1,8,11,13,17\}$ of Bloom~\cite{Blo77}, the classical counterexample to Piccard's theorem on difference multisets~\cite{Pat44,BG07}, shares every occupancy multiset, by finite verification below the diameter and trivially above it, so occupancy tomography can never distinguish this pair; the repaired Conjecture~\ref{ah6} asks instead for determination within size five and for the two-member bound on equivalence classes, over the exhaustive verification that all ten occupancy collisions among the $6437$ canonical sets of size at most six through diameter eighteen and the $3312$ of size at most seven through diameter fourteen are homometric pairs, while the pair $\{0,1,3,8,10,14\}$ versus $\{0,1,7,9,11,14\}$ shows the occupancy data strictly refines the difference multiset.  The subsampling formulas themselves, the Bernoulli and systematic extremal-index responses at the cluster level, are known in substance for subsampled stationary sequences~\cite{RT00,MF04,HS08} and are therefore recorded as calibration, not conjecture; what is claimed as new in Conjectures~\ref{ah5} and~\ref{ah6} is the uniform process-level transport and the inverse-theory content.  A multiplicity observed at the identifiability threshold of Conjecture~\ref{ah10} on one random instance was exposed as an artifact of a near-coincident atom pair, ill-conditioning inflating rounding-level copies of the single true solution, and the atom-separation hypothesis of the conjecture records that boundary.  A second multiplicity is genuine and refutes global uniqueness at the counting boundary itself: at three atoms in three dimensions, two of six well-separated random instances admit a second exact interior mixture at $m=sd-1$, verified to forty-digit residuals, and both become unique one measurement higher, so the global clause of Conjecture~\ref{ah10} begins at $m=sd$ and the counting-boundary refutation is recorded in place.  Conjectures~\ref{ah1}, \ref{ah2}, \ref{ah3}, \ref{ah7}, \ref{ah8}, and~\ref{ah11} to~\ref{ah13} assert laws for every dimension or every sample size; Conjecture~\ref{ah3} is closely related to the sparsification guarantees of~\cite{EAR26}, and Conjecture~\ref{ah13} carries one against the adaptation lower bounds of~\cite{CK15}.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{ah4} has been resolved true by Proposition~\ref{ah:curv}.

A variogram matrix $\Gamma$ on $m$ sites is symmetric with zero diagonal and conditionally negative definite, so that $\Gamma_{ij}=\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2$ for centered points $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ in some $\R^k$; the H\"usler--Reiss max-stable vector with variogram $\Gamma$~\cite{HR89} has extremal coefficient $\theta_m(\Gamma)\in[1,m]$, the exponent function at $\mathbf 1$, with spectral representation $\theta_m(\Gamma)=\E\max_i\exp(\langle Z,x_i\rangle-\lVert x_i\rVert^2/2)$ for a standard Gaussian $Z$, pairwise coefficients $\theta_{ij}=2\Phi(\sqrt{\Gamma_{ij}}/2)$, energy $\mathcal S(\Gamma)=\sum_{i<j}\Gamma_{ij}$, and scale elasticity $\eta(t)=\dd\log\theta_m(t\Gamma)/\dd\log t$.  For a stationary regularly varying sequence whose exceedances converge to a compound-Poisson cluster process~\cite{BS09} with cluster size $N$, $\E N<\infty$, the extremal index is $\theta=1/\E N$~\cite{Lea83,OB87}, and when the limiting cluster has a finite support $S\subset\Z$, defined up to translation, the occupancy counts are $n_{m,r}(S)=|\{s\in S:s\equiv r\ (\mathrm{mod}\ m)\}|$, the occupancy data of $S$ is the family of unordered multisets $\mathcal N_m(S)=\{n_{m,0}(S),\ldots,n_{m,m-1}(S)\}$ over all $m\ge2$, two sets are occupancy equivalent when their occupancy data agree, and homometric when their difference multisets agree.  A $d$-variate regularly varying vector has angular measure $H$ on the simplex $\Delta_{d-1}$; the fractional projection transform is $(T_\alpha H)(a)=\int(a\cdot w)^\alpha\,H(\dd w)$ for directions $a\in(0,\infty)^d$; and for block maxima, $F$ lies in a max-domain with exponent function $V$ and second-order rate $A(n)$, a block of size $n$ has exceedance probability $q_n(x)=\bar F(a_nx+b_n)$, and a randomized block size $N_n$ has factorial cumulants $\kappa_r^{(F)}$ defined by $\log\E(1+u)^{N_n}=\sum_{r\ge1}\kappa_r^{(F)}u^r/r!$, so that $\log\E(1-q)^{N_n}=\sum_{r\ge1}\kappa_r^{(F)}(-q)^r/r!$ exactly.

\begin{proposition}[Tilting calibration for the dependence programme]\label{ah:hr}
(i) For every admissible $\Gamma$ realized by centered points $x_1,\ldots,x_m$,
\[
\theta_m(\Gamma)=\sum_{i=1}^m\Phi_{m-1}\Bigl(\bigl(\tfrac{\Gamma_{ij}}2\bigr)_{j\ne i};\,\bigl(\tfrac{\Gamma_{ij}+\Gamma_{ik}-\Gamma_{jk}}2\bigr)_{j,k\ne i}\Bigr),
\]
where $\Phi_{m-1}(\,\cdot\;C)$ is the centered Gaussian orthant probability with covariance $C$.  (ii) For $m=2$ the elasticity satisfies $0\le\eta(t)\le\sup_{x>0}x\varphi(x)/(2\Phi(x))=0.1472\ldots<1/2$ for all $t>0$.  (iii) If the points $x_i$ are collinear, then with $M=\max_i\langle Z,x_i\rangle$ and $I$ the almost-surely unique argmax, $\E[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2]=0$: every collinear configuration has vanishing second curvature.  (iv) For $3\le k\le m$ let the $k$-active configuration place $k$ points at the vertices of a centered regular simplex and $m-k$ points at the origin, with energy $S$.  Its Gaussian width is
\[
W_k(m,S)=\E\max_i\langle Z,x_i\rangle=\sqrt{\tfrac Sm}\,\frac{e_k}{\sqrt{k-1}},
\]
where $e_k$ is the expected maximum of $k$ independent standard Gaussians; and $e_3/\sqrt2=0.59841\ldots$ exceeds $e_4/\sqrt3=0.59431\ldots$ and $e_5/2=0.58148\ldots$, so for $m\in\{4,5\}$ the triangle configuration $k=3$ has strictly larger width than the full simplex $k=m$, and hence strictly larger $\theta_m$ at fixed energy for all sufficiently small scale.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Write $G_i=\langle Z,x_i\rangle$ and $\sigma_i^2=\lVert x_i\rVert^2$.  Each summand of $\theta_m=\sum_i\E[e^{G_i-\sigma_i^2/2}\,\mathbf 1\{G_i-\sigma_i^2/2\ \text{maximal}\}]$ is an Esscher tilt: under the measure with density $e^{G_i-\sigma_i^2/2}$ the vector $Z$ is a standard Gaussian shifted by $x_i$, so the summand equals the probability that $\langle Z,x_j-x_i\rangle\le(\sigma_i^2+\sigma_j^2-2\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)/2=\Gamma_{ij}/2$ for all $j\ne i$, a Gaussian orthant probability with covariances $\langle x_j-x_i,x_k-x_i\rangle=(\Gamma_{ij}+\Gamma_{ik}-\Gamma_{jk})/2$.  (ii) Here $\theta_2(t\Gamma)=2\Phi(x)$ with $x=\sqrt{t\Gamma_{12}}/2$, so $\eta=x\varphi(x)/(2\Phi(x))$, which is positive, vanishes at $x\to0$ and $x\to\infty$, and is bounded by $x\varphi(x)\le\varphi(1)=0.2419\ldots$ since $\Phi(x)\ge1/2$; the stated supremum is attained at $x=0.8399\ldots$.  (iii) For collinear $x_i=c_ie$ with a unit vector $e$ and $\zeta=\langle Z,e\rangle$, only the two extreme coefficients $c_{\min}<c_{\max}$ can be argmax, according to the sign of $\zeta$, so
\[
\E[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2]=c_{\max}^2\,\E[(\zeta^2-1)\mathbf 1\{\zeta>0\}]+c_{\min}^2\,\E[(\zeta^2-1)\mathbf 1\{\zeta<0\}]=0,
\]
each term vanishing because $\E[\zeta^2\mathbf 1\{\zeta>0\}]=\tfrac12=\Pr(\zeta>0)$.  For (iv): a centered configuration has $\sum_{i<j}\Gamma_{ij}=m\sum_i\lVert x_i\rVert^2$, so the $k$ active vertices have squared norm $a=S/(mk)$; unit regular-simplex directions $u_1,\ldots,u_k$ satisfy $\langle u_i,u_j\rangle=-1/(k-1)$ and $\sum_iu_i=0$, so the Gaussian vector $(\langle Z,u_i\rangle)_i$ has the law of $\sqrt{k/(k-1)}\,(\xi_i-\bar\xi)_i$ for independent standard $\xi_i$, whose expected maximum is $\sqrt{k/(k-1)}\,e_k$; the origin points never exceed the active maximum, which is nonnegative because the active values sum to zero; so $W_k=\sqrt a\,\sqrt{k/(k-1)}\,e_k=\sqrt{S/m}\,e_k/\sqrt{k-1}$.  The constants are $e_3=\tfrac32\pi^{-1/2}$ and the classical one-dimensional quadratures $e_4=1.029375\ldots$, $e_5=1.162964\ldots$, giving the stated ordering with margins $4\times10^{-3}$ and $1.7\times10^{-2}$; the width dominates the expansion of Conjecture~\ref{ah4} as the scale falls, so the triangle configuration exceeds the simplex for small scale.
\end{proof}

\section{The geometry of H\"usler--Reiss dependence}

\begin{conjecture}[Isoperimetry and symmetry breaking at fixed energy]\label{ah1}
(a) For $m=3$ and every $S>0$, among all admissible variograms with energy $\mathcal S(\Gamma)=S$, the equidistant variogram $\Gamma^{\mathrm{eq}}$ with all off-diagonal entries $S/\binom m2$, realized by a regular triangle, uniquely maximizes $\theta_3(\Gamma)$, up to relabeling.  (b) For every $m\ge4$ and every $S$, the maximum of $\theta_m$ at energy $S$ is attained by a $k$-active configuration of Proposition~\ref{ah:hr}(iv), $k$ components at the vertices of a centered regular simplex and $m-k$ coincident at the centroid, for some $3\le k\le m$, uniquely up to relabeling; the maximizing $k$ is nondecreasing in $S$, equals $3$ for all sufficiently small $S$, equals $m$ for all sufficiently large $S$, and passes through every intermediate value, so the fixed-energy optimizer recruits one component at a time through a staircase of symmetry-breaking transitions.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The extremal coefficient is the effective number of asymptotically independent components, and the deposited claim was that at fixed total variogram energy the most even allocation always buys the most independence; the refutation recorded in the preamble and in Proposition~\ref{ah:hr}(iv) shows this fails for $m\ge4$, because a centered second-moment budget rewards concentrating separation on few directions: the width identity $W_k=\sqrt{S/m}\,e_k/\sqrt{k-1}$ peaks at three active components, so near complete dependence a regular triangle with the other components parked at the centroid strictly beats the simplex.  What replaces the isoperimetry is a recruitment staircase inside the same one-parameter family.  In exact orthant computations at $m=5$, the three-active configuration is optimal among the family at scale $0.1$, the four-active configuration from scale $0.2$ through $0.5$, beating the simplex by $3.5\times10^{-3}$ at scale $0.35$, and the full simplex from scale $0.7$; unrestricted eighteen-parameter optimization at scale $0.35$ converges to the four-active configuration to three decimals, with paired Monte Carlo over one hundred million common samples confirming its margin $+3.4\times10^{-3}\pm1.5\times10^{-5}$ over the simplex, while at scales $1.0$ and $2.4$ no candidate beat the simplex; at $m=4$ the single interior transition sits near scale $0.125$.  At $m=3$ adversarial optimization returns the equilateral triangle to eight digits at every scale, so (a) keeps the deposited law where it is true.  The weak-dependence endpoint is forced by convexity of the pairwise deficit at large scale, and the nearest theorems, the simplex mean-width results, classical in Gaussian form~\cite{KLZ17} with a proof announced~\cite{Gol21}, fix the circumradius rather than the second moment and see no transition; the functional here is the finite-point Wills exponential~\cite{Vit96}.  A counterexample would be a scale where some configuration outside the $k$-active family wins, or a re-entrant staircase, either of which would break the recruitment mechanism.

\begin{conjecture}[Pairwise closure at weak dependence]\label{ah2}
Fix an admissible $\Gamma$ with strictly positive off-diagonal entries such that no three-or-higher-way Gaussian large-deviation saddle shares the exact rate of a contributing pairwise saddle.  Then, with $\delta_{ij}(t)=2-\theta_{ij}(t\Gamma)=2[1-\Phi(\sqrt{t\Gamma_{ij}}/2)]$,
\[
m-\theta_m(t\Gamma)\ \sim\ \sum_{i<j}\delta_{ij}(t),\qquad t\to\infty.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
At independence $\theta_m=m$, and the deficit $m-\theta_m$ measures residual simultaneous dependence; the consistency inequalities of Schlather and Tawn~\cite{ST02} give the Bonferroni bound $m-\theta_m\le\sum_{i<j}\delta_{ij}$ for every max-stable law, so the conjecture asserts that for H\"usler--Reiss models the bound is asymptotically exact: pair overlaps carry Gaussian-tail rates $t^{-1/2}e^{-t\Gamma_{ij}/8}$, and any triple overlap should demand an additional transversal Gaussian constraint and hence a strictly larger rate, exactly as pair interactions dominate dilute systems.  The genericity hypothesis is the honest boundary: a third site sitting exactly on a pairwise saddle can conceivably share its exponential rate, and the conjecture isolates rather than hides that set.  The higher-order expansions known for H\"usler--Reiss maxima~\cite{HPW16} concern convergence of Gaussian triangular arrays to the limit, not the independence asymptotics of $\theta_m$ in the variogram scale, so the equivalence appears to be new.  In exact tests on random, equilateral, and near-degenerate geometries at $m=3,4$ the ratio of the two sides rose monotonically toward one across $t=6$ to $96$, reaching $0.9215$, $0.9795$, $0.9988$, $0.999996$, $1.000000$ on a random triangle, $1.000000$ from $t=12$ on a random and a near-degenerate quadrilateral, and rising more slowly, $0.831$ to $0.998$, on the equilateral triangle, whose symmetric triple competition is the strongest.  A counterexample would be a geometry whose triple saddle survives at pairwise rate, and would identify the exceptional set as substantive rather than technical.

\begin{conjecture}[Scale elasticity and monotone dependence]\label{ah3}
For every admissible nonzero $\Gamma$: (a) $0\le\eta(t)\le\tfrac12$ for all $t>0$; (b) if $\Gamma'$ is admissible and $\Gamma_{ij}\le\Gamma'_{ij}$ entrywise, then $\theta_m(\Gamma)\le\theta_m(\Gamma')$.  Consequently, if $L,\widetilde L$ are connected graph Laplacians with $(1-\eps)L\preceq\widetilde L\preceq(1+\eps)L$ on $\mathbf 1^\perp$ and $\Gamma(L)$ is the resistance variogram $\Gamma_{ij}(L)=(e_i-e_j)^\top L^\dagger(e_i-e_j)$, then
\[
(1+\eps)^{-1/2}\ \le\ \frac{\theta_m(\Gamma(\widetilde L))}{\theta_m(\Gamma(L))}\ \le\ (1-\eps)^{-1/2}.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The two claims are a differential and an order-theoretic rigidity for the extremal coefficient, and together they convert spectral sparsification into a dimension-free guarantee for extremal dependence: the Laplacian sandwich passes to effective resistances entrywise, monotonicity passes it to $\theta_m$, and the elasticity bound integrates to the displayed square-root distortion, so the conclusion follows from (a) and (b) by a three-line chain recorded here.  Proposition~\ref{ah:hr} proves (a) for $m=2$ with best constant $0.1472$, far inside the conjectured bound, and the bound $1/2$ is the log-log elasticity of $\theta_m-1$, whose leading $\sqrt t$ term at $t\downarrow0$ from Conjecture~\ref{ah4} has elasticity exactly $1/2$, whereas the elasticity of $\theta_m$ itself, $\eta(t)=t\theta_m'/\theta_m=(c/2)\sqrt t+O(t)$, tends to zero there, so $1/2$ is a conjectural cap and not a value forced by the complete-dependence expansion; monotonicity in the entrywise order is Slepian-type folklore for which no published statement at the level of $\theta_m$ on the full admissible cone was found.  This conjecture is close to prior work: spectral sparsification of H\"usler--Reiss graphical models is the subject of~\cite{EAR26}, which proves multiplicative variogram preservation and likelihood control under exactly this sandwich, so the new content is the transfer to the extremal coefficient with the universal exponent one half, strengthening rather than paralleling their guarantees; the graphical-model calculus itself is~\cite{EH20,HES25}.  In tests, the elasticity over eighty-three random geometries at $m\le5$, twelve scales each, and over near-degenerate and elongated shapes, never exceeded $0.334$, and $\theta_m$ was monotone on all $150$ admissible entrywise-increase pairs, sixty-seven of them with non-variogram difference, and on sixty additive cone directions.  A counterexample to (a) above one half would break the sparsification law at its stated exponent; one to (b) would exhibit dependence that decreases when every pair separates.

\begin{conjecture}[Positive curvature at complete dependence, resolved true]\label{ah4}
For centered points $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ realizing $\Gamma$, with $M=\max_i\langle Z,x_i\rangle$ and $I$ the argmax, as $t\downarrow0$,
\[
\theta_m(t\Gamma)=1+\sqrt t\,\E M+t\,q(\Gamma)+o(t),\qquad q(\Gamma)=\tfrac12\,\E\bigl[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2\bigr],
\]
and $q(\Gamma)\ge0$ always, with $q(\Gamma)=0$ if and only if, after deleting non-exposed points, the convex hull of the $x_i$ is a point or a segment.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The first-order coefficient $\E M$ is the Gaussian mean-width functional of the configuration, so the expansion says the departure of $\theta_m$ from complete dependence opens at Sudakov's term and the conjecture locates the sign and the null set of the second term: a genuinely two-or-higher-dimensional exposed geometry always curves upward.  The convex-body shadow is classical, the Wills functional of a body expands in intrinsic volumes with nonnegative second coefficient vanishing exactly on segments~\cite{Vit96}, but $\theta_m$ is the finite-point analogue, its argmax form $\E[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2]$ is not an intrinsic volume of the hull, and no strong-dependence expansion of H\"usler--Reiss extremal coefficients appears in the extremes literature.  Proposition~\ref{ah:hr}(iii) proves the null direction, every collinear configuration has $q=0$ by an exact sign-conditioning identity, so the open content is strict positivity off segments together with the validity of the expansion.  In tests, $q$ was computed exactly for planar configurations by polar quadrature: adversarial minimization at $m=3$ and $m=4$ drives the minimum to $-2\times10^{-16}$, machine zero, attained in both cases at collinear configurations, while thin triangles of height $h$ over a unit base keep $q>0$ with $q$ vanishing linearly in $h$, from $4.3\times10^{-2}$ at $h=0.3$ to $4.8\times10^{-4}$ at $h=0.003$, and with $w$ and $q$ computed exactly by polar quadrature on a random planar triple, the finite-$t$ residual $[\theta_3(t\Gamma)-1-\sqrt t\,w]/t$ rose to the exact $q=0.08370$ through $0.07993$, $0.08183$, $0.08277$, $0.08324$ as $t$ fell from $6.4\times10^{-3}$ to $10^{-4}$, the deficit shrinking like $\sqrt t$.  A counterexample would be an exposed planar configuration with vanishing or negative curvature, which would refute the finite-point Wills analogy at its first nontrivial order.  Since deposit the conjecture has been resolved true: Proposition~\ref{ah:curv} proves the expansion together with the nonnegativity of $q(\Gamma)$ and the equality classification, the positivity following from a Gaussian integration by parts for the support function of the exposed hull.

\section{Cluster inverse problems under thinning}

\begin{proposition}[Thinning calibration for the cluster programme]\label{ah:thin}
Let the limiting cluster have size $N$ with generating function $G_N$ and, where stated, finite support $S\subset\Z$.  At the level of the limiting compound-Poisson cluster process:
(i) independent retention with probability $p$ gives the response $\theta(p)=\theta\,(1-G_N(1-p))/p$;
(ii) retention of one residue class modulo $m$ with uniform random phase gives $\theta^{\mathrm{sys}}_m=\theta\,\E R_m(S)$, where $R_m(S)$ is the number of occupied residues;
(iii) the joint response $Q_{m,S}(p)=\tfrac1m\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}[1-(1-p)^{n_{m,r}(S)}]$, known for $p$ in any infinite subset of $(0,1)$, determines the occupancy multiset $\mathcal N_m(S)$;
(iv) the occupancy data $\{\mathcal N_m(S):m\ge2\}$ determines the difference multiset of $S$;
(v) occupancy equivalence is closed under dilation: $\mathcal N_m(tS)=\mathcal N_{m/\gcd(t,m)}(S)$ for every $t\ge1$, so $S\sim S'$ implies $tS\sim tS'$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Thinning replaces each cluster by a $\operatorname{Binomial}(N,p)$ survivor count $K$; the surviving-cluster intensity is the original cluster intensity times $\Pr(K>0)=1-G_N(1-p)$, the exceedance intensity is scaled by $\E K=p\,\E N$, and the extremal index is their ratio, giving $(1-G_N(1-p))/(p\,\E N)$.  (ii) With uniform phase $U$, the retained count is $K=|\{s\in S:s\equiv U\}|$, so $\Pr(K>0\mid S)=R_m(S)/m$ and $\E(K\mid S)=|S|/m$; the ratio of expectations is $\E R_m(S)/\E|S|$.  (iii) Averaging Bernoulli thinning over the phase gives exactly $Q_{m,S}(p)$; the functions $p\mapsto1-(1-p)^k$ for distinct positive integers $k$ are linearly independent, being polynomials of distinct degrees in $1-p$, so the coefficients of the representation of $Q_{m,S}$ in this family, which are $\tfrac1m$ times the multiplicities of the occupancy counts, are determined.  (iv) From $\mathcal N_m(S)$ form $g(m)=\sum_r\binom{n_{m,r}(S)}2$, the number of pairs of $S$ congruent modulo $m$, and set $g(1)=\binom{|S|}2$; if $c_\delta$ is the number of pairs at difference $\delta\ge1$ then $g(m)=\sum_{m\mid\delta}c_\delta$ for every $m\ge1$, a finitely supported divisor sum, and M\"obius inversion gives $c_\delta=\sum_{j\ge1}\mu(j)\,g(j\delta)$.  (v) Write $g=\gcd(t,m)$, $m=gm_1$, $t=gt_1$.  Then $ts\bmod m=g\,(t_1s\bmod m_1)$, and since $\gcd(t_1,m_1)=1$ the map $u\mapsto t_1u$ permutes the residues modulo $m_1$; so the nonzero occupancy counts of $tS$ modulo $m$ are exactly those of $S$ modulo $m_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Resolution of the complete-dependence curvature law]\label{ah:curv}
Conjecture~\ref{ah4} holds in full: the displayed expansion is valid, $q(\Gamma)\ge0$ for every admissible $\Gamma$, and $q(\Gamma)=0$ if and only if the convex hull of the exposed points is a point or a segment.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write $\eps=\sqrt t$, $G_i=\langle Z,x_i\rangle$, $M=\max_iG_i$ with almost-surely unique argmax $I$ after deleting non-exposed and duplicate points, and $V_\eps=\max_i(\eps G_i-\tfrac{\eps^2}2\lVert x_i\rVert^2)$, so $\theta_m(t\Gamma)=\E e^{V_\eps}$.  From $|V_\eps-\eps M|\le\tfrac{\eps^2}2\max_i\lVert x_i\rVert^2$ and uniform integrability of $e^{\eps M}$ for small $\eps$, dominated expansion gives $\theta_m(t\Gamma)=1+\eps\,\E M+\tfrac{\eps^2}2\E[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2]+o(\eps^2)$, the asserted expansion with $q(\Gamma)=\tfrac12\E[M^2-\lVert x_I\rVert^2]$.  Now $M=h_K(Z)$ is the support function of $K=\operatorname{conv}\{x_i\}$; the $x_i$ are centered, so $0=\tfrac1m\sum_ix_i$ lies in the relative interior of $K$ and $M\ge0$, while $M$ is convex and $1$-homogeneous with $\nabla M=x_I$ almost everywhere.  Gaussian integration by parts and Euler's identity $\langle z,\nabla M\rangle=M$ give
\[
\E[M^2]=\E\langle Z,M\nabla M\rangle=\E\lVert\nabla M\rVert^2+\E[M\,\Delta M],
\]
where $\Delta M\ge0$ is the curvature measure of the convex function $M$; since $M\ge0$ the last term is nonnegative and $\lVert\nabla M\rVert^2=\lVert x_I\rVert^2$ almost everywhere, so $q(\Gamma)\ge0$.  Equality forces $M=0$ on $\operatorname{supp}\Delta M$; if $\dim K\ge2$ then $0$ lies in the relative interior of $K$, so $M>0$ at every nonzero point of the affine span of $K$, on which the nonzero curvature measure $\Delta M$ is supported, and the term is strictly positive.  Hence $q(\Gamma)=0$ iff $\dim K\le1$, and for a point or a segment the curvature measure sits where $M=0$, giving $q=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Bernoulli-thinning spectroscopy of clusters]\label{ah5}
Let $(X_t)$ be stationary and regularly varying, with exceedances converging to a compound-Poisson cluster process with cluster size $N$, $\E N<\infty$, and extremal index $\theta=1/\E N$, under mixing and anti-clustering conditions.  Retain each observation independently with probability $p$ and compress the time axis.  Then the retained sequence satisfies the same hypotheses with extremal index $\theta(p)=\theta\,(1-G_N(1-p))/p$, uniformly for $p$ in compact subsets of $(0,1]$; consequently the response curve $p\mapsto\theta(p)$ identifies the entire limiting cluster-size law.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The formula itself is the cluster-level algebra of Proposition~\ref{ah:thin}(i), and extremal indices of randomly subsampled sequences are an established subject~\cite{HS08,MF04,RT00}, so the formula is claimed as calibration, not novelty; the conjectural content is the transport theorem, that thinning commutes with the cluster limit uniformly enough in $p$ for the curve to be an inferential object, and the spectroscopic consequence, that a one-parameter family of scalar extremal indices inverts to the full cluster-size distribution via $G_N(1-p)=1-p\,\theta(p)/\theta$, for which no statement was found.  Cluster-size inference is otherwise a direct estimation problem~\cite{Rob09}; the conjecture replaces estimation of a distribution by estimation of a curve of scalars, each a standard blocks quantity.  In process-level tests on a four-lag moving-maximum process with twelve million steps, the blocks estimator of the thinned sequence matched the formula at $p=1,\,0.7,\,0.4,\,0.2$ with ratios $0.988$, $0.989$, $0.954$, $0.976$, the common shortfall being the finite-threshold bias of the estimator itself.  A counterexample would be a process whose thinned clusters fail the predicted limit at some $p$, which would locate a genuine obstruction to interchanging thinning and clustering.

\begin{conjecture}[Occupancy tomography of cluster supports]\label{ah6}
(a) Every finite $S\subset\Z$ with $|S|\le5$ is determined by its occupancy data up to translation and reflection.  (b) For every finite size, each occupancy-equivalence class of finite integer sets contains at most two translation--reflection classes.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The two-parameter thinning response determines exactly the occupancy data, by Proposition~\ref{ah:thin}(iii), so this conjecture is the precise inverse theory of cluster-shape tomography, and its shape is dictated by a refutation recorded in the part preamble: full reconstruction is impossible, because Bloom's pair $\{0,1,4,10,12,17\}$, $\{0,1,8,11,13,17\}$~\cite{Blo77}, the classical counterexample to Piccard's theorem~\cite{Pat44}, shares every occupancy multiset, by finite check through modulus seventeen and trivially beyond the diameter.  Occupancy equivalence thus sits strictly between congruence and homometry: it implies homometry by Proposition~\ref{ah:thin}(iv), the census found every collision homometric, ten collisions among the $6437$ canonical sets of size at most six through diameter eighteen and the $3312$ of size at most seven through diameter fourteen, while the homometric pair $\{0,1,3,8,10,14\}$, $\{0,1,7,9,11,14\}$ is occupancy-distinguished, so the refinement is strict on both sides, and dilation closure, Proposition~\ref{ah:thin}(v), generates infinite equivalent families from each collision.
