Among Sidon sets clause (b) is a theorem: occupancy equivalence implies homometry, and Bekir and Golomb proved Bloom's pair essentially the only homometric Sidon ambiguity~\cite{BG07}; the general case, and the five-mark determination (a), verified exhaustively through diameter twenty-two, are open, with the turnpike literature~\cite{LSS03} the nearest boundary.  A counterexample to (a) would be a five-mark ambiguity below every census run; one to (b) would be a triple of pairwise occupancy-equivalent, pairwise non-congruent sets.

\section{The topology of extreme directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Consistency of persistent angular homology]\label{ah7}
Let $X$ be $d$-variate regularly varying whose angular law $H$ is supported on a compact $C^2$ $s$-dimensional manifold $M$ of positive reach in the open simplex, with density bounded above and below.  Let $A_{n,k}$ be the angular components of the $k=k_n$ largest radii, $k\to\infty$, $k/n\to0$, and suppose the conditional angular law beyond radius $t$ couples to $H$ with Hausdorff bias at most $b(t)\to0$.  Then for every homological degree $q$,
\[
d_B\bigl(\operatorname{Dgm}_q(\operatorname{VR}(A_{n,k})),\operatorname{Dgm}_q(\operatorname{VR}(M))\bigr)
=O_p\Bigl(b(U(n/k))+\bigl(\tfrac{\log k}k\bigr)^{1/s}\Bigr),
\]
with $U$ the radial quantile function and $d_B$ the bottleneck distance.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Angular inference in extremes estimates masses, faces, and linear structure; the conjecture makes loops and components of the support an estimand with a rate, composing two known machines, the stability of persistence diagrams under Hausdorff perturbation~\cite{CEH07} and the $(\log k/k)^{1/s}$ covering rates of manifold samples~\cite{NSW08,CGLM15}, with a genuinely extreme-value ingredient: the angular points are selected by top-$k$ radii, are not an independent sample from $H$, and sit at finite threshold, displaced by $b(U(n/k))$.  The nearest body of work, the topology of extreme sample clouds and its persistence limit theorems~\cite{Owa18}, studies the crackle of the cloud itself, not consistency for the angular support, so the statement appears new while its proof budget, a Poissonization of the order-statistics selection, is plausibly within reach; the rate also gives a threshold-selection principle, balancing radial bias against topological sampling error.  In process-level tests on a ring in the three-part simplex with an explicit second-order bias $b(t)=0.9/t$ and two million observations, the Hausdorff distance tracked the predicted two-term sum within a factor $0.55$ to $1.22$ across $k=50$ to $3200$, top-$k$ covering radii matched independent-sample covering radii, and the Vietoris--Rips diagrams of an independent $\mathbb F_2$ implementation showed a single dominant loop with death $0.3123$ against the analytic $\sqrt3\,\rho=0.3118$, the bottleneck error falling from $0.115$ at $k=40$ to $0.049$ at $k=120$.  A counterexample would show the intermediate-order selection itself distorting the covering rate, the failure mode the conjecture exists to exclude.

\begin{conjecture}[A leakage trichotomy for hidden extremes]\label{ah8}
Let $X=R_0W_0+R_1W_1$ with independent components: $R_0$ regularly varying with index $\alpha_0$, $R_1$ with index $\alpha_1>\alpha_0$, and angular laws $W_0\sim H_0$, $W_1\sim H_1$ supported on compact sets $M_0$, $M_1$ separated in the simplex, $H_1$ as in Conjecture~\ref{ah7}.  Remove the angular neighborhood $N_{\delta_n}(M_0)$, rerank the surviving radii, and let $L_n$ be the ratio of the primary to the hidden mechanism's contribution to the surviving exceedance intensity at the hidden threshold.  Let $\Lambda_n$ be the expected number of surviving leaked primary exceedances in the reranked top-$k_n$ sample, and suppose the leaked support $M_{\mathrm{leak}}$ is persistence-separated from $M_1$, $d_B(\mathrm{Dgm}_q(M_1\cup M_{\mathrm{leak}}),\mathrm{Dgm}_q(M_1))\ge c_0>0$.  Then: if $\Lambda_n\to0$, the persistence diagrams of the surviving angular sample recover those of $M_1$ at the rate of Conjecture~\ref{ah7}; if $\Lambda_n\to\infty$ they do not; and for $\Lambda_n\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$ the surviving leaked primaries are asymptotically Poisson-$\lambda$ and the probability of recovery within any fixed bottleneck tolerance below the hidden feature scale converges to a limit $p(\lambda)\in(0,1)$, so feature detection switches on the leaked-count scale $\Lambda_n\asymp1$, that is $L_n\asymp1/k_n$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Hidden regular variation is a competition of tail orders on nested cones~\cite{Res08,MR11}, and the filtering primitive, removing the cone of the first-order limit and asking what remains, is exactly the detection scheme of Mitra and Resnick; the conjecture makes the competition quantitative at the level of topology, asserting that what decides visibility is not the index gap $\alpha_1-\alpha_0$ but the finite-threshold leakage ratio after support removal, because a handful of leaked heavy points can fill a loop or bridge components.  The two-mechanism additive model makes the ratio well-defined without reference to unobservable labels, and sparse-support methods~\cite{MW21} are the statistical neighbors.  In tests at $\alpha_0=1$, $\alpha_1=2$ with primary mass on the axes spread by a parameter $\eta$ and hidden mass on a ring: the unfiltered top sample had three components and no loop; after filtering, at leakage $0.034$ and $0.081$ the ring was recovered with bottleneck error $0.090$ and $0.075$, while at leakage $2.9$ and $120$ the error rose to $0.143$ and $0.156$, the failure value being half the true persistence, so the diagram no longer matched the ring on either side of the crossover, exactly the predicted switch.  The governing scale is the leaked count, not the intensity ratio: under the intermediate-order sampling of Conjecture~\ref{ah7} a fixed ratio $L_n\to\lambda>0$ leaks order-$k_n$ points and floods the diagram, so the nondegenerate crossover sits at $\Lambda_n\asymp1$, and the finite-sample transition seen near $L_n\asymp1$ is its reflection at the tested sizes.  A counterexample would be a regime with $\Lambda_n\to0$ and persistent contamination, or recovery surviving $\Lambda_n\to\infty$, either of which would refute the leaked count as the governing scale.

\section{Tail tomography and its stability}

\begin{proposition}[Moment calibration for the tomography programme]\label{ah:moment}
(i) If $\alpha>0$ is not an integer, then $T_\alpha H$ restricted to any open subset of $(0,\infty)^d$ determines the finite measure $H$ on $\Delta_{d-1}$ uniquely.  (ii) If $\alpha=q\in\mathbb N_0$, then $T_qH$ depends only on the moments of $H$ of degree at most $q$, and injectivity fails; explicitly, for $d=2$, $q=2$, the measures
\[
H_1=\tfrac12\delta_{0.2}+\tfrac12\delta_{0.8},\qquad
H_2=0.28125\,\delta_{0.1}+0.4375\,\delta_{0.5}+0.28125\,\delta_{0.9}
\]
satisfy $T_2H_1=T_2H_2$ identically while $T_{3/2}H_1\ne T_{3/2}H_2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) Since $\mathbf 1\cdot w=1$ on the simplex, directions $a=c(\mathbf 1+z)$ with $\lVert z\rVert_\infty<1$ give $(a\cdot w)^\alpha=c^\alpha(1+z\cdot w)^\alpha$, and $z\mapsto\int(1+z\cdot w)^\alpha H(\dd w)$ is real-analytic on $\lVert z\rVert_\infty<1$, its binomial series converging uniformly.  Agreement of $T_\alpha H$ on an open set forces agreement of this analytic function everywhere on the polydisc, hence of all its Taylor coefficients at $z=0$, which are $\binom\alpha k$ times the degree-$k$ moment forms of $H$; for noninteger $\alpha$ every $\binom\alpha k\ne0$, so all mixed moments agree, and moments determine a finite measure on a compact simplex by Stone--Weierstrass and Riesz representation.  (ii) For integer $q$ the binomial series terminates at degree $q$.  Identifying $w\in\Delta_1$ with its first coordinate, $(a\cdot w)^2=(a_2+(a_1-a_2)w)^2$ involves only $\int w^j\,\dd H$ for $j\le2$; both displayed measures have total mass $1$, first moment $0.028125+0.21875+0.253125=0.5$ and second moment $0.0028125+0.109375+0.2278125=0.34$ against $\tfrac12(0.2+0.8)=0.5$ and $\tfrac12(0.04+0.64)=0.34$, so $T_2H_1=T_2H_2$; their third moments are $0.26$ and $0.2456\ldots$, so by (i) any noninteger power separates them, and at $\alpha=3/2$ the relative difference reaches $2.0\times10^{-3}$ on the tested direction grid.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[The stability barrier of fractional tail tomography]\label{ah9}
Fix noninteger $\alpha>0$, $0<\eta<1$, and the direction box $A_\eta=\{a:\eta\le a_i\le\eta^{-1}\}$.  (a) There exist no $C,\beta>0$ with $W_1(H_1,H_2)\le C\,\lVert T_\alpha H_1-T_\alpha H_2\rVert_{L^\infty(A_\eta)}^\beta$ for all probability measures $H_1,H_2$ on $\Delta_{d-1}$.  (b) On the class of angular densities lying in a H\"older ball $\{f:\lVert f\rVert_{C^s}\le L,\ f\ge c>0\}$, the inverse admits a logarithmic modulus of continuity: $W_1(H_1,H_2)\lesssim(\log(1/\eps))^{-\kappa_s}$ with $\eps$ the transform error, for some $\kappa_s>0$ depending on $s$, and no polynomial modulus $\eps^\beta$ is valid on the class.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Proposition~\ref{ah:moment} settles identifiability, integers lose it algebraically, fractional powers keep it, the dichotomy known in substance from the theory of zonoid equivalence and diagonal Minkowski classes~\cite{MN21} and visible in extreme-value practice as the non-uniqueness of angular measures behind the tail pairwise dependence matrix at $\alpha=2$~\cite{CT19}; the conjecture is the quantitative sequel, that fractional identifiability is severely ill-posed, because the kernel $(a\cdot w)^\alpha$ is real-analytic on the box, its singular values collapse geometrically, and recovery passes through arbitrarily high moments, the phenomenon known for analytic-kernel moment problems~\cite{Tal87} but not instantiated for one-sided projection tails of angular measures.  In discretized tests at $\alpha=3/2$ against $\alpha=2$: the $\alpha=2$ transform matrix had exact numerical rank three while the $\alpha=3/2$ matrix had effective ranks $4$, $10$, $15$ at thresholds $10^{-4}$, $10^{-8}$, $10^{-12}$ with tenth singular value $2.2\times10^{-9}$, and zero-mass oscillating perturbations at frequencies $2$ through $16$ drove the ratio of transform norm to Wasserstein scale from $0.70$ down to $0.048$, the super-polynomial collapse the barrier predicts.  A counterexample to (a), a global H\"older inverse, would make nonparametric angular tomography from tail constants routine, against all numerical evidence; a proof of (b) would explain why sparse and parametric tail models succeed where unrestricted reconstruction fails.

\begin{conjecture}[A parameter-count threshold for sparse tail tomography]\label{ah10}
Let $H=\sum_{r=1}^s\pi_r\delta_{w_r}$ with distinct atoms in the open simplex $\Delta_{d-1}^\circ$, weights $\pi_r>0$ summing to one, and let $p=sd-1$ be the parameter count.  Fix noninteger $\alpha>0$ and observe $y_j=(T_\alpha H)(a_j)$ at generic positive directions $a_1,\ldots,a_m$.  Then, outside a proper real-analytic exceptional set of atom configurations and designs, and quantitatively away from atom collisions and the simplex boundary: for $m<p$ identifiability fails on a positive-dimensional fiber; for $m=p$ the Jacobian has full rank and the fiber is finite, so the mixture is locally rigid but need not be unique; and for every $m\ge sd$ the measurement vector determines $H$ globally up to permutation of atoms, with local inverse modulus controlled by atom separation and boundary distance.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The placement of the global threshold one measurement above the count is forced by two computations recorded in the preamble.  A near-coincident atom pair first produced ten apparent interpolants at $m=p$ that all collapsed under forty-digit Newton polishing into the single true solution, an artifact of conditioning fixed by the separation hypothesis; then a genuine multiplicity survived every polish: at $(d,s)=(3,3)$, two of six well-separated random instances admit a second exact interior three-atom mixture at $m=p=8$, with atoms nowhere near the truth and residuals below $10^{-25}$, and in both instances the ambiguity disappears at $m=9$.  So the counting boundary buys exactly local rigidity, the fractional analogue of the identifiability counts of multivariate Prony and super-resolution theory, which live on integer moments and have no counterpart here, and global uniqueness is conjectured to begin at $m=sd$, where both refuting instances become unique again.  In tests at noninteger $\alpha=1.37$: at $m=p-1$ the fiber is visibly a continuum, fifty distinct exact interior interpolants from one hundred twenty starts at $(d,s)=(3,2)$; at $m=p$, all six separated instances at $(d,s)=(3,2)$ and four of six at $(3,3)$ returned exactly the true mixture, the other two returning the truth plus one extra that dissolves at $m=9$.  A counterexample would be a separated generic instance with two exact mixtures persisting above the count, which would push the design requirement higher still.

\section{Randomized block designs}

\begin{proposition}[Design calibration for the block programme]\label{ah:block}
(i) If $\bar F(x)=x^{-\alpha}$ and $N_n\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(n)$, then $\Pr(M_{N_n}/n^{1/\alpha}\le x)=e^{-x^{-\alpha}}$ exactly for every $n$.  (ii) For any block-size law, $\log\E(1-q)^{N_n}=\sum_{r\ge1}\kappa_r^{(F)}(-q)^r/r!$, so matching factorial cumulants of the Poisson law through order $r$ cancels the sampling corrections through order $q^r$.  (iii) For every $r\ge2$ there is a law $\xi$ on a finite subset of $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$, not Poisson, whose cumulants match those of $\operatorname{Poisson}(1)$ through order $r$; the convolution $N_n=\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_n$ then has $\E N_n=n$, $\operatorname{Var}N_n=n$, $\kappa_j^{(F)}(N_n)=0$ for $2\le j\le r$, $\kappa_{r+1}^{(F)}(N_n)=O(n)$, and for the Pareto seed
\[
\sup_x\bigl|\Pr(M_{N_n}/n^{1/\alpha}\le x)-e^{-x^{-\alpha}}\bigr|=O(n^{-r})
\]
uniformly on compact $x$-sets.  For $r=3$ the law on $\{0,1,3\}$ with weights $(\tfrac13,\tfrac12,\tfrac16)$ and for $r=4$ the law on $\{0,1,2,4\}$ with weights $(\tfrac38,\tfrac13,\tfrac14,\tfrac1{24})$ are such laws.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) The Poisson generating function gives $\E(1-q)^{N_n}=e^{-nq}$, and $q=x^{-\alpha}/n$ makes the exponent exactly $-x^{-\alpha}$.  (ii) is the definition of factorial cumulants at argument $u=-q$.  (iii) The moment vector $(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$ of $\operatorname{Poisson}(1)$ is the convex combination $\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-1}/k!\,(k,k^2,\ldots,k^r)$ of points on the integer moment curve, so by Carath\'eodory it is a convex combination of at most $r+1$ such points: a law $\xi$ on at most $r+1$ nonnegative integers with the first $r$ moments, hence the first $r$ cumulants, of $\operatorname{Poisson}(1)$.  No finitely supported law is Poisson.  Cumulants add under convolution, so $\kappa_j(N_n)=n\kappa_j(\xi)$ matches $\kappa_j(\operatorname{Poisson}(n))$ for $j\le r$; each factorial cumulant $\kappa_j^{(F)}$ is a fixed linear combination of $\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_j$, and Poisson$(n)$ has $\kappa_j^{(F)}=0$ for $j\ge2$, so $\kappa_j^{(F)}(N_n)=0$ for $2\le j\le r$, while $\kappa_{r+1}^{(F)}(N_n)$ is $n$ times a constant depending on $\xi$.  Because the summand factorial cumulants vanish through order $r$, the analytic function $q\mapsto\log\E(1-q)^{\xi}$ equals $-q+O(q^{r+1})$ on $[0,q_0]$, so $\log\E(1-q)^{N_n}=-nq+O(nq^{r+1})$; with $q=x^{-\alpha}/n$ bounded on compacts this is $-x^{-\alpha}+O(n^{-r})$, and exponentiating gives the uniform bound.  For the displayed laws the moment checks are exact rational arithmetic: on $\{0,1,3\}$ the raw moments are $\tfrac12+\tfrac36=1$, $\tfrac12+\tfrac96=2$, $\tfrac12+\tfrac{27}6=5$, matching $\operatorname{Poisson}(1)$ through order three with fourth cumulant $0\ne1$; on $\{0,1,2,4\}$ the raw moments are $1,2,5,15$, matching through order four with fifth cumulant differing; so both are non-Poisson with all factorial cumulants of order at most $r$ vanishing.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Poissonized blocks remove the universal bias]\label{ah11}
Let $F$ lie in a max-domain of attraction with a uniform second-order expansion $n\bar F(a_nx+b_n)=V(x)+A(n)B(x)+o(A(n))+o(n^{-1})$ on compact interior sets.  Then Poissonized block maxima satisfy $\log\Pr(M_{N_n}\le a_nx+b_n)=-V(x)-A(n)B(x)+o(A(n))+o(n^{-1})$, the universal $V(x)^2/(2n)$ correction of fixed blocks being absent; and for generalized-extreme-value likelihood estimation from many independent blocks, Poissonization leaves the first-order asymptotic variance unchanged while removing the universal $n^{-1}$ bias contribution, so that when $A(n)=o(n^{-1})$ the estimator bias improves from order $n^{-1}$ to the intrinsic second order.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The identity behind the conjecture is elementary and exact for the Pareto seed, Proposition~\ref{ah:block}(i), the Poisson generating function exponentiating the one-observation tail with no binomial discretization error, and the object it removes is precisely the universal finite-block term documented in the second-order block-maxima theory~\cite{BVZ19,DF19} and in the comparison of block maxima with threshold methods~\cite{BZ21}; the distributional clause needs no lift beyond the seed, since $\Pr(M_{N_n}\le y)=\E F(y)^{N_n}=e^{-n\bar F(y)}$ exactly for Poisson exposure and every $F$, so the second-order expansion removes the $V^2/(2n)$ term across the whole second-order max-domain; what is genuinely conjectured is the estimator clause, the transfer of that cancellation to generalized-extreme-value likelihood, in the framework of~\cite{dHF06}.  Maxima over random sample sizes have been studied for their dependence attractors, not as a bias-cancellation design, so the design reading appears new, and the natural objection, that a Poisson number of observations per block is threshold exceedance in disguise, is answered by the estimator clause: the procedure remains a blocks procedure with blockwise likelihood, changing only the exposure law.  In estimator-level tests with three hundred thousand blocks of Pareto data, the Fr\'echet shape estimate from fixed blocks carried the predicted order-$1/n$ bias while the honestly Poissonized version removed it: shape bias $+0.0396$ against $+0.0017$ at $n=32$, and $+0.0100$ against $+0.0031$ at $n=128$, the fixed-block bias falling exactly like $1/n$ and the Poissonized residual sitting at the finite-sample likelihood level.  A counterexample would be a second-order family where Poissonization leaves an $n^{-1}$ term, which would locate a non-universal component in the finite-block correction.

\begin{conjecture}[The factorial-cumulant design ladder]\label{ah12}
Fix $r\ge2$ and let $N_n$ be an $r$-th ladder law as in Proposition~\ref{ah:block}(iii).  Then in every max-domain with the second-order expansion of Conjecture~\ref{ah11}, block maxima with exposure $N_n$ satisfy the expansion with sampling-mechanism corrections of order $O(n^{-r})$ in place of $V^2/(2n)$; and generalized-extreme-value likelihood estimation from many independent randomized blocks retains the first-order limit law and variance of deterministic blocks while its sampling-mechanism bias falls to $O(n^{-r})+o(A(n))$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The algebra is proved: Proposition~\ref{ah:block} exhibits, for every $r$, integer exposure laws with variance $n$ whose factorial cumulants vanish through order $r$ and whose exact finite-block error for the Pareto seed is $O(n^{-r})$, so the ladder exists constructively, block design becoming a quadrature problem in which each matched factorial cumulant annihilates one universal error term.  What remains conjectural is the statistical half: that the cancellation survives general second-order domains and passes through blockwise likelihood with unchanged first-order variance, and that the bounded-support ladder laws, whose cumulants are all $O(n)$, avoid the degradation that heavy exposure randomization would cause.  No design principle of this kind appears in the random-sample-size or block-maxima literature.  In exact tests at Pareto seed with $\alpha=2$ across $n=64$ to $16384$: fixed blocks gave sup-error slope $-1.001$, the two-point law $n\pm\sqrt n$ gave $-2.002$, and the ladder laws of Proposition~\ref{ah:block} gave $-3.004$ and $-4.004$ in fifty-digit arithmetic, each error falling by its predicted factor, eighty-three-fold and two-hundred-fifty-six-fold, per fourfold block growth.  A counterexample would be a domain in which some non-universal $n^{-j}$ term, $j\le r$, survives every exposure law, which would split the finite-block error into design-cancellable and intrinsic parts.

\begin{conjecture}[An adaptation cusp at second-order cancellation]\label{ah13}
In a smooth Hall family $\bar F_\lambda(x)=x^{-\alpha}[1+c(\lambda)x^{-\beta}+d(\lambda)x^{-2\beta}+o(x^{-2\beta})]$ with $c(\lambda_0)=0$, $c'(\lambda_0)\ne0$, $d(\lambda_0)\ne0$, the oracle threshold for Hill-type estimation moves from $k\asymp n^{2\beta/(\alpha+2\beta)}$ generically to $k\asymp n^{4\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$ at cancellation, the two regimes meeting at the critical window $|c(\lambda)|\asymp n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$; and no data-driven threshold selector is uniformly oracle-rate optimal, with the same constants, over both $|c(\lambda)|\le Cn^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$ and $|c(\lambda)|\gg n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$: an adaptation penalty, at least logarithmic or a nontrivial constant, is unavoidable in the cusp.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This conjecture is close to prior work: that adaptive tail estimation pays an unavoidable logarithmic-type penalty is the theorem of Carpentier and Kim~\cite{CK15}, with the threshold-selection literature going back to~\cite{Hall82,DK98,Pic75}; the new content is the location and geometry of the obstruction, a cusp of measure zero in the parameter but of width $n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$ in samples, where exact cancellation doubles the effective second-order exponent and the oracle itself is discontinuous in $\lambda$ at fixed $n$.  The window exponent is forced by a two-line balance, the revived first correction $|c|u^{-\beta}$ matching the second correction $u^{-2\beta}$ at the cancellation-oracle threshold, and the conjecture asserts this balance is not just heuristic but the exact boundary of uniform adaptivity.  In tests, the tail-error slope doubled from $-\beta$ to $-2\beta$ at cancellation across two decades of thresholds, and the empirically critical $|c|$ tracked $n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$ with constant ratio $0.500$, the value of $d(\lambda_0)$, across $n=10^3$ to $10^9$.  A counterexample, a selector uniformly optimal across the cusp, would be a genuinely new adaptation mechanism, evading the usual two-point lower-bound construction at its most degenerate point.

\part{Extremal, randomized, and inverse laws for persistent topology}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 20 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The twelve conjectures below concern a single organizing question of topological data analysis: which parts of a persistence computation are laws rather than artifacts, sharp constants instead of worst-case bounds, invertible summaries instead of lossy signatures, and calibrated randomness instead of parameter sensitivity.  They form five programmes.  An extremal-and-sampling programme (Conjectures~\ref{ai1} to~\ref{ai3}) concerns degree-one Vietoris--Rips persistence: a circle isoperimetry asserting that among $n$ points on a Euclidean circle the regular polygon uniquely maximizes the multiplicative persistence ratio, the chordal, every-$n$, ratio-level refinement of the geodesic persistence-set extremality of G\'omez and M\'emoli~\cite{GoM24}; a saturation law asserting that the classical factor two of Vietoris--Rips stability~\cite{CSO14} is asymptotically attained by greedy landmarking of smooth convex curves; and a two-sided Johnson--Lindenstrauss threshold~\cite{JL84,LN17} for the simultaneous preservation of the loop ratios of orthogonal hexagonal channels under Gaussian projection, whose upper half is known in substance~\cite{Lot19,MKG24} and whose lower half would be the first matching bound for a topological statistic.  A statistical programme (Conjectures~\ref{ai4} and~\ref{ai5}) makes the geometry of Wasserstein means of diagrams~\cite{MMH11,TMMH14} quantitative: an optional feature of prevalence $q$ appears in the mean at exactly $q$ times its conditional persistence up to exponentially small matching leakage, sharpening the shrinkage phenomenon visible in the probabilistic Fr\'echet means of~\cite{MTB15} and the grouping calculus of~\cite{CaM24}, and empirical means use the intended latent grouping up to $CNm\,e^{-c\gamma^2/\sigma^2}$.  A Mapper programme (Conjectures~\ref{ai6} and~\ref{ai7}) builds on an exact phase calculus proved here: randomizing the phase of a uniform one-dimensional cover~\cite{CO18} makes the survival probability of an isolated Reeb cycle the universal piecewise-linear function $F_\alpha(\ell/h)$ with an explicit kernel, the phase-averaged Betti curve of a chain of cycles is exactly additive with the spans recoverable from its kinks, and the dithered midpoint estimator of a branch critical value is exactly unbiased with the quantization variance $s^2/12$ of~\cite{Sch64}; the conjectures transfer this calculus to general tame Reeb graphs with a stable inversion, and to discretized and sampled Mapper with mesh-order corrections.  A tomography programme (Conjecture~\ref{ai8}) concerns rectangle-decomposable two-parameter modules~\cite{BL23}, for which the fibered barcode over all lines is a complete invariant~\cite{BLO22}: a proposition proved here sharpens completeness to a single generic direction with the line parameterization retained, the deposited three-direction claim being recorded as calibration, and the conjecture asserts the quantitative sequel, that three fixed generic directions give a locally bi-Lipschitz invariant with polynomially controlled constant and that the direction profile of the matching distance is never needle-like, so uniformly random slopes see near-maximal discrepancy; it is closely related to the local metric equivalence of Vipond~\cite{Vip20}, proved with a universal constant over all lines, and the Lipschitz foliation bounds of~\cite{CDFFL13} behind deterministic approximation schemes~\cite{KN20,BHLMS23}.  A finite-summary programme (Conjectures~\ref{ai9} to~\ref{ai12}) asks how small a complete or faithful summary can be: a restricted-isometry law for random Fourier sketches~\cite{RR07} of the persistence-weighted Gaussian kernel~\cite{KFH16}, bi-Lipschitz to the Wasserstein metric on separated bounded-cardinality classes, which the known non-embeddability theorems~\cite{CB19,BW20} do not forbid because they require collisions or unbounded cardinality, with restricted-class embeddings known in spirit~\cite{MV24}; a Whitney-count law~\cite{Whi44} asserting that $4m+1$ generic evaluations of the Gaussian persistence surface, whose continuum injectivity is known~\cite{CHLP22} while grid images are not injective~\cite{AEK17}, form a complete invariant of $m$-point diagrams; a moment law asserting that the first $4m$ moments of the aggregate landscape~\cite{Bub15} determine a generic $m$-bar diagram, a compressed instance of the finite algebraic coordinate systems of~\cite{ACC16,Kal19}; and an average-case kinetic law asserting that random affine motion of $n$ planar points produces only $O(n^2\log n)$ expected changes of the degree-one persistence pairing, far below the quartic worst-case count that vineyard algorithms~\cite{CEM06,DH21,Hic22,GM26} are built to survive.  The proved layer is three calibrations.  Proposition~\ref{ai:map} proves the exact survival law with kernel $F_\alpha(x)=\min(1,\max(0,(x-1)/(1-\alpha)))$, the exact additivity and kink inversion of the phase-averaged Betti curve for chains of isolated cycles, and the exact dither law for branch critical values.  Proposition~\ref{ai:rect} proves that one generic direction of the parameterized fiber field determines a generic rectangle-decomposable module, by tracking the interval pairs of the fiber barcodes through the parallel family and reading each rectangle off the envelope of its track.  Proposition~\ref{ai:sum} proves the exact closed form of the aggregate-landscape moments and the one-bar case of the moment law, a single bar being determined by its first two moments.  Three negative findings are retained as controls, and they shape the part.  The unrestricted planar version of the extremality claim is refuted: a six-point perturbation search found planar configurations whose multiplicative loop persistence exceeds the regular hexagon's by the factor $1.052$, exact to the arithmetic of the boundary-matrix reduction, so the circle hypothesis of Conjecture~\ref{ai1} is essential and is recorded with the refuting instance; this failure of unrestricted extremality appears to be undocumented.  The deposited three-direction tomography claim is true but not sharp, one direction sufficing by Proposition~\ref{ai:rect}, and is recorded as calibration.  A deposited majority-threshold claim for barycenter features, that an optional feature appears in the mean exactly when its prevalence exceeds one half, is refuted by the flat grouping algebra itself, the mean feature shrinking continuously with prevalence instead, and Conjecture~\ref{ai4} carries the corrected law.  The deposited linear stable-inversion clause of Conjecture~\ref{ai6} is refuted at coalescing spans: the two-cycle span multisets $\{\ell,\ell\}$ and $\{\ell-\delta,\ell+\delta\}$ have bottleneck distance $\delta$, yet on the affine middle branch of the survival kernel the symmetric perturbation cancels, so the phase-averaged Betti curves differ only in $O(\delta)$-wide neighborhoods of the moving kinks and $\lVert S_G-S_{G'}\rVert_{L^2(\dd h/h)}=\Theta(\delta^{3/2})$, whence no bound $\delta\le C\eta$ can hold; the repaired clause requires the span values to be pairwise separated, near-collisions admitting only a H\"older inverse of exponent $2/3$, the constant $\eta/\delta^{3/2}\to6.51$ at $\alpha=0.3$, $\ell=0.5$ found by exact integration.  Conjectures~\ref{ai2} to~\ref{ai5}, \ref{ai6}, \ref{ai7}, and~\ref{ai9} to~\ref{ai12} assert asymptotic or every-instance laws; Conjecture~\ref{ai1} is closely related to~\cite{GoM24}, and Conjecture~\ref{ai8} is closely related to~\cite{Vip20} and~\cite{CDFFL13}.

For a finite metric space $X$, the Vietoris--Rips complex at scale $r$ has as simplices the subsets of diameter at most $r$; homology is over the two-element field, computed here by boundary-matrix reduction of the full two-skeleton, which suffices in degree one.  For a degree-one bar $(b,d)$ with $b>0$ the multiplicative persistence is $d/b$, and $\Pi_1^\times(X)$ is its maximum over bars, set to one if none exists; $d_B$ and $W_2$ are the bottleneck and two-Wasserstein distances with diagonal matching.  For a regular $n$-gon inscribed in the unit circle the dominant degree-one bar has $b_n=2\sin(\pi/n)$ and $d_n=2\sin(\lceil n/3\rceil\pi/n)$~\cite{ACJS18,AdAd17}, so $\Pi_1^\times=\sin(\lceil n/3\rceil\pi/n)/\sin(\pi/n)$, reproduced exactly by the present implementation for $n\le12$.  A uniform one-dimensional Mapper cover has interval length $h$, overlap fraction $\alpha\in(0,1)$, step $s=h(1-\alpha)$, intervals $[ks-U,\,ks-U+h]$, and uniformly random phase $U$ on $[0,s)$; the Mapper graph is the simple nerve of the connected components of the interval preimages, and an isolated cycle of a tame Reeb graph is a pair of arcs joining two branch points whose filter values differ by the span $\ell$ (its degree-one extended-persistence bar length), with all other critical values farther than the cover scale.  A rectangle-decomposable module is a finite direct sum of interval modules supported on axis-parallel rectangles; for a positive-slope direction $v$, the fiber field assigns to each line parallel to $v$, indexed by its transverse intercept $\tau$, the multiset of parameter intervals cut by the rectangles, and endpoints are generic when the finitely many coincidence conditions among side coordinates and crossing values fail.  The Gaussian persistence surface of a diagram $D$ is $\rho_D(z)=\sum_{p\in D}\operatorname{pers}(p)\exp(-\lVert z-p\rVert^2/2\sigma^2)$; the aggregate landscape is $A_D(t)=\sum_i\max\{0,\min(t-b_i,d_i-t)\}$ with moments $M_r(D)=\int t^rA_D(t)\,\dd t$; and for points moving affinely in the plane, a vineyard event is a time at which the multiset of (birth edge, death triangle) pairs of the degree-one reduction changes.

\begin{proposition}[Phase calculus for one-dimensional Mapper]\label{ai:map}
Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and the uniform random phase.  (i) For an isolated cycle of span $\ell$,
\[
\Pr\bigl(\beta_1(M_{h,U})=1\bigr)=F_\alpha(\ell/h),\qquad
F_\alpha(x)=\min\Bigl(1,\max\Bigl(0,\frac{x-1}{1-\alpha}\Bigr)\Bigr),
\]
and $\beta_1=0$ otherwise: the survival probability is a universal piecewise-linear function of $\ell/h$, zero for $h\ge\ell$ and one for $h\le\ell/(2-\alpha)$.  (ii) For a series chain of isolated cycles with spans $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$, the phase-averaged Betti curve satisfies $S(h)=\E_U\,\beta_1(M_{h,U})=\sum_jF_\alpha(\ell_j/h)$ exactly for every $h>0$, and the multiset $\{\ell_j\}$ is recovered from $S$: its kinks in $h$ occur exactly at the points $\ell_j$ and $\ell_j/(2-\alpha)$, and descending induction on the largest kink identifies every span with multiplicity.  (iii) For an isolated branch critical value $c$, the midpoint estimator $\widehat c(U)=L(U)-s/2$, with $L(U)$ the lower endpoint of the first interval whose preimage has the post-branch component count, satisfies $\widehat c-c\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,s]-s/2$, so $\E\widehat c=c$ exactly and $\operatorname{Var}\widehat c=s^2/12$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) If some interval $I$ lies strictly inside the open span $(c,c+\ell)$ between the two branch values, its preimage in the cycle is two arcs, giving two nerve vertices; the neighboring intervals containing the branch values have connected preimages, and the resulting simple nerve contains exactly one cycle through the doubled vertices, while everything else is a tree by isolation, so $\beta_1=1$.  If no interval lies inside the span, every interval meeting it contains a branch value, its preimage is connected through the branch point, all nerve vertices along the feature are single, and the nerve is a path, so $\beta_1=0$; note that when two single vertices overlap inside the span their preimages meet in two arcs but the simple nerve still carries one edge.  The lattice of interval left endpoints has spacing $s$, and an interval lies inside the span exactly when its left endpoint falls in a window of length $(\ell-h)_+$, so the survival probability is $\min(1,(\ell-h)_+/s)=F_\alpha(\ell/h)$.  (ii) The survival criterion is local to each span, the criteria are functions of the same phase, and expectations add; each summand $F_\alpha(\ell_j/h)$ is smooth in $h$ except at $h=\ell_j$ and $h=\ell_j/(2-\alpha)$, where the one-sided slopes differ, and distinct spans contribute kink locations $\ell_j$ that are largest among all kinks of their terms, so the largest kink of $S$ is the largest span, and subtracting its term and iterating recovers the multiset.  (iii) An interval $[lo,lo+h]$ has the post-branch count exactly when $lo>c$, by isolation, so $L$ is the smallest lattice point above $c$; as $U$ runs uniformly through one period, $L-c$ is uniform on $(0,s]$, and $\widehat c-c=(L-c)-s/2$ is centered uniform of width $s$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One direction determines a rectangle module]\label{ai:rect}
Let $M=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathbf k_{R_i}$ be rectangle-decomposable with generic endpoints, and fix any direction $v$ of positive slope.  Then the fiber field of $M$ along $v$, with the line parameterization retained, determines the multiset $\{R_1,\ldots,R_m\}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Along the parallel family, the interval cut by a fixed rectangle has entry and exit endpoints that are piecewise-linear functions of the intercept $\tau$, with two possible slopes according to which side the line enters or leaves, and each rectangle's interval exists on a closed $\tau$-window, entering and leaving with zero length at the corner-touching lines.  Two distinct rectangles cannot cut identical intervals over a $\tau$-interval: equality of entry functions on an interval forces the same active side and the same side coordinate, excluded by generic endpoints; equality of the pairs at a single $\tau$ requires an entry crossing and an exit crossing at the same intercept, one further coincidence excluded by genericity.  Hence the multiset-valued fiber field decomposes into uniquely tracked continuous single-valued branches, one per rectangle, distinct pairs never colliding.  On its window each branch sweeps the entry point along the union of the left and bottom sides, a polyline from the top-left to the bottom-right corner, so the coordinate extremes of the traced entry and exit points recover all four sides of the rectangle, and the multiset is determined.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Moment calibration for aggregate landscapes]\label{ai:sum}
Write bar $i$ as center $c_i=(b_i+d_i)/2$ and half-width $a_i=(d_i-b_i)/2$.  (i) For every $r\ge0$,
\[
M_r(D)=\sum_{i=1}^m\;\sum_{\substack{0\le j\le r\\ j\ \mathrm{even}}}\binom rj c_i^{\,r-j}\,\frac{2a_i^{\,j+2}}{(j+1)(j+2)}.
\]
(ii) For $m=1$, the first two moments determine the bar: $M_0=a^2$ and $M_1=c\,a^2$, so $a=\sqrt{M_0}$ and $c=M_1/M_0$; in particular the first $4m$ moments of Conjecture~\ref{ai11} suffice at $m=1$ with two to spare.  (iii) The second distributional derivative $A_D''=\sum_i(\delta_{b_i}-2\delta_{c_i}+\delta_{d_i})$ is a signed measure with at most $3m$ atoms whose moments obey $\mu_0=\mu_1=0$ and $\mu_k=k(k-1)M_{k-2}$ for $k\ge2$; hence for a diagram with $3m$ distinct nodes the first $6m-2$ aggregate moments $M_0,\ldots,M_{6m-3}$ determine the diagram, by Prony reconstruction of the nodes from $\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_{6m-1}$ and the pairing $b_i+d_i=2c_i$ of endpoints to centers by the weights $+1$ and $-2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The aggregate landscape is the sum of the tent functions $t\mapsto\max\{0,\min(t-b_i,d_i-t)\}=\max\{0,a_i-|t-c_i|\}$.  Substituting $t=c_i+u$,
\[
\int t^r\max\{0,a_i-|u|\}\,\dd t=\sum_{j=0}^r\binom rj c_i^{\,r-j}\int_{-a_i}^{a_i}u^j(a_i-|u|)\,\dd u,
\]
the odd-$j$ integrals vanish by symmetry, and for even $j$ the integral is $2(a_i^{\,j+2}/(j+1)-a_i^{\,j+2}/(j+2))=2a_i^{\,j+2}/((j+1)(j+2))$.  Part (ii) is the case $r\le1$: $M_0=a^2$ and $M_1=c\,a^2$ directly.  (iii) The tent $\max\{0,a_i-|t-c_i|\}$ has second derivative $\delta_{b_i}-2\delta_{c_i}+\delta_{d_i}$, so $A_D''=\sum_i(\delta_{b_i}-2\delta_{c_i}+\delta_{d_i})$; two integrations by parts give $\mu_k=\int t^k\,\dd A_D''=k(k-1)M_{k-2}$ for $k\ge2$, with $\mu_0=\mu_1=0$ by compact support.  A signed measure with $s=3m$ distinct atoms is determined by $2s$ consecutive moments through the Prony--Hankel construction off a proper algebraic set; the known $\mu_0=\mu_1=0$ leave $\mu_2,\ldots,\mu_{6m-1}$, that is $M_0,\ldots,M_{6m-3}$, and the weight $-2$ marks each center against $+1$ at each endpoint, so $b_i+d_i=2c_i$ pairs them uniquely off a further proper algebraic set.
\end{proof}

\section{Extremal and sampling laws for Vietoris--Rips persistence}

\begin{conjecture}[Circle isoperimetry for multiplicative persistence]\label{ai1}
For every $n\ge4$ and every set $X$ of $n$ distinct points on the Euclidean unit circle,
\[
\Pi_1^\times(X)\ \le\ \frac{\sin(\lceil n/3\rceil\pi/n)}{\sin(\pi/n)},
\]
with equality exactly for the regular $n$-gon, up to isometries of the circle.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This conjecture is close to prior work: the extremality of the regular polygon among circle configurations is known in the geodesic metric through the persistence sets of G\'omez and M\'emoli~\cite{GoM24}, who characterize the Vietoris--Rips diagrams of $n$-point subsets of the circle and prove the regular polygon the unique extreme configuration in the principal cases; the present statement is the chordal refinement, every $n$ at once, for the multiplicative ratio rather than additive persistence, over the exact regular-polygon bars of~\cite{ACJS18,AdAd17}.  The circle hypothesis is essential and its necessity is a retained control: in the unrestricted plane, a perturbation search with exact two-skeleton reduction found six-point configurations beating the regular hexagon by the factor $1.052$, so no global planar isoperimetry of this type exists, a failure that appears to be undocumented.  The mechanism is a two-sided balancing: equal spacing minimizes the largest chordal gap, which controls the birth from below, while distributing the third-circle chords that fill the fundamental cycle, which controls the death from above; a proof must handle the combinatorial switching of the death simplex across the chambers of the gap simplex.  In adversarial tests at $n=4$ to $10$, fifteen hundred random circular configurations per $n$ plus local optimization from the best of them and from perturbed regular polygons never exceeded the regular value, the closest competitor reaching $0.9988$ of it, while the formula itself was reproduced to $10^{-15}$ for $n\le12$.  A counterexample would exhibit irregular spacing manufacturing a more persistent loop, and would separate the chordal from the geodesic extremal theory.

\begin{conjecture}[Saturation of the stability factor two]\label{ai2}
Let $\Gamma\subset\R^2$ be a $C^3$ strictly convex closed curve, let $L_m$ be the first $m$ points of a farthest-point sampling of $\Gamma$ from a generic seed, and let $\rho_m=d_H(L_m,\Gamma)$.  Then
\[
\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{d_B\bigl(\mathrm{Dgm}_1(L_m),\mathrm{Dgm}_1(\Gamma)\bigr)}{\rho_m}=2.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Vietoris--Rips stability~\cite{CSO14} bounds the bottleneck error of a landmark diagram by twice the Hausdorff distance, and the conjecture asserts that on the most classical objects, smooth convex loops under the canonical deterministic sampling scheme, the constant two is not slack but attained in the limit: the discrete loop cannot be born before the largest gap chord closes, the largest greedy cell has radius $\rho_m$ and gap chord $2\rho_m+O(\rho_m^3)$, and the continuum loop is born at zero, so the birth discrepancy alone forces the factor, provided the death error stays of lower order, which is the open half.  On the exactly regular inscribed $m$-gon the model computation is elementary, $b_m/\rho_m=2\cos(\pi/2m)\to2$.  No sharpness result for the stability constant under sampling was found; the neighboring literature bounds errors from above.  In tests with exact reduction and greedy samples from three seeds, the ratio on the circle ran $1.990$, $2.014$, $2.032$, $2.000$ at $m=24$ to $128$ against the analytic bar $(0,\sqrt3)$, and on the ellipse with axes $1.3$ and $0.7$ it ran $1.955$ to $2.019$ at $m=16$ to $100$ against a dense reference bar.  A counterexample would be a convex curve where death error cancels birth error, revealing a curvature-dependent constant below two.

\begin{conjecture}[A two-sided projection threshold for loop ratios]\label{ai3}
For $q\ge2$ let $H_1,\ldots,H_q$ be regular hexagons in mutually orthogonal coordinate two-planes of $\R^{2q}$, let $A$ be an $m\times2q$ Gaussian matrix with independent $N(0,1/m)$ entries, and for fixed small $\eps>0$ let $\mathcal E_{q,m,\eps}$ be the event that every channel ratio $\Pi_1^\times(AH_j)/\Pi_1^\times(H_j)$ lies within $\eps$ of one.  Then there are constants $0<c<C$ with
\[
m\le c\,\eps^{-2}\log q\implies\Pr(\mathcal E_{q,m,\eps})\to0,
\qquad
m\ge C\,\eps^{-2}\log q\implies\Pr(\mathcal E_{q,m,\eps})\to1,
\]
as $q\to\infty$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Johnson--Lindenstrauss projection~\cite{JL84} preserves persistence because it preserves all pairwise distances, the principle quantified for distance-function persistence by Sheehy~\cite{She14}, and upper bounds of this type are known~\cite{Lot19,MKG24}; the conjecture asks for the converse scale on a purely topological observable: the restrictions of a Gaussian matrix to the $q$ orthogonal planes are independent blocks, a single channel's ratio distortion has a tail exponential in $m\eps^2$, and the extreme value of $q$ independent channels should cross from failure to success exactly when $qe^{-cm\eps^2}\asymp1$, the same logarithmic law that governs metric distortion and is optimal for it~\cite{LN17}.  The lower half would be the first matching lower bound for a persistence statistic; the concern, recorded here, is that it reduces to metric Johnson--Lindenstrauss optimality because hexagon ratios encode the anisotropy of the projected plane.  In tests at $\eps=0.3$ the empirical critical dimension fit $m^*=5.92\log q+1.00$ across $q=4$ to $256$ with maximum residual $1.4$, and the transition profile at $q=64$ rose from $0.00$ at $m=14$ through $0.45$ at $m=24$ to $0.92$ at $m=44$.  A counterexample would be a threshold at a scale other than $\log q$, showing that loop ratios discard enough metric information to change the dimension law.

\section{The statistical geometry of diagram means}

\begin{conjecture}[Prevalence shrinkage with exponential leakage]\label{ai4}
Let random diagrams consist of a background diagram plus, with probability $q$, one signal point, the signal cluster separated from the background and the diagonal by a matching margin $\gamma$, with conditional perturbations centered subgaussian of scale $\sigma\ll\gamma$.  Then the population $W_2$ Fr\'echet mean has a unique signal point whose diagonal coordinate satisfies $\bar U=\E[U\mid\text{present}]+O(e^{-c\gamma^2/\sigma^2})$ and whose distance to the diagonal satisfies
\[
\bar V=q\,\E[V\mid\text{present}]+O\bigl(e^{-c\gamma^2/\sigma^2}\bigr),
\]
uniformly over bounded separated model classes.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
When an absent diagram matches the candidate mean point to the diagonal, the flat first-order conditions give exactly $\bar V=q\,\E V$, so a rare feature does not vanish from the mean, it shrinks toward the diagonal in proportion to its prevalence; the phenomenon is visible in the probabilistic Fr\'echet means of~\cite{MTB15} and the grouping calculus of~\cite{TMMH14,CaM24}, and a deposited majority-threshold claim, appearance exactly above prevalence one half, is refuted by this algebra and retained as a control.  The conjectural content is global: that the full Fr\'echet problem inherits the flat law with only exponentially small matching leakage, so that the persistence of a barycentric feature is interpretable as conditional strength times prevalence, and prevalence becomes estimable from calibrated mean diagrams.  In tests with a real alternating-minimization mean over five hundred diagrams per prevalence, the ratio of the mean feature's diagonal distance to $q\,\E[V\mid\text{present}]$ was $0.98$ to $1.02$ across $q=0.1$ to $0.9$, and shrinking the margin to three noise scales left the deviation at the finite-sample floor near $0.02$, consistent with leakage remaining below sampling error at every tested margin.  A counterexample would be polynomial-in-margin leakage, which would make mean diagrams systematically misestimate rare features.

\begin{conjecture}[Exponential stability of latent groupings]\label{ai5}
Let $D_1,\ldots,D_N$ be independent diagrams from a latent model with $m$ feature clusters, matching margin $\gamma$ between clusters and to the diagonal, subgaussian scale $\sigma$, and prevalences bounded away from zero.  Then
\[
\Pr\{\text{some optimal mean grouping differs from the latent grouping}\}\le CNm\,e^{-c\gamma^2/\sigma^2},
\]
and on the complementary event the empirical $W_2$ Fr\'echet mean is unique, its coordinates obey the flat projection formulas, and featurewise central-limit behavior holds at rate $N^{-1/2}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The singular geometry of diagram space enters averaging only through combinatorial matching changes, and under a margin every such change requires a noise excursion of scale $\gamma$; a union bound over samples and features then predicts the stated form, and the substance is that all globally optimal Wasserstein assignments respect the latent grouping whenever no local excursion occurs, upgrading the deterministic uniqueness condition of~\cite{CaM24} to a quantitative probabilistic regime in which barycenter statistics are ordinary Euclidean statistics.  No exponential grouping-stability theorem was found.  In tests with two latent features at margin one, the identity-swap frequency of the optimal matching was $0$ at noise scales through $0.25$, then $0.0027$, $0.0103$, $0.0307$ at scales $0.35$, $0.45$, $0.60$, a margin-controlled transition with the observed logarithms decaying faster than $\gamma^2/4\sigma^2$.  A counterexample would be a polynomial failure rate, forcing heavy-tailed corrections to every barycenter confidence statement.

\section{A phase calculus for Mapper}

\begin{conjecture}[Stable survival tomography of Reeb graphs]\label{ai6}
Let $(G,f)$ be a tame Reeb graph whose $r$ degree-one extended-persistence bars have lengths (spans) $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$, each below the separation ($\ell_j<\gamma$), and pairwise critical-value separation at least $\gamma>0$, and let $S_G(h)=\E_U\,\beta_1(M_{h,U})$ be the phase-averaged Betti curve at overlap $\alpha$.  Then (a) $S_G(h)=\sum_jF_\alpha(\ell_j/h)$ for every $h<\gamma$, with the kernel of Proposition~\ref{ai:map}; and (b) the inversion is stable away from the collision stratum: if two tame Reeb graphs with $\gamma$-separated features and distinct span values pairwise separated by at least $\beta>0$ have curves with $\lVert S_G-S_{G'}\rVert_{L^2((0,\gamma),\,\dd h/h)}\le\eta$, then the equal-cardinality span multisets are within bottleneck distance $C(\gamma,\alpha,r,\beta)\,\eta$ of each other; the span separation is essential, coalescing spans admitting only a H\"older inverse of exponent $2/3$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Proposition~\ref{ai:map} makes the phase-averaged calculus exact for chains of isolated cycles: survival is the universal kernel $F_\alpha$, curves add, and kinks invert; the conjecture asserts that the calculus survives on general tame Reeb graphs below the separation scale, where nested and adjacent features can interact through shared branch points, the span multiset being read canonically as the degree-one persistence bar lengths of $(G,f)$, and that the kink inversion is quantitatively stable, turning the notorious cover-position sensitivity of Mapper~\cite{CO18} into an invertible multiscale signature: the randomness of the phase is not noise but a probe, in the spirit of randomized numerical analysis rather than of the sampling randomness studied in~\cite{BBMW21}.  In tests, the empirical survival probability of an isolated cycle matched $F_\alpha$ to three decimals at overlaps $0.30$ and $0.45$ across the full range of $\ell/h$, and the two-cycle curve matched the additive prediction within $0.0055$ across twenty-eight scales spanning both kinks, the curve passing value one exactly at the smaller span.  A counterexample to (a) would be an interaction term surviving separation, to (b) an instability of the kink locations under curve perturbation, either of which would locate a genuine obstruction to randomized Mapper inference.  The span bound $\ell_j<\gamma$ is essential and is retained as a control: a feature whose span exceeds the separation saturates the survival kernel, $F_\alpha(\ell_j/h)=1$, throughout the interaction-free window $h<\gamma$, so its length leaves no trace on $S_G$ there; two graphs with spans $3$ and $4$ at $\gamma=1$ have identical curves on $(0,\gamma)$, and stable inversion requires every kink, at $h=\ell_j$ and $h=\ell_j/(2-\alpha)$, to lie inside the observed window.  A second control is the collision stratum: two equal spans $\{\ell,\ell\}$ and a symmetric split $\{\ell-\delta,\ell+\delta\}$ have curves differing only near their moving kinks, so the $L^2(\dd h/h)$ distance is of order $\delta^{3/2}$ while the span bottleneck is $\delta$; the deposited linear inversion of clause~(b) is thus false without the span-separation hypothesis, and near collisions the inverse modulus is no better than $\delta=O(\eta^{2/3})$.

\begin{conjecture}[The dither law survives discretization]\label{ai7}
For a Reeb graph discretized at filter mesh $\eta=o(h)$, or sampled densely enough that its Mapper is that of the underlying graph, the midpoint estimator of an isolated branch critical value satisfies
\[
\E\widehat c-c=O(\eta),\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat c)=\frac{s^2}{12}+O(s\eta+\eta^2),
\]
uniformly over admissible discretizations, with constants depending only on the local branch geometry.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Proposition~\ref{ai:map}(iii) is the continuum law: random cover translation converts the deterministic quantization bias of Mapper critical values into centered noise of exactly the dithered-quantizer variance $s^2/12$~\cite{Sch64}; the conjecture asserts that nothing worse than mesh-order corrections appears on discretized or sampled objects, so that branch locations come with exact error bars, an elementary but genuinely usable uncertainty quantification that the Mapper literature does not provide.  The content is that the first-split event on a discrete graph tracks the continuum event to one mesh cell, without a topological bias from components fragmenting at the sampling scale.  In tests on a discretized branch graph at mesh $10^{-3}$, the phase-averaged bias was between $-1.7\times10^{-4}$ and $-4\times10^{-5}$ across three cover resolutions, of mesh order as predicted, and the variance ratio to $s^2/12$ was $1.000$ at all three.  A counterexample would be a discretization scheme with an order-$s$ bias, which would identify a topological failure mode of dithering absent from classical quantization.

\section{Rectangle tomography}

\begin{conjecture}[Three-direction stability and random-slope observability]\label{ai8}
Fix a box, a maximum count $m$, and $\delta>0$, and consider rectangle-decomposable modules whose corner coordinates, side lengths, and pairwise separations are at least $\delta$, and whose corners stay at distance at least $\delta$ from the coincidence loci of $v_1,v_2,v_3$, the configurations at which two rectangles cut a common fiber-interval endpoint along some $v_j$.  (a) For generic fixed positive-slope directions $v_1,v_2,v_3$, the invariant $d_3(M,N)=\max_j\sup_{L\parallel v_j}d_B(\mathrm{Dgm}(M_L),\mathrm{Dgm}(N_L))$ is locally bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the minimal corner displacement $d_{\mathrm{rect}}$, with constants polynomial in $m$ and $1/\delta$.  (b) The weighted direction profile $g(\theta)$ of the matching distance between two such modules is Lipschitz relative to its own maximum on compact slope ranges, $\operatorname{Lip}g\le C\lVert g\rVert_\infty$ with $C$ polynomial in $m$, the box size, $1/\delta$, and the slope margin, so its near-maximal set has measure bounded below and $K$ uniformly random slopes recover a $(1-\eps)$-approximation of the matching distance with failure probability exponentially small in $K$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This conjecture is close to prior work on two counts.  Local bi-Lipschitz equivalence between the matching distance, the supremum over all lines, and the interleaving distance is the theorem of Vipond~\cite{Vip20}, with a universal constant; and Lipschitz dependence of the fiber bottleneck on the line is classical in the foliation method~\cite{CDFFL13} and is what deterministic approximation schemes exploit~\cite{KN20,BHLMS23}.  What is asked here is strictly finite-direction and strictly quantitative: three fixed directions replacing the continuum of lines, with an inverse constant that is polynomial rather than combinatorial in the number of rectangles, over the identifiability base of Proposition~\ref{ai:rect}, which sharpens the all-line completeness of~\cite{BLO22} to a single generic direction and records the deposited three-direction claim as calibration, the polynomial conditioning claimed only on the transversality-margin class, since with three fixed directions a module can drift toward a direction-specific endpoint coincidence while keeping its own corners $\delta$-separated; and a width lower bound for the near-maximal set of the profile, which is what makes Monte Carlo approximation of the matching distance trustworthy, complementing the switch-point enumeration of~\cite{BHLMS23}.  In tests on separated three-rectangle modules, the ratio of corner displacement to the three-direction metric stayed below $0.48$ over thirty perturbed pairs, the empirical profile Lipschitz constant stayed below $22$, and the near-maximal fraction of one hundred eighty slopes never fell below $0.017$.  A counterexample to (a) would be a separated family with exponentially degenerating three-direction conditioning; to (b), a needle-like profile, which would doom random-direction estimates on even the simplest module class.

\section{Finite summaries and dynamic complexity}

\begin{conjecture}[A restricted isometry for persistence sketches]\label{ai9}
On the class of diagrams with at most $m$ points, persistence and pairwise separation at least $\delta$, in a box of diameter $R$, let $\Phi_M$ be the random Fourier sketch of the persistence-weighted Gaussian embedding at bandwidth comparable to $\delta^{-1}$ with $M$ frequencies.  Then there are class constants $0<c_0<C_0$, polynomial in $m,R,1/\delta$, such that with probability $1-\eta$,
\[
c_0(1-\eps)\,W_2(D,E)\le\lVert\Phi_M(D)-\Phi_M(E)\rVert_2\le C_0(1+\eps)\,W_2(D,E)
\]
for all $D,E$ in the class, provided $M\ge C\eps^{-2}m\log(mR/(\delta\eta))$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Diagrams famously do not embed: bounded-cardinality classes admit no bi-Lipschitz map to finite-dimensional Hilbert space in general~\cite{CB19}, and the full space embeds in no Hilbert space at all~\cite{BW20}; the conjecture threads the needle those theorems leave open, because their obstructions require collisions or vanishing separation, which the class excludes, and restricted-class embeddings with controlled distortion are known in spirit~\cite{MV24}.  The proposal is concrete: the kernel mean embedding of the persistence-weighted Gaussian kernel~\cite{KFH16} should be bi-Lipschitz to transport on the separated class, and random Fourier features~\cite{RR07} should preserve that comparison at dimension nearly linear in the diagram cardinality, giving a streaming-compatible, provably Wasserstein-faithful vectorization.  The polynomial dependence of the lower constant is the exposed clause: inverting Gaussian mixtures from kernel embeddings can be exponentially ill-conditioned in the number of components, and separation excludes collisions without yet excluding that decay.  In tests, the ratio of kernel distance to $W_2$ over eight hundred separated four-point pairs stayed within the two-sided band $[0.90,2.75]$, and the sketch-to-kernel relative deviation halved with each fourfold increase in frequencies, from $0.10$ at $M=16$ to $0.0087$ at $M=1024$, the parametric rate the concentration half requires.  A counterexample would be a separated family collapsing the lower constant, which would locate a genuinely non-Euclidean direction inside the separated class.

\begin{conjecture}[Whitney-count evaluations of persistence surfaces]\label{ai10}
Fix $\sigma>0$ and the class of diagrams with exactly $m$ points, pairwise $\delta$-separated and $\delta$-far from the diagonal, in a compact box.  Choose $q\ge4m+1$ evaluation points independently from any distribution with positive density on a neighborhood of the box.  Then, almost surely in the evaluations, the map $D\mapsto(\rho_D(z_1),\ldots,\rho_D(z_q))$ is injective on the class, and locally bi-Lipschitz off the discriminant.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The continuum Gaussian surface is injective~\cite{CHLP22}, while gridded persistence images are not~\cite{AEK17}; the conjecture asserts that the dimension-theoretically minimal number of generic point evaluations, the Whitney embedding count $4m+1$ for the $2m$-dimensional diagram manifold~\cite{Whi44}, already suffices, so that a complete summary needs no grid and no continuum, only $4m+1$ numbers.  The mechanism is transversality of the real-analytic evaluation family, adjacent to the moment identifiability of Gaussian mixtures, with the persistence weights breaking the symmetries that make mixture recovery delicate.  In tests at $m=3$, $q=13$, sixty adversarial searches for well-separated pairs with equal evaluations never drove the evaluation gap below $2.0\times10^{-2}$, and local Jacobians had full rank throughout the search paths.  A counterexample would be a collision pair at the Whitney count, pushing the truth toward the information-theoretic worst case and revealing hidden algebraic relations among Gaussian surface evaluations.

\begin{conjecture}[Aggregate-landscape moment determinacy]\label{ai11}
For a Zariski-open, full-measure set of $m$-bar diagrams, the first $4m$ moments $M_0,\ldots,M_{4m-1}$ of the aggregate landscape determine the diagram uniquely up to bar permutation.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The full landscape is invertible~\cite{Bub15}, and finite complete coordinate systems for barcodes exist~\cite{ACC16,Kal19}; the compression claimed here is that $4m$ scalar integrals of one aggregated function suffice, through the exact closed form of Proposition~\ref{ai:sum}, a constrained Prony problem in which each bar contributes a rigid two-parameter moment stream rather than a free point mass.  The one-bar case is proved, two moments sufficing, and no claim of numerical robustness is made, the smallest singular values of the moment map decaying rapidly; a deposited claim that the first $2m$ moments form a robust coordinate system was withdrawn on conditioning grounds by the source analysis and is retained here only as the observation that multistart inversion of the first $2m$ exact moments already returned a unique reconstruction on every tested instance at $m=2,3$, so the $4m$ threshold is conservative and possibly not sharp; the generic determinacy from $6m-2$ aggregate moments is unconditional, Proposition~\ref{ai:sum}(iii), and the conjectured $4m$ is the compression below that Prony benchmark.  In tests, exact-moment multistart inversion at $m=2$ and $m=3$ found exactly one solution at $2m$, $3m$, and $4m$ moments across one hundred fifty starts each.  A counterexample would be a moment symmetry among tent functions, a hidden relation that would be interesting in itself; a proof would give the smallest known complete statistic for generic barcodes.

\begin{conjecture}[Near-quadratic vineyard complexity in the mean]\label{ai12}
Let $n$ planar points move affinely, $x_i(t)=a_i+tv_i$ on $[0,1]$, with $a_i,v_i$ independent standard Gaussians, and let $N_1(n)$ be the number of times the degree-one Vietoris--Rips persistence pairing changes.  Then $\E N_1(n)=O(n^2\log n)$, and $N_1(n)=O(n^2\log^2n)$ with probability $1-n^{-c}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
There are quadratically many edge lengths and quartically many candidate order swaps, and vineyard-type algorithms~\cite{CEM06,DH21,Hic22,GM26} are engineered to process whatever event sequence arrives; the conjecture asserts that on random affine motion almost all swaps are topologically silent, the pairing changing only near kinetically critical local configurations, so the true event count is governed by the sparse geometry of the moving point set rather than by the full distance arrangement, the first average-case law for dynamic persistence.  In exact tests with adaptive time refinement at $n=6$ to $14$, the mean event count grew with log-log exponent $2.36$, matching the local slope $2.45$ of $n^2\log n$ over the same range and far below the quartic candidate count, with absolute counts twenty to thirty times smaller than $n^4/100$.  A superquadratic counterexample would show topological pairings are kinetically volatile in a way static sparsity cannot see, itself a finding with algorithmic consequences.

\part{Temporal irreversibility and spectral selection in nonequilibrium dynamics}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The fifteen conjectures below study how much of the thermodynamic arrow of time survives when a stationary nonequilibrium process is observed only through two time points.  For an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain the complete trajectory over an interval of length $t$ carries a path-space entropy production $\sigma t$; reducing the trajectory to its endpoints keeps only the \emph{lag irreversibility} $L(t)$, the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the stationary two-time law and its time reverse, and data processing gives $0\le L(t)\le\sigma t$.  The organizing object is the \emph{temporal sampling efficiency} $\eta(t)=L(t)/(\sigma t)\in[0,1]$, the fraction of dissipation still visible at lag $t$.  The conjectures form three programmes.  A temporal-and-spectral programme (Conjectures~\ref{aj1} to~\ref{aj7}) asserts monotone loss of efficiency, spectral bounds on the temporal support and the integrated budget of the arrow of time, an irreversibility-specific relaxation exponent that doubles the slowest dissipative mode, its generic coincidence with the ordinary spectral gap together with an exceptional invisible-slow-mode phenomenon, and the discrete mode selection performed by deterministic coarse-graining.  A unicyclic-and-winding programme (Conjectures~\ref{aj8} to~\ref{aj12}) sharpens these on a single driven cycle, where endpoint sampling loses exactly the integer winding number, giving a strict efficiency law, an amplitude cap, a weak-affinity wrapped-Brownian scaling limit, a ballistic winding-aliasing horizon, and a single P\'eclet crossover unifying the two.  A Gaussian programme (Conjectures~\ref{aj13} to~\ref{aj15}) transfers the peak-horizon, integrated-budget, and mode-doubling laws to multivariate Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes, where every quantity is an explicit function of the drift and diffusion matrices.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{aj:basic}: the endpoint data-processing bounds, the short-time expansion $L(t)=\sigma t+O(t^2)$ giving $\eta(t)\to1$, and the exact Gaussian lag-KL formula.  Conjectures~\ref{aj4}, \ref{aj6}, \ref{aj7}, and~\ref{aj15} assert long-time exponential laws; Conjectures~\ref{aj10} to~\ref{aj12} are scaling-limit statements; Conjecture~\ref{aj5} is a genericity statement carrying its own exceptional set.  The central observable is the lag irreversibility of Merino Negrete, Maldonado, and Salgado-Garc\'ia~\cite{MMS23}, and the closest spectral precedent is the finite-time cross-correlation asymmetry of Van Vu, Vo, and Saito~\cite{VVS24}; the normalization by path entropy production, the temporal horizons and integrated budgets, the doubled irreversibility exponent and its coarse-grained selection, and the winding scaling laws are what is proposed as new.  Since deposit, Conjectures~\ref{aj4}, \ref{aj6}, and~\ref{aj15}, the discrete and Gaussian irreversibility-doubling and coarse-grained mode-selection laws, have been resolved true by Propositions~\ref{aj:doubling} and~\ref{aj:oudoubling} from the quadratic equivalence of lag KL with the antisymmetric endpoint flux, and Conjecture~\ref{aj10}, the wrapped-Brownian limit, by Proposition~\ref{aj:wrapped}.  Since deposit, Conjectures~\ref{aj1} and~\ref{aj8}, the efficiency-monotonicity and unicyclic strict-monotonicity laws, have been resolved false by Proposition~\ref{aj:c1}: a homogeneous ten-state ring has non-monotone efficiency, rising by more than two orders of magnitude across an interior lag interval through winding aliasing, so the winding effect of Conjectures~\ref{aj11} and~\ref{aj12} produces a resonant revival rather than the proposed monotone loss.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{aj7}, the hidden-mode exponential-separation law, has been resolved false by Proposition~\ref{aj:c7}: a product of two driven three-cycles has an oscillatory dominant mode with exact zeros, so the coarse-to-full ratio returns to one at infinitely many times and the liminf separation exponent is zero rather than the exponent gap.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{aj12}, the universal diffusive-to-ballistic P\'eclet crossover, has been resolved false as stated by Proposition~\ref{aj:c12}: the ballistic first-crossing coefficient depends on the edge affinity, so no single P\'eclet function recovers the ballistic law of Conjecture~\ref{aj11} for every fixed affinity, though a one-variable crossover survives in the weak-edge-bias regime.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{aj9}, the sharp unicyclic amplitude cap $\sup_t\gamma L(t)/\sigma\le\tfrac12$, has been resolved false by Proposition~\ref{aj:c9}: an explicit near-decomposable seven-state ring reaches $0.643>\tfrac12$, so the constant $\tfrac12$ is not universal.  Since deposit, Conjectures~\ref{aj13} and~\ref{aj14}, the Gaussian peak-horizon $g_At_*\le1$ and spectral-area $\int L_{\mathrm{OU}}\le\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}/g_A^2$ bounds, have likewise been resolved false by Proposition~\ref{aj:c1314}: a five-dimensional Jordan-block Ornstein--Uhlenbeck drift with $g_A=1$ has its lag-KL peak at $t_*\approx1.069$ and normalized area $\approx1.266$, so the spectral abscissa alone cannot bound the temporal horizon or the integrated budget of a strongly nonnormal drift, and a repaired bound needs a nonnormality constant.

Let $X_t$ be an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with row generator $Q=(q_{ij})$, stationary law $\pi>0$, and bidirected support ($q_{ij}>0\Leftrightarrow q_{ji}>0$), so the steady-state entropy production is finite.  Write $P_t=e^{tQ}$, the stationary endpoint law $F_t(i,j)=\pi_iP_t(i,j)$, its time reverse $F_t^\top$, the lag irreversibility
\[
L(t)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(F_t\Vert F_t^\top)=\sum_{i,j}F_t(i,j)\log\frac{F_t(i,j)}{F_t(j,i)},
\]
and the entropy-production rate $\sigma=\sum_{i\neq j}\pi_iq_{ij}\log(\pi_iq_{ij}/\pi_jq_{ji})$, so that $\eta(t)=L(t)/(\sigma t)$.  Let $q^*_{ij}=\pi_jq_{ji}/\pi_i$ be the reversed generator, $\bar Q=(Q+Q^*)/2$ the additive reversibilization, $\gamma=\lambda_2(-\bar Q)>0$ its reversible $L^2(\pi)$ spectral gap, and $g=\min\{-\Re\lambda:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(Q)\setminus\{0\}\}$ the ordinary spectral-abscissa gap.  Write $A_t=F_t-F_t^\top=\Pi e^{tQ}-e^{tQ^\top}\Pi$ with $\Pi=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)$, and let $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$ be the smallest $-\Re\lambda>0$ over generator eigenmodes whose coefficient in $A_t$ is nonzero (on generalized eigenspaces for Jordan blocks, the polynomial factors not affecting the rate).  For a deterministic map $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $F_t^f(a,b)=\sum_{f(i)=a,\,f(j)=b}F_t(i,j)$, $L_f(t)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(F_t^f\Vert(F_t^f)^\top)$, and $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)$ the smallest such rate surviving the block summation.  For the homogeneous $N$-cycle with clockwise/counterclockwise rates $p_N=e^{A/(2N)}$, $q_N=e^{-A/(2N)}$ and time $t_N=N^2\tau/(p_N+q_N)$, the wrapped Gaussian on $x\in[0,1)$ is $w_{A,\tau}(x)=\sum_{k\in\Z}(2\pi\tau)^{-1/2}\exp[-(x+k-A\tau/2)^2/(2\tau)]$, with reverse $w_{-A,\tau}$; at fixed edge affinity $a\neq0$ write $p=e^{a/2}$, $q=e^{-a/2}$, $v=p-q$, the P\'eclet number $\mathrm{Pe}=N(p-q)/(p+q)$, and $t_c(N,\cdot)=\inf\{t:\eta_N(t)\le c\}$.  For the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process $dX_t=AX_t\,dt+\sqrt{2D}\,dW_t$ with $A$ Hurwitz and $D\succ0$, the stationary covariance solves $AC+CA^\top+2D=0$, the two-time law is Gaussian with cross-covariance $Ce^{A^\top t}$, $L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)$ is the KL divergence to its block-swapped reverse, $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}=\operatorname{tr}[(A+DC^{-1})^\top D^{-1}(A+DC^{-1})C]$, $g_A=\min_\lambda(-\Re\lambda(A))$, $H(t)=e^{At}C-Ce^{A^\top t}$, and $\alpha_H$ the slowest exponential rate in $H(t)$.

\begin{proposition}[Endpoint bounds, short-time efficiency, and the Gaussian lag KL]\label{aj:basic}
For every chain in the stated class, $0\le L(t)\le\sigma t$, and as $t\downarrow0$ single-jump paths dominate, giving $L(t)=\sigma t+O(t^2)$ and $\eta(t)\to1$; as $t\to\infty$, $F_t\to\pi\otimes\pi$ and $L(t)\to0$.  For the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process the two-time covariance and its block swap have equal determinants, so
\[
L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)=\tfrac12\bigl[\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_t^{R\,-1}\Sigma_t)-2d\bigr].
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint map is a measurable function of the path, so data processing for KL gives $L(t)\le D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ of the path law to its reverse $=\sigma t$, and $L(t)\ge0$; positivity of $\sigma$ makes the interval nondegenerate.  For small $t$, $P_t=I+tQ+O(t^2)$, and the off-diagonal contribution to $\sum F_t\log(F_t/F_t^\top)$ is $t\sum_{i\neq j}\pi_iq_{ij}\log(\pi_iq_{ij}/\pi_jq_{ji})+O(t^2)=\sigma t+O(t^2)$, the diagonal terms cancelling to first order, whence $\eta(t)\to1$; irreducibility gives $P_t\to\mathbf 1\pi^\top$ and $F_t\to\pi\otimes\pi$, a symmetric limit, so $L(t)\to0$.  For the Gaussian case both covariances are $2d\times2d$ block matrices differing by a swap of the two time blocks, a similarity by the block permutation, so $\det\Sigma_t^R=\det\Sigma_t$ and the log-determinant term of the Gaussian KL vanishes, leaving the displayed trace formula.
\end{proof}

\section{Temporal irreversibility and spectral selection}

\begin{conjecture}[Temporal sampling-efficiency monotonicity, resolved false]\label{aj1}
For every finite irreducible bidirected chain with $\sigma>0$, the efficiency $\eta(t)=L(t)/(\sigma t)$ is non-increasing on $(0,\infty)$, and strictly decreasing for a generic nonequilibrium chain.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Data processing gives only $\eta\le1$; the conjecture asserts the far stronger statement that lengthening the observation lag can never raise the \emph{fraction} of path irreversibility retained by two endpoints, so every coarsening of the observation clock loses thermodynamic information per unit elapsed time.  The comparison is between different endpoint maps, so no single contraction theorem applies; a proof route compares a length-$t$ path to a random subdivision into blocks and seeks a conditional-relative-entropy inequality for the endpoint statistic, while a counterexample would exhibit a resonant lag at which more dissipation becomes visible.  The nearest related result is the lag-irreversibility observable of~\cite{MMS23}.  A first decisive theorem would be monotonicity for three-state chains.  A counterexample would be a chain and two lags with $\eta$ strictly rising.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false: on the homogeneous $10$-cycle with edge affinity $1$, $\eta$ falls to $9.3\times10^{-6}$ at $vt/N\approx0.54$ and then rises by a factor above $130$ to $1.2\times10^{-3}$ at $vt/N\approx0.68$ before mixing erases it, verified at eighty digits (Proposition~\ref{aj:c1}).  The mechanism is the resonant lag the significance anticipates: near half a winding the forward and reverse wrapped endpoint laws nearly coincide and then separate again before diffusion mixes the cycle, so the winding effect of Conjectures~\ref{aj11} and~\ref{aj12} produces a revival of efficiency rather than monotone loss.

\begin{conjecture}[Two-gap-time location bound]\label{aj2}
If $t_*$ is any global maximizer of $L(t)$, then $\gamma t_*\le2$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Since $L$ rises linearly from zero and returns to zero, it has a maximizer; the reversible part of the dynamics erases endpoint memory while the antisymmetric part supplies irreversibility, making the dimensionless product $\gamma t_*$ a natural temporal horizon for the visible arrow of time.  A proof may combine a reversible $L^2(\pi)$ contraction for $P_t$ with a comparison between $L$ and an antisymmetric $\chi^2$ divergence, the obstacle being that KL can be sensitive to rare states, so a successful argument must avoid $\pi_{\min}^{-1}$ prefactors.  The nearest related results are the entropy-production spectral bounds of~\cite{KOI24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the bound for birth--death chains with one added shortcut.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the maximum $\gamma t_*$ over sizes three to nine was $0.775$, far inside the bound.  A counterexample with $\gamma t_*\gg1$ would isolate arrow-of-time information latent long after reversible mixing.

\begin{conjecture}[Spectral integrated-budget bound]\label{aj3}
For every chain in the class, $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty L(t)\,dt\le\frac{2\sigma}{\gamma^2}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The integral has the units of $\sigma/\gamma^2$, the unique scale built from the entropy-production rate and the reversible gap, so the conjecture caps the total area under all two-endpoint irreversibility measurements once the mixing timescale is fixed.  Monotonicity alone does not imply it, since a monotone function can decay arbitrarily slowly, so genuine spectral input is required; a proof route bounds $L$ by a weighted $\chi^2$ norm of $A_t$ and applies additive-reversibilization Dirichlet-form estimates.  The nearest related results are~\cite{VVS24,KOI24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the bound restricted to reversibilizations with a spectral gap of multiplicity one.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the maximum normalized area $\gamma^2\!\int L\,dt/\sigma$ was $0.527$.  A counterexample would be a chain whose efficiency curve decays slowly enough to exceed the budget.

\begin{conjecture}[Irreversibility-gap doubling law, resolved true]\label{aj4}
The long-time envelope of lag KL decays at twice the slowest irreversible rate:
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\frac1{2t}\log L(t)=\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}},
\]
and generically $L(t)=t^{m}e^{-2\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}[c(t)+o(1)]$ with $m\ge0$ a Jordan multiplicity and $c$ bounded, nonnegative, and not identically zero.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
At long times $F_t=\pi\otimes\pi+\delta F_t$ and KL is locally quadratic in the antisymmetric perturbation $A_t$, so a leading amplitude $e^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}$ in $A_t$ doubles to $e^{-2\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}$ in $L$; the conjectural content is the clean modal characterization under degeneracy, complex modes, and cancellations.  A proof route uses the Jordan--Chevalley expansion of $e^{tQ}$ and a second-order KL expansion around $\pi\otimes\pi$.  The nearest related result is the spectral-gap-controlled correlation-asymmetry decay of~\cite{VVS24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the diagonalizable case with a simple slowest irreversible mode.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, fitting the KL tail and the antisymmetric-flux tail gave a ratio of exponents with median $1.0000$ over the tested chains.  A counterexample would be a chain whose lag KL decays at a rate other than twice an antisymmetric-flux rate.  \emph{Resolution.} Now proved, Proposition~\ref{aj:doubling}: the exponent identity holds unconditionally, and the refined law holds with power $m=2r$, twice the Jordan-polynomial degree, rather than a single multiplicity, without genericity.
