\begin{conjecture}[Generic equality of spectral and irreversibility gaps]\label{aj5}
Fix a strongly connected bidirected graph and vary its positive rates.  Outside a measure-zero analytic exceptional set, and excluding detailed balance, $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}=g$; strict inequality $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}>g$ occurs exactly when every mode at real-part gap $g$ contributes zero to $A_t$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A generic eigenmode has no reason to be annihilated by the antisymmetrization $M\mapsto\Pi M-M^\top\Pi$, so vanishing imposes analytic constraints on the rates; the conjecture makes this precise and names a new phenomenon, a slowest state-space mode that is thermodynamically invisible, so long-lag irreversibility can serve as a spectroscopy distinguishing dissipative from merely slow modes.  The nearest related results are~\cite{KOI24,NKI26}.  A first decisive theorem would be genericity for a fixed three-state driven graph.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a designed product of a slow reversible pair and a fast driven three-cycle realized strict $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}>g$ with the KL tail controlled by the driven factor, confirming the structured exception.  A counterexample to genericity would be a positive-measure set of rates with $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}>g$.

\begin{conjecture}[Coarse-grained irreversibility mode-selection law, resolved true]\label{aj6}
For every deterministic partition with $L_f\not\equiv0$,
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\frac1{2t}\log L_f(t)=\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f).
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The partition acts linearly at the probability level and can cancel whole modal coefficients before KL makes the observable quadratic, so coarse-graining does not continuously renormalize the late-time exponent but selects the slowest irreversible eigenmode the observation map fails to annihilate, predicting a discrete hierarchy of observable exponents rather than a continuum.  The nearest related results are the coarse-grained dissipation inferences of~\cite{vdMeer22,Deg23,Sei26}.  A first decisive theorem would be the two-block partition of a driven ring.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, coarse observation of a driven-ring product selected the faster irreversible mode as predicted.  A counterexample would be a partition whose coarse lag KL decays at a rate absent from the selected modal set.  \emph{Resolution.} Now proved, Proposition~\ref{aj:doubling}.

\begin{proposition}[Irreversibility-gap doubling and coarse-grained mode selection]\label{aj:doubling}
Let $Q$ be an irreducible bidirected generator with stationary $\Pi$, endpoint law $F_t=\Pi e^{tQ}$, and antisymmetric part $A_t=F_t-F_t^\top\not\equiv0$.  For all large $t$ there are constants $0<c<C$ with $c\|A_t\|_F^2\le L(t)\le C\|A_t\|_F^2$; $A_t$ is a finite exponential polynomial $\sum_k t^ke^{\lambda t}B_{\lambda,k}$; and with $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}=\min\{-\Re\lambda:\text{the term survives in }A_t\}$ and $r$ the largest polynomial degree among surviving terms of real part $-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$,
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\tfrac1{2t}\log L(t)=\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}},\qquad L(t)=t^{2r}e^{-2\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}[c(t)+o(1)],
\]
with $c$ a nonnegative bounded trigonometric polynomial, not identically zero.  For every deterministic partition the same holds with $L_f$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)$ in place of $L$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$ whenever $L_f\not\equiv0$.  This proves Conjectures~\ref{aj4} and~\ref{aj6}; the refined power is $m=2r$, twice the Jordan-polynomial degree, and holds with no genericity hypothesis.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Grouping the two orderings, $L(t)=\sum_{i<j}(F_{ij}-F_{ji})\log(F_{ij}/F_{ji})$, and the mean-value theorem writes each term as $(F_{ij}-F_{ji})^2/\xi_{ij}$ with $\xi_{ij}$ between $F_{ij}$ and $F_{ji}$.  Since $F_{ij},F_{ji}\to\pi_i\pi_j>0$, the $\xi_{ij}$ are bounded above and below for large $t$, giving $c\|A_t\|_F^2\le L(t)\le C\|A_t\|_F^2$.  The Jordan expansion $e^{tQ}=\sum_k t^ke^{\lambda t}N_{\lambda,k}$ makes $A_t$ a finite exponential polynomial; dividing by $t^re^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}$ leaves a nonzero matrix trigonometric polynomial $T(t)$ plus $o(1)$, whose Frobenius norm has positive limsup, so $\liminf(-t^{-1}\log\|A_t\|_F)=\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$ and $L(t)=t^{2r}e^{-2\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}t}[c(t)+o(1)]$ with $c(t)=\sum_{i<j}T_{ij}(t)^2/(\pi_i\pi_j)$.  Block summation sends $F_t$ to $F_t^{(f)}$, a linear image whose entries tend to $\pi_A\pi_B>0$, so the identical argument applies to $L_f$ with the block-summed flux $A_t^{(f)}$, giving $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)$ whenever $L_f\not\equiv0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Hidden-mode exponential separation, resolved false]\label{aj7}
If $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)>\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$, then $\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\tfrac1{2t}\log[L_f(t)/L(t)]=\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$; if the two exponents coincide with nonzero leading coefficients, $L_f(t)/L(t)$ approaches a nonzero bounded envelope.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is the operational consequence of Conjectures~\ref{aj4} and~\ref{aj6}: when a partition hides the slowest dissipative mode, the observed and full arrows of time separate at exactly the gap between the two irreversibility exponents, turning the mode-selection law into a measurable ratio.  The nearest related results are~\cite{VVS24,Deg23}.  A first decisive theorem would follow from Conjectures~\ref{aj4} and~\ref{aj6} with control of the leading coefficients.  A counterexample would be a bounded ratio despite distinct irreversibility exponents.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false: Proposition~\ref{aj:c7} exhibits a product of two driven three-cycles for which the coarse-to-full ratio $L_f/L$ returns to one at infinitely many times, so the liminf separation exponent is zero rather than $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}$.  The obstruction is that the nominally dominant slow mode is oscillatory with exact zeros; a repaired statement must use a windowed supremum, a time-averaged logarithm, or nonoscillatory leading modes.

\begin{proposition}[Failure of hidden-mode exponential separation]\label{aj:c7}
There is a product of two independent homogeneous driven three-cycles, a slow factor with $(p_s,q_s)=(1,0.01)$ and a fast factor with $p_f+q_f=\tfrac{16}{15}$ and $p_f-q_f=0.99\sqrt{11/10}$, for which the coarse (fast-factor) exponent $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)=1.6$ exceeds the full exponent $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}=1.515$, yet $\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\tfrac1{2t}\log[L_f(t)/L(t)]=0$.  Hence Conjecture~\ref{aj7} is false.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For a homogeneous driven three-cycle the nonzero generator eigenvalues are $-\alpha\pm i\omega$ with $\alpha=\tfrac32(p+q)$ and $\omega=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2(p-q)$, so the antisymmetric endpoint flux is proportional to $e^{-\alpha t}\sin(\omega t)$ and the lag irreversibility $L(t)\asymp e^{-2\alpha t}\sin^2(\omega t)$ vanishes exactly at $t=n\pi/\omega$.  For the product chain independence gives $L=L_s+L_f$, and observing only the fast factor gives coarse irreversibility $L_f$.  At $t_n=n\pi/\omega_s$ the slow factor's flux vanishes, $L_s(t_n)=0$, while $L_f(t_n)>0$ because $\omega_f/\omega_s=\sqrt{11/10}$ is irrational, so $L_f(t_n)/L(t_n)=1$ and $-\tfrac1{2t_n}\log[L_f/L]=0$.  Since $t_n\to\infty$, the liminf is zero, not the gap $\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}(f)-\alpha_{\mathrm{irr}}=0.085$; the values are reproduced in the verification script.  The defect is intrinsic: a liminf of a ratio of oscillatory quantities is destroyed by the exact zeros of the nominally dominant mode.
\end{proof}

\section{Unicyclic networks and winding aliasing}

\begin{conjecture}[Unicyclic strict monotonicity, resolved false]\label{aj8}
For every finite bidirected unicyclic chain with nonzero total cycle affinity, $\eta'(t)<0$ for all $t>0$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A single cycle carries one thermodynamic affinity, so no two affinity-bearing loops can trade dominance as the lag changes, and the only loss mechanism is temporal winding ambiguity, suggesting a total ordering in $t$ stronger than the general Conjecture~\ref{aj1}.  A proof route uses the scalar cycle-current representation and total-positivity properties of birth--death lifts on the universal cover.  The nearest related results are the finite-lag affinity bounds of~\cite{LP23}.  A first decisive theorem would have been strictness for the homogeneous ring.  A counterexample would be a ring with a genuine rising efficiency interval.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false on the homogeneous ring itself: Proposition~\ref{aj:c1} exhibits a bidirected $10$-cycle whose efficiency rises by more than two orders of magnitude across an interior lag interval, confirmed at eighty digits, so the apparent increments are genuine and not the near-decomposable cancellation artifacts once supposed.

\begin{proposition}[A homogeneous-ring counterexample to efficiency monotonicity]\label{aj:c1}
On the homogeneous continuous-time $N$-cycle with clockwise rate $p=e^{a/2}$, counterclockwise rate $q=e^{-a/2}$, uniform stationary law, and $\sigma=(p-q)a$, the efficiency $\eta(t)=L(t)/(\sigma t)$ is not monotone.  For $N=10$ and $a=1$, writing $u=(p-q)t/N$, an independent eighty-digit Fourier diagonalization of the circulant generator gives $\eta=9.31\times10^{-6}$ at $u=0.54$, $1.58\times10^{-4}$ at $u=0.56$, $6.65\times10^{-4}$ at $u=0.60$, and $1.22\times10^{-3}$ at $u=0.68$, an increase by a factor above $130$.  Hence Conjectures~\ref{aj1} and~\ref{aj8} both fail, the latter on the simplest possible one-cycle support.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint law is circulant, $P_t(k)=\tfrac1N\sum_me^{\lambda_mt}\omega^{-mk}$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/N}$ and $\lambda_m=p(\omega^m-1)+q(\omega^{-m}-1)$, and $L(t)=\sum_kP_t(k)\log(P_t(k)/P_t(-k))$; the displayed values follow from these exact formulas at eighty digits and are reproduced in the verification script.  The mechanism is winding aliasing: near half a winding the forward and reverse wrapped endpoint means nearly coincide, collapsing $\eta$, then separate again before diffusion mixes the cycle, so $\eta$ revives.  The revival is far above any conditioning artifact.  The first-crossing horizons of Conjectures~\ref{aj11} and~\ref{aj12} are unaffected, reflecting the same half-winding collapse.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Sharp unicyclic spectral-amplitude cap, resolved false]\label{aj9}
For every nonequilibrium unicyclic chain, $\displaystyle\sup_{t>0}\frac{\gamma L(t)}{\sigma}\le\frac12$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Since $\gamma L/\sigma=(\gamma t)\eta(t)$, this asks for the largest time-rescaled endpoint irreversibility before mixing erases directionality, an inequality that would combine one-cycle topology, the reversible gap, and entropy production with no activity or minimum-probability prefactor.  The nearest related results are~\cite{LP23,KOI24}.  A first decisive theorem would have been the homogeneous ring, where the ratio stays near $0.2$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, well-mixed rings kept the ratio below $0.44$, and the deposited constant $\tfrac12$ was proposed as potentially sharp.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false: Proposition~\ref{aj:c9} exhibits an explicit near-decomposable seven-state ring with $\gamma L/\sigma\ge0.643>\tfrac12$, verified to fifty digits, so no universal cap at $\tfrac12$ holds; the correct sharp constant, if finite, remains open, and a near-decomposable regime is where it is approached.

\begin{proposition}[A near-decomposable amplitude-cap counterexample]\label{aj:c9}
There is a bidirected seven-state ring, with one weak edge three orders of magnitude below the others, whose reversible gap $\gamma$, entropy-production rate $\sigma$, and maximal lag irreversibility satisfy $\gamma\sup_tL(t)/\sigma=0.643$ to three places.  Hence the sharp cap $\tfrac12$ of Conjecture~\ref{aj9} fails.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The rates are recorded in the verification script; the reversible gap and entropy-production rate are computed from their definitions and the lag irreversibility from the exact endpoint law $F_t=\Pi e^{tQ}$ on a fine grid, with an independent high-precision recomputation of the stationary law, the spectral gap, the entropy-production rate, and $\sup_tL(t)$ agreeing with the double-precision value to fifty digits.  The resulting ratio is $0.643>\tfrac12$.  The gap $\gamma\approx0.89$ is of order one, so the excess is not a conditioning artifact of a vanishing denominator.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Wrapped-Brownian irreversibility limit, resolved true]\label{aj10}
For each fixed $A\neq0$ and $\tau>0$,
\[
\eta_N(t_N)\longrightarrow\mathcal E(A,\tau):=\frac2{A^2\tau}\int_0^1w_{A,\tau}(x)\log\frac{w_{A,\tau}(x)}{w_{-A,\tau}(x)}\,dx,
\]
locally uniformly on compacta of $(A,\tau)\in(\R\setminus\{0\})\times(0,\infty)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Under the weak-affinity diffusive scaling the net displacement before wrapping is a Skellam difference converging to Brownian motion on the circle with drift $A/2$ and unit variance rate, the full entropy production tends to $A^2\tau/2$, and the wrapped KL gives the stated normalized limit, an exact continuum law for endpoint irreversibility on a driven ring.  A proof route proves a local central limit theorem for the wrapped Skellam displacement and controls the KL by density lower bounds.  The nearest related results are the circulant mixing-time moments of~\cite{ACMM13}.  A first decisive theorem would be the limit at a single $(A,\tau)$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, rings up to $N=128$ matched $\mathcal E(A,\tau)$ to within $5\times10^{-5}$.  A counterexample would be a scaling point where $\eta_N(t_N)$ misses the wrapped-Brownian value.  \emph{Resolution.} Now proved, Proposition~\ref{aj:wrapped}.

\begin{proposition}[Wrapped-Brownian irreversibility limit]\label{aj:wrapped}
On the homogeneous $N$-cycle with $p_N=e^{A/(2N)}$, $q_N=e^{-A/(2N)}$, and $t_N=N^2\tau/(p_N+q_N)$, the efficiency satisfies $\eta_N(t_N)\to\mathcal E(A,\tau)$ locally uniformly on compacta of $(A,\tau)\in(\R\setminus\{0\})\times(0,\infty)$.  This proves Conjecture~\ref{aj10}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The endpoint law is the wrapped difference of two independent Poisson counts; its mode-$m$ Fourier coefficient $\exp(t_N[p_N(\omega^m-1)+q_N(\omega^{-m}-1)])$ converges to $e^{-2\pi^2m^2\tau+i\pi mA\tau}$, so by Gaussian Fourier-tail control the wrapped lattice density converges uniformly to the wrapped Gaussian $w_{A,\tau}$, which is bounded below.  Continuity of the Kullback--Leibler integrand and $\sigma_Nt_N=(p_N-q_N)(A/N)t_N\to A^2\tau/2$ give $\eta_N(t_N)\to\mathcal E(A,\tau)$, with local uniformity inherited from the uniform Fourier convergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Ballistic winding-aliasing horizon]\label{aj11}
For fixed edge affinity $a\neq0$ and level $c\in(0,1)$ there is a finite positive $u_c(a)$ with $|v|\,t_c(N,a)/N\to u_c(a)$ as $N\to\infty$, so fixed-bias endpoint irreversibility is lost on the ballistic winding timescale $N/|v|$, not the diffusive mixing timescale.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The path entropy production is proportional to the signed winding current, which an endpoint reveals only modulo $N$; at fixed nonzero drift the uncertainty about the integer winding number becomes macroscopic once the mean displacement is of order $N$, producing a ballistic information horizon even though positional mixing is diffusive.  A proof route compares competing winding sectors by Laplace asymptotics.  The nearest related results are~\cite{LP23,ACMM13}.  A first decisive theorem would be the horizon for $c=\tfrac12$ on the homogeneous ring.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, half-efficiency times up to $N=192$ scaled linearly in $N$ with slope near one, and $|v|t_{1/2}/N$ approached a finite constant.  A counterexample would be a diffusive $N^2$ scaling of the fixed-bias horizon.

\begin{conjecture}[Diffusive-to-ballistic irreversibility crossover, resolved false]\label{aj12}
For every fixed $c\in(0,1)$ there is a universal function $\Phi_c$ with $t_c=\tfrac{N^2}{p+q}\Phi_c(\mathrm{Pe})[1+o(1)]$ in the joint large-$N$ scaling, where $\Phi_c(z)\to\Phi_c(0)\in(0,\infty)$ as $z\to0$ and $\Phi_c(z)\sim u_c/|z|$ as $|z|\to\infty$, so Conjectures~\ref{aj10} and~\ref{aj11} are its weak- and strong-drift limits.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The P\'eclet number is the single dimensionless group controlling the transition from diffusive to ballistic loss of winding information, and the conjecture asserts that the half-efficiency time collapses onto one crossover curve interpolating the two proved-limit regimes.  A proof route matches the wrapped-Brownian and ballistic asymptotics through a uniform winding-sector expansion.  The nearest related results are~\cite{ACMM13}.  A first decisive theorem would be the collapse at small P\'eclet.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, at fixed affinity the scaled half-efficiency time across $N=64,128,192$ collapsed with a cross-$N$ spread below one percent.  A counterexample would be a P\'eclet value where the scaled times fail to collapse.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false as stated: Proposition~\ref{aj:c12} shows the ballistic first-crossing coefficient $u_c(a)$ of Conjecture~\ref{aj11} depends on the edge affinity $a$, so no single universal $\Phi_c(\mathrm{Pe})$ can have Conjecture~\ref{aj11} as its strong-drift limit for every fixed affinity.  A genuine one-variable P\'eclet crossover survives in the weak-edge-bias regime $a_N\to0$, which is the intended restriction.

\begin{proposition}[Affinity-dependence of the ballistic crossover coefficient]\label{aj:c12}
The ballistic first-crossing coefficient $u_c(a)$ of Conjecture~\ref{aj11} depends nontrivially on the edge affinity $a$, so no single universal $\Phi_c(\mathrm{Pe})$ with $\Phi_c(z)\sim u_c/|z|$ recovers Conjecture~\ref{aj11} for every fixed affinity.  With the Skellam rate function $I_{u,a}(d)=\tfrac uv J_{p,q}(dv/u)$, $p=e^{a/2}$, $q=e^{-a/2}$, $v=p-q$, the level-$\tfrac12$ coefficient solving $\min\{1,I_{u,a}(1-u)/(au)\}=\tfrac12$ equals $0.2923$, $0.2894$, $0.2806$, $0.2576$, $0.2354$ at $a=0.2,0.5,1,2,3$, with $u_{1/2}(a)\to\tfrac1{2(1+\sqrt{1/2})}=0.2929$ as $a\downarrow0$ and $u_{1/2}(a)\to0$ as $a\to\infty$.  Hence Conjecture~\ref{aj12} is false as a universal crossover covering every fixed affinity.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Since $\mathrm{Pe}\asymp|v|N/(p+q)$, fixing $a$ and letting $N\to\infty$ drives $\mathrm{Pe}\to\infty$, and matching $t_c=\tfrac{N^2}{p+q}\Phi_c(\mathrm{Pe})$ to the ballistic law $t_c\sim u_c(a)N/|v|$ of Conjecture~\ref{aj11} forces the tail constant $u_c$ in $\Phi_c(z)\sim u_c/|z|$ to equal $u_c(a)$ for every $a$.  The fluctuation relation gives $I_{u,a}(-u)=au$, so $\eta_\infty(u,a)=\min\{1,I_{u,a}(1-u)/(au)\}$; as $a\downarrow0$ the Skellam rate has the Gaussian form $I_{u,a}(1-u)=a(1-2u)^2/(4u)+o(a)$, giving $u_c(a)\to1/(2(1+\sqrt c))$, while as $a\to\infty$ backward jumps vanish and $I_{u,a}(1-u)$ tends to the finite Poisson cost $(1-u)\log\tfrac{1-u}u-1+2u$ against the linear denominator $au$, forcing $\eta_\infty\to0$ and $u_c(a)\to0$.  The tabulated values are reproduced in the verification script.  A single $\Phi_c$ therefore cannot hold across fixed affinities; restricting to the weak-edge-bias regime $a_N\to0$ with $\mathrm{Pe}$ finite or $o(N)$ restores a genuine one-variable P\'eclet crossover.
\end{proof}

\section{Nonequilibrium Ornstein--Uhlenbeck dynamics}

\begin{conjecture}[OU one-relaxation-time peak horizon, resolved false]\label{aj13}
If $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}>0$ and $t_*$ is a global maximizer of $L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)$, then $g_At_*\le1$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The Gaussian lag KL rises from zero as infinitesimal trajectory irreversibility becomes resolvable and falls as cross-time covariance vanishes, and the slowest drift timescale appears to cap the location of the dominant peak even under strong nonnormal transient amplification, a sharper Gaussian analogue of Conjecture~\ref{aj2}.  A proof route expresses the Gaussian KL through canonical correlations of the two-time covariance.  The nearest related results are the OU dissipation decompositions of~\cite{NKI26} and the signal-response mapping irreversibility of~\cite{Auc19}.  A first decisive theorem would be the normal (commuting) drift case.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the maximum $g_At_*$ over stable systems in dimensions two to five, including nonnormal drifts, was $0.774$.  A counterexample would be a stable OU process whose lag-KL peak lies beyond one drift-relaxation time.  \emph{Resolution.} The bound is false: Proposition~\ref{aj:c1314} exhibits a five-dimensional nonnormal drift, a single Jordan block with every eigenvalue $-1$ (so $g_A=1$) and isotropic diffusion, whose lag-KL peak lies at $t_*=1.069\ldots$, giving $g_At_*=1.069>1$; the earlier stress test sampled only drifts with negative-definite symmetric part and so missed the strong nonnormal transient amplification that pushes the horizon past one drift-relaxation time, and a repaired bound must control nonnormality (a numerical-abscissa or hypocoercive constant), not the spectral abscissa alone.

\begin{conjecture}[OU spectral-area bound, resolved false]\label{aj14}
For every stable nonequilibrium OU process, $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)\,dt\le\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}}{g_A^2}$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is the Gaussian analogue of Conjecture~\ref{aj3} with a sharper constant, Gaussianity removing the rare-state KL amplification that forces the factor-of-two safety margin for arbitrary chains.  A proof route uses Lyapunov/operator inequalities for the integrated two-time covariance.  The nearest related results are~\cite{NKI26,Auc19}.  A first decisive theorem would be the scalar and normal-drift cases.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the maximum normalized area $g_A^2\!\int L_{\mathrm{OU}}\,dt/\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}$ was $0.553$, including strongly nonnormal drifts.  A counterexample would be a stable OU process exceeding the budget.  \emph{Resolution.} The bound is false: for the same five-dimensional Jordan-block drift of Proposition~\ref{aj:c1314}, $g_A=1$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}=32$ while $\int_0^\infty L_{\mathrm{OU}}\,dt=40.50\ldots$, so the normalized area is $1.266>1$; as with Conjecture~\ref{aj13}, only a nonnormality-corrected budget can hold.

\begin{proposition}[A nonnormal Ornstein--Uhlenbeck counterexample to the peak-horizon and spectral-area bounds]\label{aj:c1314}
Let $A=-I_5+2N$ with $N$ the $5\times5$ nilpotent first-superdiagonal shift and $D=I_5$, a Hurwitz drift with every eigenvalue $-1$, so $g_A=1$.  The stationary covariance solving $AC+CA^\top+2D=0$ has integer entries, the entropy-production rate is $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}=32$, and the Gaussian lag KL $L_{\mathrm{OU}}$ of Proposition~\ref{aj:basic} attains its global maximum at $t_*=1.0693\ldots$, so $g_At_*=1.0693\ldots>1$, and has total area $\int_0^\infty L_{\mathrm{OU}}\,dt=40.497\ldots$, so $g_A^2\!\int L_{\mathrm{OU}}\,dt/\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}=1.2655\ldots>1$.  Hence Conjectures~\ref{aj13} and~\ref{aj14} both fail: the spectral abscissa $g_A$ alone bounds neither the peak location nor the integrated budget of the Gaussian arrow of time.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The covariance $C$ is obtained by solving the Lyapunov equation; substitution confirms $AC+CA^\top+2I_5=0$ with zero residual, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}=\operatorname{tr}[(A+DC^{-1})^\top D^{-1}(A+DC^{-1})C]=32$.  Using the Jordan-polynomial matrix exponential $e^{At}$ and the trace formula of Proposition~\ref{aj:basic}, $L_{\mathrm{OU}}$ rises from $L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)=\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}t+O(t^2)$, is still increasing at $t=1$ ($L_{\mathrm{OU}}'(1)\approx1.60>0$), peaks at $t_*=1.0693\ldots$, and has integral $40.497\ldots$; all quantities are reproduced in the verification script, and the margins ($6.9\%$ and $26.5\%$) far exceed any conditioning artifact.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[OU antisymmetric-covariance doubling law, resolved true]\label{aj15}
For every stable OU process with $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}>0$,
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\frac1{2t}\log L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)=\alpha_H,
\]
so the long-time Gaussian arrow of time decays at twice the slowest time-antisymmetric covariance mode.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
At long times $\Sigma_t$ approaches $C\oplus C$, its difference from the time-reversed covariance is linear in $H(t)$, and Gaussian KL between nearby covariances is quadratic in that difference, so the exponent doubles, the Gaussian counterpart of Conjecture~\ref{aj4}.  A proof route is a matrix Taylor expansion of the Gaussian KL around $C\oplus C$.  The nearest related results are~\cite{NKI26}.  A first decisive theorem would be the normal-drift case, where $H$ has an explicit modal form.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the ratio of the lag-KL tail exponent to twice the $H(t)$ tail exponent had median $1.0000$ over stable systems in dimensions two to five.  A counterexample would be a decay rate other than twice an antisymmetric-covariance rate.  \emph{Resolution.} Now proved, Proposition~\ref{aj:oudoubling}.

\begin{proposition}[Gaussian antisymmetric-covariance doubling]\label{aj:oudoubling}
For a stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process with stationary covariance $C\succ0$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{OU}}>0$, the two-time covariance tends to $C\oplus C\succ0$, its time-antisymmetric part is $H(t)=e^{At}C-Ce^{A^\top t}\not\equiv0$, and for all large $t$ there are $0<c<C'$ with $c\|H(t)\|_F^2\le L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)\le C'\|H(t)\|_F^2$.  Since $H$ is a matrix exponential polynomial with slowest surviving rate $\alpha_H$, $\liminf_{t\to\infty}-\tfrac1{2t}\log L_{\mathrm{OU}}(t)=\alpha_H$.  This proves Conjecture~\ref{aj15}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The Gaussian Kullback--Leibler divergence between the two-time law and its time reversal is a smooth function of the covariance vanishing to second order at the positive-definite limit $C\oplus C$, hence is bounded above and below by $\|H(t)\|_F^2$ near the limit; $H(t)=e^{At}C-Ce^{A^\top t}$ is an exponential polynomial, and the $\liminf$ argument of Proposition~\ref{aj:doubling} gives the exponent $\alpha_H$.
\end{proof}


\part{Log-concavity laws for exactly solved random conformal geometry}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The two conjectures below concern the shape of two exactly solved objects in random conformal geometry: the DOZZ three-point structure constant of Liouville conformal field theory, and the modulus law of the Brownian annulus.  Each asserts strict log-concavity of an exact special-function density along its natural spectral or scale coordinate.  Such a law forces one preferred value, forbids secondary shoulders or competing saddles, and turns qualitative bootstrap and shape questions into convex-analysis problems, with globally controlled saddle-point approximations and certified one-dimensional quadrature as corollaries.  Both objects are given by closed forms---the Barnes-function representation of the DOZZ constant~\cite{KRV20} and the exact modulus transform of the Brownian annulus~\cite{ARS22}---so both conjectures are exactly and finitely checkable on any grid of parameters, in contrast with continuum-limit shape statements that admit only finite-size surrogates.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{ak:basic}: the reduction of each curvature to the part of the closed form that carries its sign, the vanishing of the DOZZ modulus at zero momentum, and the boundary-swap symmetry of the annulus modulus.  The nearest precedents are the DOZZ formula of Kupiainen, Rhodes, and Vargas~\cite{KRV20} and the annulus modulus law of Ang, Remy, and Sun~\cite{ARS22}; the strict log-concavity in the internal Liouville momentum and in the logarithmic annulus modulus, together with the charge chamber that makes the first hold, is what is proposed as new.  Both statements are checkable on grids but not proved, and a rigorous proof requires continuous rather than gridwise control of the second derivative; the interior charge chamber of the first is necessary, its two boundaries each carrying an explicit sign reversal recorded below.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{ak2}, the annulus modular log-concavity, has been resolved false by Proposition~\ref{ak:c2}: at large boundary-length ratio the logarithmic-modulus curvature turns positive, so log-concavity fails in the tail, while the DOZZ law of Conjecture~\ref{ak1} stands.

For Liouville conformal field theory fix $b>0$, write $Q=b+b^{-1}$, $\gamma(y)=\Gamma(y)/\Gamma(1-y)$, and let $\mu>0$ be the cosmological constant.  The Barnes function $\Upsilon_b$ is defined for $0<\Re x<Q$ by
\[
\log\Upsilon_b(x)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\dd t}{t}\left[\Bigl(\tfrac Q2-x\Bigr)^2e^{-t}-\frac{\sinh^2\!\bigl((\tfrac Q2-x)t/2\bigr)}{\sinh(bt/2)\,\sinh(t/2b)}\right],
\]
and extends to an entire function.  The DOZZ structure constant for real charges $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$ with $\bar\alpha=\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3$ is
\[
C_b(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=\bigl[\pi\mu\,\gamma(b^2)b^{2-2b^2}\bigr]^{(Q-\bar\alpha)/b}\,\frac{\Upsilon_b'(0)\,\prod_{i=1}^3\Upsilon_b(2\alpha_i)}{\Upsilon_b(\bar\alpha-Q)\,\prod_{i=1}^3\Upsilon_b(\bar\alpha-2\alpha_i)},
\]
and the principal series is parameterized by internal momentum $P\ge0$ through $\alpha=\tfrac Q2+iP$.  For an equal external charge $a$ write $M_a(P)=\bigl|C_b(a,a,\tfrac Q2+iP)\bigr|$ for the symmetric spectral modulus.  For the Brownian annulus, following Ang, Remy, and Sun~\cite{ARS22}, let $\eta$ be the Dedekind eta function, and conditional on the boundary-length ratio $x>0$ let $X_\tau$ be the positive random variable with Mellin transform
\[
\E[X_\tau^{it}]=\frac{2\pi t}{3\sinh(2\pi t/3)}\,e^{-2\pi\tau t^2/3},\qquad t\in\R,
\]
and density $\rho_\tau$; the modulus $\tau>0$ then has density $p_x(\tau)\propto\eta(2i\tau)\,\rho_\tau(x)$, the constant of proportionality depending only on $x$.

\begin{proposition}[Curvature reductions and boundary symmetry]\label{ak:basic}
$\Upsilon_b$ is entire with simple zeros exactly at $-b\,\mathbb N_0-b^{-1}\mathbb N_0$ and at $Q+b\,\mathbb N_0+b^{-1}\mathbb N_0$; in particular $\Upsilon_b(Q)=0$, so $M_a(0)=0$ and the log-concavity of $M_a$ is a statement on $P>0$.  The prefactor modulus and the momentum-independent factor $|\Upsilon_b(2a)|$ are constant in $P$, so
\[
\frac{\dd^2}{\dd P^2}\log M_a(P)=\frac{\dd^2}{\dd P^2}\Bigl[\log|\Upsilon_b(Q+2iP)|-2\log|\Upsilon_b(\tfrac Q2+iP)|-2\log|\Upsilon_b(2a-\tfrac Q2+iP)|\Bigr].
\]
For the Brownian annulus, $\log p_x(e^s)=\log\eta(2ie^s)+\log\rho_{e^s}(x)+\kappa(x)$ with $\kappa$ independent of $s$, so $\dd^2\!\log p_x(e^s)/\dd s^2$ is independent of the normalization, and $p_{1/x}(\tau)=x^2p_x(\tau)$, so that curvature is invariant under $x\mapsto1/x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The standard shift relations $\Upsilon_b(x+b)=\gamma(bx)b^{1-2bx}\Upsilon_b(x)$ and $\Upsilon_b(x+b^{-1})=\gamma(x/b)b^{2x/b-1}\Upsilon_b(x)$ extend $\Upsilon_b$ to an entire function with the stated zeros; $Q=Q+0\cdot b+0\cdot b^{-1}$ is one of them, so $\Upsilon_b(Q)=0$ and the numerator factor $\Upsilon_b(2\alpha_3)=\Upsilon_b(Q+2iP)$ vanishes at $P=0$, giving $M_a(0)=0$.  In $C_b(a,a,\tfrac Q2+iP)$ the base $\pi\mu\,\gamma(b^2)b^{2-2b^2}$ is real and positive for $0<b^2<1$, so the prefactor modulus is that base raised to $\Re[(Q-\bar\alpha)/b]=(Q/2-2a)/b$, independent of $P$; for general $b>0$ the base or a self-duality branch factor may enter, but any such factor has modulus exponential-linear in $P$ and is therefore annihilated by the second $P$-derivative, so the curvature identity holds for every $b>0$; the factors $\Upsilon_b(2a)$ are real and $P$-independent, and $\Upsilon_b(\bar\alpha-2\alpha_3)=\Upsilon_b(2a-\tfrac Q2-iP)$ is the complex conjugate of $\Upsilon_b(2a-\tfrac Q2+iP)$, so has the same modulus; collecting the surviving factors gives the displayed identity.  For the annulus, $\eta(2i\tau)$ is real and positive for $\tau>0$, the proportionality constant is $s$-independent, and $\rho_\tau(x)=g_\tau(\log x)/x$ with $g_\tau$ the even density of $\log X_\tau$, whence $\rho_\tau(1/x)=x^2\rho_\tau(x)$ and the swap invariance follows.
\end{proof}

\section{Spectral and modular log-concavity}

\begin{conjecture}[DOZZ spectral log-concavity]\label{ak1}
For every $b>0$ and every real external charge $a$ with $\tfrac Q3\le a<\tfrac Q2$, the symmetric DOZZ spectral modulus is strictly log-concave in the internal momentum:
\[
\frac{\dd^2}{\dd P^2}\log\bigl|C_b(a,a,\tfrac Q2+iP)\bigr|<0\qquad\text{for all }P>0.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The principal-series decomposition of a symmetric four-point Liouville amplitude weights the internal momentum by $M_a(P)^2$ times a conformal block, so strict log-concavity of $M_a$ gives the spectral density a single mode and forbids competing saddles, the structure-constant half of a total-positivity picture for Liouville data.  The leading operator-product factor already carries the sign; the conjectural content is that the Barnes-function descendant structure never overturns it.  The chamber $\tfrac Q3\le a<\tfrac Q2$ is necessary at both ends: below $\tfrac Q3$ the spectral curvature turns positive, already at $b=1$, $a=0.55$, and the joint log-concavity of $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)\mapsto\log|C_b|$ fails even at the symmetric point, a positive Hessian eigenvalue appearing at $(1.3,1.3,1.3)$, so only the one-dimensional spectral statement inside the interior chamber survives.  A proof route turns the second momentum derivative of the integral representation of $\log\Upsilon_b$ into a sign inequality for a hyperbolic-kernel integral.  The nearest related result is the DOZZ formula of Kupiainen, Rhodes, and Vargas~\cite{KRV20}.  A first decisive theorem would be the self-dual point $b=1$, where $\Upsilon_1$ has an elementary form.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, an independent evaluation of the exact $\Upsilon_b$ integral over $b\in\{0.5,0.8,1,1.3\}$ and the full chamber gave strictly negative spectral curvature throughout, with the two boundary controls turning positive as required.  A counterexample would be one regular point inside the chamber with nonnegative spectral curvature.

\begin{conjecture}[Brownian-annulus modular log-concavity, resolved false]\label{ak2}
For the Brownian annulus and every boundary-length ratio $x>0$, the modulus density is log-concave in the logarithmic modulus:
\[
s\longmapsto\log p_x(e^s)\quad\text{is strictly concave on }\R.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The modulus of a random annulus is the one conformal invariant of its shape, and the conjecture asserts that after passing to the multiplicative coordinate $s=\log\tau$ its law has a single preferred scale, with no secondary shoulder at very thin or very thick annuli.  The density is the product of a Dedekind-eta conformal-ghost factor and a heat-smoothed log-ratio density, and the content is that this product preserves concavity in logarithmic time, which neither factor forces separately.  A proof route combines tail control as $\tau\to0,\infty$ with a sign computation for the second logarithmic derivative of the exact modulus transform.  The nearest related result is the annulus modulus law of Ang, Remy, and Sun~\cite{ARS22}.  A first decisive theorem would be the symmetric annulus $x=1$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, an independent Fourier inversion of the exact transform, multiplied by the exact eta factor, gave strictly negative logarithmic-modulus curvature at every moderate boundary ratio tested, with the $x\mapsto1/x$ symmetry reproduced.  A counterexample would be a boundary ratio and a modulus at which the logarithmic density is locally convex.  \emph{Resolution.} The conjecture is false at large boundary ratio.  Writing $\log X_\tau=Z+G_\tau$ with $Z$ logistic of scale $\tfrac23$ and $G_\tau$ Gaussian of variance $\tfrac{4\pi\tau}3$, the logistic right tail $f_Z(z)\sim\tfrac32e^{-3z/2}$ gives $g_\tau(y)\sim\tfrac32e^{-3y/2}e^{3\pi\tau/2}$, so as $x=e^y\to\infty$ the logarithmic-modulus curvature tends to a positive limit $\mathcal C_\infty(\tau)$, equal to $0.9746$ at $\tau=0.30$; a finite certificate already appears at $x=e^5$, $\tau=0.30$, where the curvature is $+0.380$ (Proposition~\ref{ak:c2}).  The deposited scan reached only moderate boundary ratios and so missed the tail; by the $x\mapsto1/x$ symmetry the same convexity occurs in the opposite tail.

\begin{proposition}[Failure of annulus log-concavity at large boundary ratio]\label{ak:c2}
For the Brownian-annulus modulus density $p_x(\tau)\propto\eta(2i\tau)\rho_\tau(x)$, the logarithmic-modulus curvature $\dd^2\log p_x(e^s)/\dd s^2$ is positive for sufficiently large boundary ratio $x$.  At $x=e^5$, $\tau=0.30$ an independent Fourier inversion of the exact modulus transform, multiplied by the exact eta factor, gives curvature $+0.3798$; the value grows to $+0.90$ at $x=e^7$ and to the positive limit $\mathcal C_\infty(0.30)=0.9746$ as $x\to\infty$.  Hence Conjecture~\ref{ak2} is false.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
From the Mellin transform $\mathbb E[X_\tau^{it}]=\tfrac{2\pi t}{3\sinh(2\pi t/3)}e^{-2\pi\tau t^2/3}$, $\log X_\tau=Z+G_\tau$ with $Z$ centred logistic of scale $\tfrac23$ and $G_\tau\sim N(0,\tfrac{4\pi\tau}3)$ independent.  Since $f_Z(z)=\tfrac38\operatorname{sech}^2(\tfrac{3z}4)\sim\tfrac32e^{-3z/2}$ as $z\to\infty$, Gaussian averaging gives $g_\tau(y)\sim\tfrac32e^{-3y/2}\,\mathbb E[e^{3G_\tau/2}]=\tfrac32e^{-3y/2}e^{3\pi\tau/2}$ locally uniformly in $\tau$, and likewise after two $\tau$-derivatives.  With $\eta(2i\tau)$ real and $\log\eta(2i\tau)=-\pi\tau/6+\sum_{n\ge1}\log(1-e^{-4\pi\tau n})$, and writing $x_n=4\pi n\tau$, $q_n=e^{-x_n}$, the curvature of $\log p_x(e^s)$ in $s=\log\tau$ tends as $x\to\infty$ to $\mathcal C_\infty(\tau)=\tfrac{4\pi}3\tau+\sum_{n\ge1}\bigl(\tfrac{x_nq_n}{1-q_n}-\tfrac{x_n^2q_n}{(1-q_n)^2}\bigr)>0$, in which the $\tfrac{4\pi}3\tau$ term is the logistic--Gaussian tail contribution $(-\tfrac\pi6+\tfrac{3\pi}2)\tau$ and the sum is the eta $q$-series, which does not vanish at finite $\tau$ and cannot be dropped.  At $\tau=0.30$ this gives $\mathcal C_\infty=0.9746$.  The finite value at $x=e^5$, $\tau=0.30$ is obtained by direct high-precision Fourier inversion of the exact transform, stable under refinement of the step, and is reproduced in the verification script.
\end{proof}

\part{Bold conjectures in theoretical fluid dynamics}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The fifteen conjectures below are sharp, falsifiable statements about the small-scale and singular behaviour of the incompressible Euler, Navier--Stokes, Boussinesq, generalized surface quasi-geostrophic, and point-vortex systems.  They fall in six groups: two-dimensional small-scale creation (Conjectures~\ref{al1} to~\ref{al3}), enhanced dissipation and hypoelliptic mixing (Conjectures~\ref{al4} and~\ref{al5}), the geometry and regularity of three-dimensional Euler and Navier--Stokes singularities (Conjectures~\ref{al6} to~\ref{al8}), band-limited kinematics and rapid rotation (Conjectures~\ref{al9} and~\ref{al10}), stratified and active-scalar singularities (Conjectures~\ref{al11} to~\ref{al13}), and point-vortex collapse and non-Beltramization (Conjectures~\ref{al14} and~\ref{al15}).  Each is a determinate law with a stated mechanism, a nearest-literature boundary, a first decisive theorem, and a route to disproof, and each is deliberately bold: a proof or a counterexample would reorganize how one reads the corresponding small-scale or singular problem.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{al:anchors}: the exact three-vortex self-similar collapse anchor, the degenerate one-drift enhanced-dissipation exponent, the homogeneity-reduced generalized-SQG neck reduction, and the exact Beltrami Lamb-vector identity with Frenet dilation invariance.  These are statements about continuum solutions---blow-up signatures, vanishing-viscosity and large-bandwidth limits, and long-time or asymptotic laws---so they lie and every one; the accompanying diagnostics test reduced models, exact anchors, or prerequisite scalings, never the full law.  Several carry attributions where a sharp exponent or anchor is due to earlier work: the degenerate-shear exponent of Albritton, Beekie, and Novack~\cite{ABN22} (Conjecture~\ref{al5}), the Lorentz-endpoint boundary of Phuc~\cite{Phuc15} (Conjecture~\ref{al8}), and the self-similar three-vortex collapse of Aref~\cite{Aref10} (Conjecture~\ref{al14}); Conjecture~\ref{al11} is where the part's novelty is most in question, since at equal viscosity and diffusivity its critical-layer anomaly may reduce to known inviscid repeated-root asymptotics times the Kelvin diffusion factor, and only its sharp generic coefficient is claimed as new.

Throughout, $u$ is a divergence-free velocity field on the flat torus or on $\mathbb R^d$, $\omega=\nabla\times u$ (the scalar curl in two dimensions) its vorticity, $S=\tfrac12(\nabla u+\nabla u^\top)$ the strain, $\xi=\omega/|\omega|$ the vorticity direction, and $\hat f(k)$ the Fourier coefficients.  Objects specific to a single conjecture are defined in its statement.

\begin{proposition}[Exact anchors and reductions]\label{al:anchors}
{\rm(i)} For three planar point vortices with circulations $\Gamma=(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2,\Gamma_3)$ satisfying $\Gamma_1\Gamma_2+\Gamma_2\Gamma_3+\Gamma_3\Gamma_1=0$ and vanishing angular impulse, the motion is exactly self-similar with a finite-time collapse or expansion; the symmetric choice $\Gamma=(1,1,-\tfrac12)$ satisfies the collapse condition.  {\rm(ii)} For the degenerate one-drift shear generator $X_0=y^m\partial_x$, $X_1=\partial_y$ with dissipation $-\nu X_1^\ast X_1$, the enhanced-dissipation gap obeys $\operatorname{gap}(L_\nu)\asymp\nu^{m/(m+2)}$ as $\nu\downarrow0$.  {\rm(iii)} The homogeneity-reduced neck equation $\dot d=-d^{\,1-\beta}$, $0<\beta\le1$, has $d(t)=[\beta(T-t)]^{1/\beta}$, so $d(t)\sim a_\beta(T-t)^{1/\beta}$ and, under the reciprocal-curvature ansatz $\kappa_{\max}\sim b_\beta(T-t)^{-1/\beta}$, the product $d\,\kappa_{\max}$ tends to a finite nonzero constant.  {\rm(iv)} A Beltrami field ($u\times\omega\equiv0$), in particular the ABC field, has identically vanishing Lamb vector; and the dimensionless pair (total curvature, scale-invariant torsion variation) of a $C^4$ space curve is invariant under spatial dilation.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
{\rm(i)} is the classical self-similar three-vortex analysis: the collapse condition makes the moment of inertia quadratic in time with the similarity geometry fixed by vanishing angular impulse~\cite{Aref10}; the displayed vector gives $1\cdot1+1\cdot(-\tfrac12)+(-\tfrac12)\cdot1=0$.  {\rm(ii)} is the degenerate-shear enhanced-dissipation estimate obtained by Fourier reduction in $x$ and hypoelliptic balance of the $m$-fold commutator against diffusion~\cite{ABN22}.  {\rm(iii)} integrates the separable ODE directly.  {\rm(iv)} is immediate: $u\times\omega=0$ makes the Lamb vector vanish pointwise, and total curvature $\int\kappa\,ds$ and $\int L|\partial_s\tau|/(1+L|\tau|)\,ds$ are scale-free, hence invariant under $u\mapsto\lambda u$.
\end{proof}

\section{Small-scale creation in two-dimensional Euler and Navier--Stokes}

\begin{conjecture}[Bulk-enstrophy spectral front]\label{al1}
Let $\omega$ be a smooth mean-zero solution of the $2$D Euler equation on $\mathbb T^2$ and, for $q\in(0,1)$, let $K_q(t)=\inf\{K\ge0:\sum_{|k|\le K}|\hat\omega(k,t)|^2\ge q\|\omega(t)\|_2^2\}$ be the radius carrying a fraction $q$ of the enstrophy.  For every $0<q<q'<1$ there are constants $C,c$ depending only on $q,q'$ such that $K_q(t)\le CK_{q'}(0)\exp(c\|\omega_0\|_\infty t)$ for all $t\ge0$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Pointwise vorticity gradients can grow double-exponentially~\cite{KiselevSverak14,Denisov15}; the conjecture asserts that a fixed \emph{bulk} quantile of the conserved enstrophy nonetheless migrates outward only single-exponentially, separating genuine small-scale creation from transport of a macroscopic fraction of enstrophy.  A proof route bounds the flux of enstrophy past a moving Fourier radius by the $L^\infty$-transport rate of the vorticity.  The nearest results are the small-scale creation constructions of Kiselev and \v Sver\'ak~\cite{KiselevSverak14}.  A first decisive theorem would be the bound for $q$ near zero.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a pseudo-spectral Euler run showed the bulk quantiles $K_{90},K_{99}$ moving far more slowly than $\max|\nabla\omega|$.  A counterexample would be a globally regular Euler flow with genuinely bulk super-exponential spectral transfer.

\begin{conjecture}[Super-exponential gradient sparsity]\label{al2}
For $\eta\in(0,1)$ let $G_\eta(t)=\{x:|\nabla\omega(x,t)|\ge\eta\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_\infty\}$.  If a smooth $2$D Euler solution has times $t_n\to\infty$ with $\log\|\nabla\omega(t_n)\|_\infty/t_n\to\infty$, then $|G_\eta(t_n)|\to0$ for every fixed $\eta\in(0,1)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The statement turns any super-exponential gradient-growth scenario into a geometric intermittency requirement: near-maximal gradients must occupy a vanishing area under the area-preserving Euler flow.  A proof route couples the $L^2$-conservation of vorticity to an area estimate for level sets of $|\nabla\omega|$.  The nearest results are again~\cite{KiselevSverak14,Denisov15}.  A first decisive theorem would be the implication for a single fixed $\eta$ under a hyperbolic-point growth ansatz.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a regular run showed a strong negative correlation between $\log\max|\nabla\omega|$ and the area fraction above $90\%$ of that maximum.  A counterexample would permit macroscopically large regions of near-maximal gradient.

\begin{conjecture}[Vanishing-viscosity global branch selection]\label{al3}
On $\mathbb T^2$ fix mean-zero vorticity and initial palinstrophy $P(\omega_0)=P_0>0$.  For viscosity $\nu>0$ and horizon $T$ let $D_{\nu,T}=\nu\int_0^T\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_2^2\,dt$ and $M_{\nu,T}$ its supremum under the palinstrophy constraint.  Fix $\tau\in(0,\infty)$, let $\nu_j\to0$ and $T_j\sqrt{P_0}\to\tau$, and take relative near-maximizers $D_{\nu_j,T_j}(\omega_{0,j})\ge(1-\varepsilon_j)M_{\nu_j,T_j}$ with $\varepsilon_j\to0$.  With $\ell_j=\|\omega_{0,j}\|_2/\|\nabla\omega_{0,j}\|_2$ and $W_j(y)=P_0^{-1/2}\omega_{0,j}(x_j+\ell_jy)$, every concentration limit is, after torus isometries, reflection, and sign, the same nontrivial profile $W_\tau$; and, when the normalized objectives are equicoercive, they $\Gamma$-converge at fixed $\tau$ to a variational problem whose maximizer is unique modulo these symmetries.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Finite-time enstrophy-dissipation and palinstrophy extremizers are computed numerically with several local branches~\cite{AyalaProtas14,AyalaDoeringSimon18,Matharu22}; the conjecture asserts unique selection only at the global vanishing-viscosity level, turning a family of numerical extreme events into one universal variational object.  A proof route is a $\Gamma$-convergence and concentration-compactness analysis of the rescaled objective.  The nearest results are the maximal-dissipation studies of~\cite{Matharu22}.  A first decisive theorem would be uniqueness of the concentration profile at a single $\tau$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a concentration-family surrogate reproduced the proposed symmetry reduction and profile collapse without performing the optimization.  A counterexample would be two inequivalent global limits, establishing genuine non-universality of worst-case dissipation.

\section{Enhanced dissipation and hypoelliptic mixing}

\begin{conjecture}[Reeb-graph spectral desert]\label{al4}
Let $H$ be a Morse Hamiltonian on a compact surface whose regular level sets form finitely many cells with quadratic saddles, and let $L_\nu=-\nabla^\perp H\cdot\nabla+\nu\Delta$ on mean-zero scalars.  In every fixed bounded window of imaginary frequency, as $\nu\to0$ the spectrum splits into slow eigenvalues $\lambda_j(\nu)=-\nu\mu_j+o(\nu)$, where $\mu_j$ are the eigenvalues of the effective weighted diffusion on the Reeb graph of $H$, and remaining eigenvalues with $\Re\lambda\le-c_H\nu^{1/2}$; in particular no eigenvalue branch decays at a rate $\nu^\alpha$ with $\tfrac12<\alpha<1$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law combines the $O(\nu)$ slow streamline-averaged dynamics on the Reeb graph~\cite{FreidlinWentzell93} with cellular enhanced dissipation~\cite{Brue24} into a two-band spectral statement with a forbidden intermediate range.  A proof route matches a graph-diffusion resolvent to a boundary-layer estimate near the separatrices.  The nearest results are~\cite{FreidlinWentzell93,Brue24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the two-band separation for a single cell with one saddle.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a coarse cellular operator robustly recovered the $O(\nu)$ slow band while the complementary $O(\nu^{1/2})$ band was not grid-resolvable, a limitation recorded there.  A counterexample would be an eigenvalue branch in the forbidden intermediate range.

\begin{conjecture}[H\"ormander-step enhanced-dissipation universality]\label{al5}
Consider $\partial_tf+X_0f=-\nu\sum_{j=1}^rX_j^\ast X_jf$ on a compact manifold with smooth invariant volume, $X_0$ volume-preserving, in a one-drift equiregular H\"ormander class where the missing drift directions are generated by Lie words containing exactly one $X_0$ and repeated commutators with the diffusive fields.  Let $m$ be the maximal number of diffusive commutators needed to span the tangent space.  If there is no nonconstant common first integral, then $\operatorname{gap}(L_\nu)\asymp\nu^{m/(m+2)}$ as $\nu\to0$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Degenerate-shear models already realize the exponent $m/(m+2)$; the conjecture is that bracket depth alone fixes the exponent across all one-drift equiregular geometries, a geometric universality class for enhanced dissipation.  A proof route is a quantitative hypoelliptic hypocoercivity estimate keyed to the commutator depth.  The nearest result, and the source of the anchor exponent, is Albritton, Beekie, and Novack~\cite{ABN22}; the exponent itself is theirs, and only the universality across geometries is claimed as new, an attribution carried in the statement.  A first decisive theorem would be a two-dimensional non-shear model with $m=2$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, Fourier-reduced shear operators with depths $m=1,2,3$ recovered the exponents $m/(m+2)$.  A counterexample would be a one-drift equiregular geometry whose exponent depends on more than the bracket depth.

\section{Geometry and regularity of three-dimensional singularities}

\begin{conjecture}[Frenet-frame completion barrier]\label{al6}
Suppose a Type-I Euler singularity at $T$ is carried by a connected high-vorticity tube $R_t$ containing a maximum-vorticity point, with radius comparable to the length $L(t)$ of a $C^4$ central vortex-line segment $\gamma_t$ of uniform chord-arc constant and nonvanishing curvature, so that Frenet torsion $\tau$ and $\partial_s\tau$ are defined.  With $K(t)=\int\kappa\,ds$ and $\mathrm{Tor}(t)=\int L(t)|\partial_s\tau|/(1+L(t)|\tau|)\,ds$, one has $\limsup_{t\to T}[K(t)+\mathrm{Tor}(t)]=\infty$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Classical geometric blow-up criteria emphasize curvature and vorticity-direction coherence; the conjecture makes torsion variation the missing Frenet obstruction inside a coherent tube, so bounded total curvature forces the scale-invariant torsion diagnostic to diverge.  A proof route feeds the Beale--Kato--Majda integral~\cite{BKM84} through the tube geometry.  The nearest results are the three-dimensional Euler geometric criteria surveyed in~\cite{Gibbon08}.  A first decisive theorem would be the barrier under an axisymmetric-with-swirl tube model.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the dimensionless (total curvature, torsion variation) pair was confirmed dilation-invariant to relative error below $10^{-6}$ on a modulated helix; the singular statement is conditional on a Type-I tube.  A counterexample would be a bona fide Type-I tube with bounded curvature and torsion.

\begin{conjecture}[Type-I stretching coherence]\label{al7}
Let $\Omega(t)=\|\omega(t)\|_\infty$, $A_\lambda(t)=\{x:|\omega(x,t)|\ge\lambda\Omega(t)\}$, $\alpha=\xi\cdot S\xi$, and let $\bar\alpha_\lambda,V_\lambda$ be the $|\omega|^2$-weighted mean and standard deviation of $\alpha$ over $A_\lambda$.  If a Type-I singularity satisfies $0<c\le(T-t)\Omega(t)\le C$, then for every $\lambda$ sufficiently close to $1$ there is a sequence $t_n\to T$ with $(T-t_n)\bar\alpha_\lambda(t_n)\to1$ and $(T-t_n)V_\lambda(t_n)\to0$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law upgrades the scalar Type-I rate to concentration of the entire local stretching-rate distribution on the intense-vorticity core, forcing an emergent coherent stretching clock in any Type-I blow-up.  A proof route differentiates $\log\Omega$ and controls the weighted variance of $\alpha$ by the Type-I hypothesis.  The nearest results are the Beale--Kato--Majda control~\cite{BKM84} and the geometric-depletion literature in~\cite{Gibbon08}.  A first decisive theorem would be the mean statement $(T-t_n)\bar\alpha_\lambda\to1$ alone.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a smooth low-resolution Taylor--Green run gave a finite subcritical weighted stretching diagnostic, the singular limit being inaccessible; the statement is conditional on a Type-I singularity.  A counterexample would be a Type-I blow-up whose core stretching-rate distribution stays spread.

\begin{conjecture}[Weak-Lorentz projected-Lamb regularity criterion]\label{al8}
Let $u$ be a Leray--Hopf solution of the $3$D Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$, or on $\mathbb T^3$ in the Galilean frame with mean velocity zero, let $\omega=\nabla\times u$, $P$ the Leray projector, and $\Lambda=P(u\times\omega)$ the projected Lamb vector.  If $\Lambda\in L^2((0,T);L^{3/2,\infty}_x)$, then $u$ is smooth on $(0,T]$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The criterion rewards local Beltrami depletion geometrically: a solution whose projected Lamb vector is small in the weak-Lorentz critical norm cannot be singular.  Its Stokes scaling lands exactly at the unresolved $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$ velocity endpoint, so the statement is deliberately placed one Lorentz index beyond the range known to be regular.  A proof route combines a forced-Stokes estimate with the Lamb-vector structure.  The nearest results are the near-Beltrami depletion of Farhat and Gruji\'c~\cite{FarhatGrujic19} and, as the boundary anchor, the finite-index regularity of Phuc~\cite{Phuc15}: $L^\infty_tL^{3,q}_x$ regularity is known for $q<\infty$, which is why the endpoint $q=\infty$ is chosen, an attribution carried in the statement.  A first decisive theorem would close the criterion under an additional smallness of the strong $L^{3/2}$ norm.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a smooth Taylor--Green run computed a finite weak-$L^{3/2}$ Lamb quasi-norm while the exact ABC Beltrami field annihilated the Lamb vector; the criterion is an analytic implication.  A counterexample would be a singular solution with finite critical projected-Lamb norm.

\section{Band-limited kinematics and rapid rotation}

\begin{conjecture}[Helicity-defect law for stretching extremals]\label{al9}
Let $V_N$ be divergence-free mean-zero fields on $\mathbb T^3$ with Fourier support $|k|\le N$.  Fix admissible kinetic energy $K$ and enstrophy $E$, put relative helicity $\rho=H/(2\sqrt{KE})$, and let $M_N(\rho;K,E)=\sup|\int\omega\cdot S\omega|$ over $V_N$ at these constraints and helicity $\rho$.  Whenever $\rho$ and $0$ are both uniformly feasible as $N\to\infty$ and the enstrophy-to-energy ratio $E/K$ is bounded away from its first-shell minimum, so that zero-sum stretching triads persist and $M_N(0;K,E)>0$ uniformly, $M_N(\rho;K,E)/M_N(0;K,E)\to(1-\rho^2)^{3/2}$ locally uniformly for $\rho$ in compact subsets of $(-1,1)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law quantifies how close-to-Beltrami alignment suppresses the strongest possible vortex stretching, through a single universal helicity-defect factor in the large-bandwidth extremal envelope.  The triad-active hypothesis is necessary: at the first-shell ratio $E/K=1$ every admissible field is supported on $|k|=1$, which contains no zero-sum triad $k+\ell+m=0$, so the stretching functional vanishes identically and the ratio is undefined; an interior ratio populates the second shell and restores $M_N(0)>0$.  A proof route is a constrained variational analysis of the stretching functional with the two quadratic and one helicity constraints.  The nearest results are the maximum-enstrophy-production optimizations with energy, enstrophy, and helicity constraints in the depletion literature.  A first decisive theorem would be the two-shell case.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a two-shell helical Monte Carlo held energy and enstrophy fixed while varying helicity and confirmed the suppression sign, not the exponent.  A counterexample would be a different exponent, revealing multiscale geometry beyond the simple helicity defect.

\begin{conjecture}[Diophantine small-divisor rotation law]\label{al10}
For $K\ge1$ let $\delta(K)$ be the minimum nonzero inertial-wave triad detuning among triads with maximal wavenumber at most $K$ on an anisotropic torus, and assume the sharp arithmetic law $\delta(K)=K^{-\tau+o(1)}$.  For fixed data of finite Sobolev regularity $H^s$ whose Fourier coefficients obey a polynomial lower envelope $|\hat u(k)|\gtrsim|k|^{-s'}$ along the wavenumbers of the triads realizing $\delta(K_\ast)$ (a frequency-rich nondegeneracy, which also excludes a single inertial-wave mode, for which $(u\cdot\nabla)u\equiv0$; for $C^\infty$ data the super-polynomial Fourier decay empties this condition, so the lower envelope forces finite regularity and only the upper bound $E(\Omega,\nu)\lesssim\epsilon_\ast^{1+o(1)}$ survives without it) and $O(1)$ times let $E(\Omega,\nu)$ be the error between rotating $3$D Navier--Stokes at rotation $\Omega$ and its exact-resonant normal form in a fixed lower Sobolev norm, with a strictly positive data constant.  In the joint regime $K_\ast=(\Omega/\nu)^{1/(\tau+2)}\to\infty$ and $\epsilon_\ast=(\Omega^2\nu^\tau)^{-1/(\tau+2)}\to0$, one has $E(\Omega,\nu)=\epsilon_\ast^{1+o(1)}$ up to Sobolev-loss, subpower, and data constants, and the $\Omega$ power cannot be uniformly improved over tori realizing the same sharp $\tau$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law ties the fluid averaging error to the sharp asymptotic exponent of the minimum nonzero triad detuning, making arithmetic properties of the torus quantitatively observable in the rate of rotational averaging and avoiding the ambiguity of a nonoptimal Diophantine lower bound.  A proof route bounds near-resonant contributions by the minimum detuning through a normal-form transformation.  The nearest results are the near-resonance approximations of Cheng and Sakellaris~\cite{ChengSakellaris23}.  A first decisive theorem would be the upper bound $E\le\epsilon_\ast^{1-o(1)}$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, integer triad enumeration on an irrational aspect ratio showed the expected algebraic minimum-detuning trend and fewer exact resonances than a rational comparison torus.  A counterexample would be nonlinear cancellation beating the naive small-divisor balance.

\section{Stratified and active-scalar singularities}

\begin{conjecture}[Critical-Richardson viscous log anomaly]\label{al11}
For a fixed Kelvin ray $(k,\eta)$, $k\ne0$, in the linearized equally viscous and diffusive $2$D Boussinesq system about Couette flow at Richardson number $\mathrm{Ri}=\tfrac14$, let $\hat\omega_{k,\eta}(t)$ be the vorticity amplitude along the sheared frequency $(k,\eta-kt)$.  For generic data with nonzero projection onto the repeated critical indicial mode, $\sup_{1\le t\le c(\nu k^2)^{-1/3}}|\hat\omega_{k,\eta}(t)|/(1+t)^{1/2}\sim C_{k,\eta}\log(1/\nu)$ as $\nu\to0$, with $C_{k,\eta}>0$; for every fixed $\mathrm{Ri}>\tfrac14$ the analogous normalized supremum is $O(1)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The conjecture predicts a sharp matched-asymptotic interaction between the inviscid critical repeated-root logarithm and the viscous enhanced-dissipation cutoff, identifying $\mathrm{Ri}=\tfrac14$ as a genuinely singular viscous asymptotic threshold rather than merely the endpoint of inviscid stability.  A proof route matches the inviscid Kelvin solution to the viscous cutoff on the enhanced-dissipation time.  The nearest results are the stratified Couette analyses of Yang and Lin~\cite{YangLin18} and Masmoudi, Said-Houari, and Zhao~\cite{MSHZ25}.  A first decisive theorem would be the reduced-ODE log growth at $\mathrm{Ri}=\tfrac14$.  This is where the part's novelty is most in question: at equal viscosity and diffusivity the diffusion term is a scalar multiple of the identity on the Kelvin $(\omega,\theta)$ system, so the viscous fundamental matrix factors as $\exp(-\nu\!\int_0^t(k^2+(\eta-ks)^2)\,\dd s)$ times the inviscid one and the logarithm is inherited from the inviscid critical repeated root; only the sharp generic coefficient $C_{k,\eta}$ and the uniform viscous matching are claimed as new.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a reduced Kelvin indicial ODE with an $e^{-\nu t^3/3}$ cutoff produced a growing logarithmic normalized peak precisely at $\mathrm{Ri}=\tfrac14$.  A counterexample would be an $O(1)$ normalized supremum at $\mathrm{Ri}=\tfrac14$.

\begin{conjecture}[Generalized-SQG neck-curvature similarity law]\label{al12}
Use $u=\nabla^\perp\Lambda^{-2+\beta}\theta$ with $0<\beta\le1$.  Suppose a smooth generalized-SQG patch boundary develops a single symmetric self-similar neck singularity at $T$, with minimum opposing-boundary distance $d(t)$ and maximum curvature $\kappa_{\max}(t)$ in the same similarity core.  Then $d(t)\sim a_\beta(T-t)^{1/\beta}$, $\kappa_{\max}(t)\sim b_\beta(T-t)^{-1/\beta}$, and $d(t)\kappa_{\max}(t)\to c_\beta\in(0,\infty)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law proposes a universal reciprocal neck/curvature exponent and a nonzero dimensionless product for the single-neck class, a simple diagnostic across the Euler-to-SQG interpolation.  A proof route is a self-similar reduction of the patch contour dynamics near the neck.  The nearest results are the no-splash and blow-up analyses of Kiselev and Luo~\cite{KiselevLuo23}, Gancedo and Patel~\cite{GancedoPatel18}, and the self-similar profiles of Hou and collaborators~\cite{Hou26gsqg}.  A first decisive theorem would be the exponent for the reduced neck ODE.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the homogeneity-reduced neck ODE of Proposition~\ref{al:anchors} reproduced $d\sim(T-t)^{1/\beta}$ with $d\kappa=O(1)$.  A counterexample would be a neck singularity with a different exponent or $d\kappa\to0,\infty$.

\begin{conjecture}[Boussinesq source-core co-location and alignment]\label{al13}
On $\mathbb T^2$ let $\theta^\circ=\theta-\langle\theta\rangle$, $\ell_\theta=\|\theta^\circ\|_\infty/\|\nabla\theta\|_\infty$, $A^\omega_\lambda=\{|\omega|\ge\lambda\|\omega\|_\infty\}$, and $A^\theta_\lambda=\{|\partial_x\theta|\ge\lambda\|\partial_x\theta\|_\infty\}$.  If a smooth inviscid Boussinesq solution develops an isolated finite-time singularity at $x_\ast$, then, intersecting both intense sets with a fixed ball isolating the core, for every $\lambda$ close to $1$ the distance between the localized sets divided by $\ell_\theta$ tends to zero; moreover, along a sequence in the core with distinct strain eigenvalues, $\nabla\theta$ aligns with the most compressive strain eigenvector.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law connects the exact vorticity source $\partial_x\theta$ with geometric strain alignment in a necessary blow-up-core localization, forcing the source, the vorticity maximum, and the compressive scalar-gradient mechanism to merge at the scalar-gradient scale.  A proof route tracks the co-evolution of the intense sets under the shared transport.  The nearest results are the Boussinesq blow-up asymptotics of Grundy and Kay~\cite{GrundyKay03} and the stagnation-point analysis of~\cite{Sarria15}.  A first decisive theorem would be the co-location clause alone.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a short smooth pseudo-spectral Boussinesq run showed a decreasing normalized distance between the vorticity maximum and the source maximum; the singular statement is conditional on a finite-time singularity.  A counterexample would be a blow-up with separated source and vorticity cores.

\section{Point-vortex collapse and non-Beltramization}

\begin{conjecture}[Minimal-admissible point-vortex collapse core]\label{al14}
Fix nonzero circulations for which at least one collapse-admissible subset exists---a subset being admissible if its isolated subsystem has a nontrivial self-similar finite-time collapse---and let $m_\ast$ be the least admissible cardinality.  Let $\mathcal C$ be the set of initial configurations undergoing a finite-time collision, with the resonance loci where two distinct minimal cores collapse simultaneously removed.  Then the union of collision strata whose fastest-collapsing core contains exactly $m_\ast$ vortices is relatively open and dense in $\mathcal C$, while strata with a strictly larger fastest core lie in positive-codimension substrata; and along every collision in this relatively generic set, similarity rescaling of the fastest core converges to an isolated self-similar $m_\ast$-vortex collapse with every spectator asymptotically farther than the core diameter.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law organizes the complicated planar collision set by a minimal-core universality principle: the smallest admissible collapsing subsystem generically dominates.  A proof route combines the classical self-similar collapse classification with a transversality analysis of the collision set.  The nearest results are the self-similar three-vortex collapse of Aref~\cite{Aref10}, whose collapse anchor is used here and is attributed in the statement, and the recent collapse analyses of Drivas and collaborators~\cite{Drivas26}.  A first decisive theorem would be relative density of the $m_\ast=3$ stratum for a circulation vector admitting a unique minimal core.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the exact anchor $\Gamma=(1,1,-\tfrac12)$ perturbed by two distant spectators contracted the core to about $2.4\%$ of its diameter while the spectator/core scale separation amplified.  A counterexample would be a robust same-codimension larger fastest core coexisting with a smaller admissible core.

\begin{conjecture}[High-vorticity non-Beltramization barrier]\label{al15}
On $\mathbb R^3$ with finite energy, or on $\mathbb T^3$ in the zero-mean Galilean frame, let $C_\lambda(t)$ be the connected component of $\{|\omega|\ge\lambda\Omega(t)\}$ containing a maximum-vorticity point, and $B_\lambda(t)=\int_{C_\lambda}|u\times\omega|^2/\int_{C_\lambda}|u|^2|\omega|^2$ when the denominator is nonzero.  Any Type-I Euler singularity with $0<c\le(T-t)\Omega(t)\le C$ satisfies $\limsup_{t\to T}B_\lambda(t)>0$ for every $\lambda$ sufficiently close to $1$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law makes persistent non-Beltramization a necessary local condition for a Type-I Euler singular core, ruling out asymptotically force-free high-vorticity cores as blow-up mechanisms.  A proof route shows that a vanishing local Lamb ratio would deplete the nonlinearity enough to contradict the Type-I rate.  The nearest results are the near-Beltrami depletion of Farhat and Gruji\'c~\cite{FarhatGrujic19} and the Beale--Kato--Majda control~\cite{BKM84}.  A first decisive theorem would be the barrier under axisymmetry with swirl.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the ABC field gave a Lamb-vector root-mean-square about $10^{-14}$ of a Taylor--Green comparison, confirming the diagnostic sharply detects exact Beltrami depletion; the singular statement is conditional on a Type-I singularity.  A counterexample would be a Type-I core that asymptotically Beltramizes.


\part{Metric geometry and spectral convexity in random conformal geometry}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The thirteen conjectures below complete the random-conformal-geometry bundle whose two exactly solved shape members---strict log-concavity of the DOZZ structure constant and of the Brownian-annulus modulus---are Conjectures~\ref{ak1} and~\ref{ak2} of Part~XX.  They fall in three groups: the metric geometry of Liouville quantum gravity (LQG), covering geodesic stars, the radial metric residual, metric-ball volume and boundary, space-filling SLE, and distance profiles (Conjectures~\ref{am1} to~\ref{am8}); the spectral convexity of Liouville conformal field theory, covering monotone likelihood ratio and log-concavity of sphere and torus blocks and DOZZ-weighted spectral densities (Conjectures~\ref{am9} to~\ref{am12}); and quantum-area nesting in conformal loop ensembles (Conjecture~\ref{am13}).  Each is a determinate, sharp, falsifiable law with a stated mechanism, a nearest-literature boundary, and a first decisive theorem.  The metric-geometry statements are continuum-limit laws (Hausdorff dimensions, scaling exponents, mixing and functional central limit theorems); the CFT statements are exact special-function shape properties whose descendant contributions are here tested only in the global (\(SL(2)\) or global-torus) block limit, a reduced-model check and a verification target.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{am:triangle}: the exact scaling triangle relating the boundary-length, roughness, and branching exponents, and the anchor reductions at the Brownian point \(\gamma=\sqrt{8/3}\).  Several statements are sharp interpolations of recognized open problems and attribute to the works whose anchors they extend.

Fix \(\gamma\in(0,2)\), write \(Q=\tfrac2\gamma+\tfrac\gamma2\), let \(h\) be a Gaussian free field variant, \(\mu_h\) the \(\gamma\)-LQG area measure, and \(D_h\) the \(\gamma\)-LQG metric, with Hausdorff dimension \(d_\gamma=\dim_{\mathrm H}(\mathbb C,D_h)\) and \(\xi=\gamma/d_\gamma\); the metric obeys Weyl scaling \(D_{h+c}=e^{\xi c}D_h\) and the area obeys \(\mu_{h+c}=e^{\gamma c}\mu_h\), and \(d_{\sqrt{8/3}}=4\).  For Liouville CFT write \(b>0\), \(Q_b=b+b^{-1}\), central charge \(c=1+6Q_b^2\), principal-series weights \(\Delta(P)=\tfrac{Q_b^2}4+P^2\), sphere OPE blocks \(\mathcal F_P(z)\) and torus blocks \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{tor}}_{a,P}(q)\) in the standard normalizations, and \(C_b\) for the DOZZ structure constant of Part~XX.  Objects specific to a single conjecture are defined in its statement.

\begin{proposition}[Scaling triangle and Brownian anchors]\label{am:triangle}
Set \(p_\gamma=d_\gamma/2\), \(H_\gamma=2/d_\gamma\), and \(\alpha_\gamma=1+2/d_\gamma\).  Then \(p_\gamma=1/H_\gamma=1/(\alpha_\gamma-1)\), so a single scalar controls the metric boundary-length dimension, the distance-profile roughness exponent, and the perimeter branching index.  At the Brownian point \(d_\gamma=4\) these are \(2,\tfrac12,\tfrac32\), the known values.  The affine star spectrum \(s_k(\gamma)=2+\tfrac{3-k}2(d_\gamma-2)\) satisfies \(s_1=d_\gamma\), \(s_3=2\) for every \(d_\gamma\), and \(s_k=5-k\) at \(d_\gamma=4\); and \(s_k\to2\) as \(d_\gamma\downarrow2\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The three displayed identities are immediate from the definitions of \(p_\gamma,H_\gamma,\alpha_\gamma\); at \(d_\gamma=4\) they evaluate to \(2,\tfrac12,\tfrac32\).  The affine spectrum is the unique affine-in-\(k\) function with \(s_1=d_\gamma\) and \(s_3=2\), and substituting \(d_\gamma=4\) gives \(5-k\), while \(d_\gamma\downarrow2\) sends every fixed \(s_k\) to \(2\).
\end{proof}

\section{Metric geometry of Liouville quantum gravity}

\begin{conjecture}[Affine LQG geodesic-star spectrum]\label{am1}
For a point \(z\) call \(z\) a \(k\)-star point if there are \(r>0\) and unit-speed \(D_h\)-geodesics \(\eta_1,\dots,\eta_k\) from \(z\) with disjoint interiors on \((0,r]\); let \(S_k\) be the set of such points.  With \(s_k(\gamma)=2+\tfrac{3-k}2(d_\gamma-2)\): if \(s_k(\gamma)>0\) then almost surely \(\dim_{\mathrm H}^{D_h}S_k=s_k(\gamma)\); if \(s_k(\gamma)<0\) then \(S_k=\varnothing\) almost surely; at the threshold \(s_k=0\) the set has \(D_h\)-dimension at most zero.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The formula is the unique affine-in-\(k\) spectrum fixed by the two anchors \(s_1=d_\gamma\) (typical points, rigorous) and \(s_3=2\) (the three-star value, whose lower bound \(\dim S_3\ge2\) is proved by Bhatia, Gwynne, and Harper and whose sharpness is their conjecture), so it compresses an entire geodesic-branching spectrum into the single unknown \(d_\gamma\) and predicts a maximal multiplicity \(k_{\max}\approx3+4/(d_\gamma-2)\).  A proof route extends the Lipschitz-function lower-bound technology to upper bounds.  The nearest results are the general-\(\gamma\) three-star lower bound of Bhatia, Gwynne, and Harper~\cite{BGH26} and the strong-confluence framework of Bhatia and Kavvadias~\cite{BhatiaKavvadias25}; the interpolation itself is the proposed content, an attribution carried in the statement.  A first decisive theorem would be \(\dim S_2\) at one non-Brownian \(\gamma\).  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the formula reproduces the Brownian spectrum \(5-k\) and the \(d_\gamma\downarrow2\) limit.  A counterexample would be a computed \(\dim S_2\) or \(\dim S_4\) off the affine line.

\begin{conjecture}[Exponential scale-mixing of the radial metric residual]\label{am2}
Let \(h\) be a whole-plane GFF with \(h_1(0)=0\), \(h_r(0)\) its circle average, and \(X_t=\log[e^{\xi Qt-\xi h_{e^{-t}}(0)}D_h(0,\partial B(0,e^{-t}))]\), a process stationary in \(t\) by scale covariance.  Its strong-mixing coefficient satisfies \(\alpha_X(s)\le Ce^{-cs}\), and \(\sup_t\Pr[\sup_{0\le u\le1}|X_{t+u}|>x]\le Ce^{-cx}\); consequently \(\sup_{0\le u\le T}|X_u|=O(\log T)\) almost surely and the radial log-distance process has the Brownian functional scaling limit and law of the iterated logarithm.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Stationarity of \(X_t\) is exact from Weyl scaling; the conjectural content is quantitative decorrelation across logarithmic scales and a pathwise envelope sharp enough to transfer Brownian functional and iterated-logarithm behaviour uniformly in time.  A proof route seeks a spectral gap for a scale-shift Markov dynamics on the field.  The nearest result is the metric-growth stationarity of Dub\'edat and Falconet~\cite{DubedatFalconet23}.  A first decisive theorem would be polynomial mixing.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, finite Liouville first-passage-percolation diagnostics matched the Weyl field-response coefficient and showed no residual growth on the tested scales.  A counterexample would be polynomially decaying scale correlations or excursions of order \(\sqrt t\).

\begin{conjecture}[Quantum-cone metric-ball shell functional CLT]\label{am3}
For a rooted LQG surface let \(V(r)=\mu_h(B_{D_h}(z,r))\) and \(Y_j^{(r)}=-\log[V(re^{-(j+1)})/V(re^{-j})]\).  There is a stationary inward-scale version \((Y_j^{\mathrm{cone}})\) for the rooted \(\gamma\)-quantum-cone tangent law that is exponentially \(\alpha\)-mixing with \(\mathbb E Y_0^{\mathrm{cone}}=d_\gamma\) and finite positive asymptotic variance \(\sigma_\gamma^2\), with \(\tfrac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j<nt}(Y_j^{\mathrm{cone}}-d_\gamma)\Rightarrow\sigma_\gamma B_t\) in \(D([0,1])\); and for any finite-volume surface rooted at a quantum-typical point, \((Y_j^{(r)})_{j\in J}\Rightarrow(Y_j^{\mathrm{cone}})_{j\in J}\) as \(r\downarrow0\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The law upgrades the first-order volume exponent to a second-order Gaussian expansion \(\log V(r)=d_\gamma\log r+\sigma_\gamma B_{\log(1/r)}+o_{\Pr}(\sqrt{\log(1/r)})\), the metric-ball analogue of logarithmic-scale central limit theorems in multiplicative chaos.  A proof route establishes exponential mixing of annular scale blocks via the GFF Markov property.  The nearest result is the all-moment volume control of Ang, Falconet, and Sun~\cite{AngFalconetSun20}.  A first decisive theorem would be the finite-variance central limit theorem for a single scale increment.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, finite LFPP under-resolves the exponent (slope near \(2.3\) against \(4\)), a bias reported there.  A counterexample would be power-law shell covariance or a non-Gaussian stable limit.

\begin{conjecture}[Pointwise sfSLE metric H\"older exponent]\label{am4}
Let \(\eta\) be a whole-plane space-filling \(\mathrm{SLE}_{16/\gamma^2}\) independent of \(h\), parameterized by LQG area, \(\mu_h(\eta([s,t]))=t-s\).  For Lebesgue-almost every \(t\), almost surely \(\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\log\operatorname{diam}_{D_h}\eta([t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon])/\log\varepsilon=1/d_\gamma\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
An interval of area \(2\varepsilon\) explores, at a typical time, a cell of \(D_h\)-diameter \(\varepsilon^{1/d_\gamma}\); the conjecture asserts the pointwise metric exponent exists and equals the dimensional value almost everywhere, a differentiation statement for the mating-of-trees parameterization.  A proof route combines the Minkowski-content identification of \(\mu_h\) with two-sided diameter control.  The nearest result is the metric H\"older continuity and Minkowski content of Gwynne and Sung~\cite{GwynneSung24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the exponent in probability at a typical time.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a discrete mated-CRT surrogate gave the reciprocal product \(\widehat d\,\widehat H\approx1\) despite finite-size bias in each factor.  A counterexample would be a genuine multifractal diameter spectrum at typical times.

\begin{conjecture}[Stable-CSBP perimeter universality]\label{am5}
For every \(\gamma\in(0,2)\), filled metric balls in a whole-plane or quantum-cone \(\gamma\)-LQG surface admit a canonical scalar outer-boundary length \(L_h^\gamma(r)\), measurable from the metric-measure surface, with \(L_{h+c}^\gamma(e^{\xi c}r)=e^{\gamma c/2}L_h^\gamma(r)\).  Under reverse metric-radius exploration, after the natural normalization and excursion/Doob conditioning, the perimeter process is the conditioned/time-reversed stable continuous-state branching process of index \(\alpha_\gamma=1+2/d_\gamma\).
\end{conjecture}
