\paragraph{Significance.}
The index is forced by self-similarity: a stable CSBP of index \(\alpha\) has mass scaling like time\(^{1/(\alpha-1)}\), and matching the proposed perimeter dimension \(d_\gamma/2\) gives \(\alpha_\gamma=1+2/d_\gamma\), exactly \(\tfrac32\) at \(d_\gamma=4\).  The consequential claim is that a scalar perimeter closes the growth dynamics Markovianly for every \(\gamma\), a hidden integrable skeleton.  A proof route constructs the boundary length from the trace field and identifies its generator.  The nearest results are the open filled-ball boundary-length problem of Gwynne and Miller~\cite{GwynneMiller21} and the boundary-trace stationarity of~\cite{DubedatFalconet23}; the index and scalar process are the proposed content, an attribution carried in the statement.  A first decisive theorem would be existence of the canonical length.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the index reduces to \(\tfrac32\) at the Brownian point via Proposition~\ref{am:triangle}.  A counterexample would be a perimeter process that is not Markov in its scalar length.

\begin{conjecture}[Linear confluence response]\label{am6}
On a unit-area \(\gamma\)-LQG sphere sample \(z,x,y\) independently from \(\mu_h\).  On \(\{D_h(x,y)\le\varepsilon\}\) let \(b\) be the terminal point of the common initial segment of the geodesics from \(z\) to \(x,y\), \(\Delta=\max\{D_h(b,x),D_h(b,y)\}\), and \(C_\varepsilon=\Delta/D_h(x,y)\).  Conditioned on \(D_h(x,y)\le\varepsilon\), \(C_\varepsilon\) converges in law as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) to a nondegenerate \(C_\gamma\in(0,\infty)\) with finite moments in a neighbourhood of zero.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Strong confluence gives only an \(\varepsilon^{1-o(1)}\) defect scale; the conjecture sharpens it to an exactly linear tangent law with a universal nondegenerate ratio, the geodesic analogue of a tangent distribution for the typical geodesic tree.  A proof route seeks a scaling limit of the branch geometry at conditioned typical points.  The nearest result is the strong confluence of Bhatia and Kavvadias~\cite{BhatiaKavvadias25}.  A first decisive theorem would be tightness of \(C_\varepsilon\) away from \(0\) and \(\infty\).  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a finite LFPP confluence diagnostic gave a log-log slope near \(1.04\) after a max/min implementation fix, a finite-grid check only.  A counterexample would be \(C_\varepsilon\to0,\infty\) or a nonlinear defect exponent.

\begin{conjecture}[Filled metric-ball outer boundary dimension]\label{am7}
Let \(h\) be a whole-plane GFF and \(B_{D_h}^{\infty,\bullet}(0,r)\) the filled metric ball targeted at infinity.  For every deterministic \(r>0\), almost surely \(\dim_{\mathrm H}^{D_h}\partial B_{D_h}^{\infty,\bullet}(0,r)=d_\gamma/2\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The ordinary ball boundary has dimension \(d_\gamma-1\); the filled outer boundary is conjectured to carry the boundary-length scaling dimension \(d_\gamma/2\), the same scalar appearing in the perimeter index of Conjecture~\ref{am5} and the roughness exponent of Conjecture~\ref{am8}, so three otherwise different observables encode one number.  A proof route relates the outer boundary to the boundary length of Conjecture~\ref{am5}.  The nearest results are the ordinary boundary dimension of Gwynne~\cite{Gwynne20} and the open-problem discussion of Gwynne and Miller~\cite{GwynneMiller21}.  A first decisive theorem would be one rigorous non-Brownian estimate.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the formula returns \(2\) at \(d_\gamma=4\) and is exactly compatible with the scaling triangle.  A counterexample would be a non-Brownian dimension off \(d_\gamma/2\).

\begin{conjecture}[Fractional-Brownian tangent of distance profiles]\label{am8}
Let \(\mathcal D\) be a finite-boundary-length \(\gamma\)-LQG disk, \(z\) sampled from \(\mu_h\), and \(X(u)=D_h(z,\partial(u))\) the distance to the boundary point at length coordinate \(u\).  At boundary-length-almost every \(u_0\) there is \(\sigma_\gamma>0\) with \(\varepsilon^{-H_\gamma}[X(u_0+\varepsilon t)-X(u_0)]\Rightarrow\sigma_\gamma B_{H_\gamma}(t)\), \(H_\gamma=2/d_\gamma\), in local uniform topology, where \(B_H\) is two-sided fractional Brownian motion.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The variation theorem forces the roughness exponent \(H_\gamma=2/d_\gamma\); the new content is that the local tangent is Gaussian fractional Brownian motion, persistent for \(d_\gamma<4\) and antipersistent for \(d_\gamma>4\), so matter coupling appears as sign-changing increment correlations in a boundary observable.  A proof route upgrades the \(d_\gamma/2\)-variation to a self-similar tangent law.  The nearest result is the \(d_\gamma/2\)-variation of distance profiles of Bhatia~\cite{Bhatia25}.  A first decisive theorem would be the Brownian case \(H=\tfrac12\) at \(\gamma=\sqrt{8/3}\).  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a finite LFPP structure-function fit gave a smoother-than-Brownian exponent, reported as pre-asymptotic bias.  A counterexample would be a non-Gaussian or non-fBm tangent with the correct exponent.

\section{Spectral convexity in Liouville conformal field theory}

\begin{conjecture}[Sphere spectral monotone likelihood ratio]\label{am9}
Fix \(b>0\), four equal real external charges \(Q_b/3\le a<Q_b/2\), and \(0<z_1<z_2\le\tfrac12\).  The OPE-normalized sphere block \(\mathcal F_P(z)\) is nonzero on this domain and \(E=P^2\mapsto|\mathcal F_{\sqrt E}(z_2)|^2/|\mathcal F_{\sqrt E}(z_1)|^2\) is strictly increasing; equivalently \(\partial_E\partial_z\log|\mathcal F_{\sqrt E}(z)|^2>0\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is a total-positivity statement: moving the cross-ratio toward the centre of moduli space shifts spectral weight monotonically toward larger internal dimensions in the likelihood-ratio order, far stronger than pointwise positivity.  The leading \(z^{\Delta}\) factor sets the sign; the conjecture is that Virasoro descendants never overturn it.  A proof route controls the descendant series through the Zamolodchikov recursion.  The nearest work is the block/recursion and positivity literature; no monotone-likelihood-ratio statement in the internal momentum was located.  A first decisive theorem would be the global \(SL(2)\) block, where the sign is explicit.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the global-block limit gave strictly positive discrete log-ratio slopes in every tested case; the full-block statement is tested only in that limit.  A counterexample would be two internal momenta whose likelihood ratio reverses.

\begin{conjecture}[Four-point spectral log-concavity]\label{am10}
For \(b>0\), \(Q_b/3\le a<Q_b/2\), \(0<z\le\tfrac12\), and \(P>0\), the principal-series magnitude \(I_z(P)=|C_b(a,a,\tfrac{Q_b}2+iP)|^2|\mathcal F_P(z)|^2\) is positive and \(\tfrac{d^2}{dP^2}\log I_z(P)<0\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Strict log-concavity gives the four-point spectral density a unique mode and rules out shoulders or competing saddles in the interior chamber, turning bootstrap questions into convex-analysis problems.  It combines the DOZZ curvature of Conjecture~\ref{ak1} with the block contribution, requiring only their sum to stay negative.  A proof route adds the Barnes-kernel curvature of Part~XX to a descendant Hessian bound.  The nearest boundary is the DOZZ formula of Kupiainen, Rhodes, and Vargas~\cite{KRV20}; the interior chamber is necessary, the broader version being falsified at \(b=1\), \(a=0.55\).  A first decisive theorem would be the \(b=1\) case.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact-\(\Upsilon_b\) quadrature combined with the global block gave negative curvature throughout the chamber and positive curvature at the excluded sub-chamber charge; the block contribution is tested only in the global limit.  A counterexample would be positive curvature at a regular interior point.

\begin{conjecture}[Torus thermal spectral monotone likelihood ratio]\label{am11}
Fix \(b>0\) and a real external charge \(Q_b/3\le a<Q_b/2\), and use the full torus block \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm{tor}}_{a,P}(q)=q^{\Delta(P)-c/24}\mathcal H^{\mathrm{tor}}_{a,P}(q)\) with \(q=e^{-2\pi\beta}\).  For \(\beta_2>\beta_1\) the blocks are nonzero for \(P>0\) and \(E=P^2\mapsto|\mathcal F^{\mathrm{tor}}_{a,\sqrt E}(q_2)|^2/|\mathcal F^{\mathrm{tor}}_{a,\sqrt E}(q_1)|^2\) is strictly decreasing.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Making the torus colder suppresses higher internal Liouville momentum in the strongest one-dimensional likelihood-ratio sense; the bare Boltzmann factor supplies the sign and the conjecture is that the descendant series preserves it, giving a family of thermal correlation inequalities for non-rational CFT.  A proof route controls the toric descendant factor \(\mathcal H^{\mathrm{tor}}\).  The nearest result is the probabilistic toric-block construction of Ghosal, Remy, Sun, and Sun~\cite{GRSS24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the global torus block.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the global torus-descendant proxy gave negative log-ratio slopes at every tested temperature pair and charge; the full-block statement is tested only in that limit.  A counterexample would be a reversal near \(q\to1\), where descendant entropy is strongest.

\begin{conjecture}[Multipoint joint spectral log-concavity of the modulus]\label{am12}
For \(n\ge5\), real moduli \(\mathbf z\) in a positive OPE cell, equal physical external charges \(Q_b/3\le a<Q_b/2\), and internal momenta \(\mathbf P=(P_1,\dots,P_{n-3})\) on the principal series, let \(K_{\mathbf z}(\mathbf P)\) be the standard-normalized comb sewing kernel (product of DOZZ vertices and the multipoint block) and \(\Phi_{\mathbf z}(\mathbf P)=\log|K_{\mathbf z}(\mathbf P)|\).  Then \(K_{\mathbf z}\ne0\) and \(\nabla^2_{\mathbf P}\Phi_{\mathbf z}\prec0\) for every \(P_j>0\).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
This is the multivariate modulus analogue of Conjecture~\ref{am10}: a unique joint spectral maximum with no flat or competing directions in the comb channels, giving global convex control on the size of multipoint sewing contributions.  A proof route seeks diagonal dominance or an M-matrix structure in the comb graph after a coordinate change.  The nearest result is the multipoint WKB analysis of Artemev and Khromov~\cite{ArtemevKhromov26}.  A first decisive theorem would be the five-point case at \(b=1\).  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a five-point coupled proxy from exact \(b=1\) DOZZ vertices and global blocks had negative-definite finite-difference Hessians on the tested interior grid; the full-block statement is tested only in that limit.  A counterexample would be a positive Hessian direction of \(\log|K_{\mathbf z}|\) in the chamber.

\section{Nesting in conformal loop ensembles}

\begin{conjecture}[Quantum-cone nesting area-ratio functional CLT]\label{am13}
Let \(\kappa\in(8/3,4)\cup(4,8)\) with \(\gamma=\sqrt\kappa\) for \(\kappa<4\) and \(\gamma=4/\sqrt\kappa\) for \(\kappa>4\).  For nested \(\mathrm{CLE}_\kappa\) around the marked point of the matched \(\gamma\)-quantum-cone tangent law, with \(U_n\) the successive marked components, \(A_n=\mu_h(U_n)\), and \(Y_n=-\log(A_{n+1}/A_n)\): the sequence \((Y_n)\) admits a stationary version that is exponentially \(\alpha\)-mixing with analytic scaled cumulant generating function near zero and positive asymptotic variance, so \(\tfrac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j<nt}(Y_j-v_{\gamma,\kappa})\Rightarrow\sigma_{\gamma,\kappa}B_t\) in \(D([0,1])\); and finite-volume deep-nesting increments converge to this stationary law.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Euclidean CLE nesting has a renewal structure in logarithmic conformal radius; the conjecture asserts the analogous Gaussian second-order law for successive ratios of genuine continuum LQG areas, which mix the radial mode, multiplicative chaos, and random boundary geometry.  A proof route seeks regeneration at nesting scales with quantitative absolute continuity of area increments.  The nearest results are the CLE nesting theory of Miller, Watson, and Wilson~\cite{MWW} and the LQG-CLE reweighting of Holden and Lehmkuehler~\cite{HoldenLehmkuehler24}; the critical point \(\kappa=4\) is excluded.  A first decisive theorem would be the central limit theorem for the stationary chain.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a structural surrogate coupling exact CLE conformal-radius cumulants to a radial-GFF area approximation showed skewness and excess kurtosis decaying toward zero with depth.  A counterexample would be long-range dependence or a non-Gaussian stable partial-sum limit.


\part{Hydrodynamic limits of interacting particle systems}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The fifteen conjectures below propose hydrodynamic scaling limits for interacting particle systems whose microscopic rules carry a new structural ingredient: an endogenous local jump index, refreshed or fatigued environments, non-Markovian renewal clocks, singular reaction surfaces, finite crossing budgets, shared common noise, odd multi-species transport, and moving or storing membranes.  They fall in five groups (Conjectures~\ref{an1} to~\ref{an3}, \ref{an4} to~\ref{an6}, \ref{an7} to~\ref{an9}, \ref{an10} to~\ref{an12}, and~\ref{an13} to~\ref{an15}).  Each states a microscopic model, the conjectured limiting equation, its conserved quantities, the critical scaling that makes the new mechanism survive, and a route to disproof.  These are scaling-limit statements about continuum PDE or SPDE,, and every one; the diagnostics test event-count scalings, conservation, reduced linearizations, or exact ODE reductions, never the limit theorem.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{an:reductions}: exact mass conservation of the limiting equations, the fatigue mobility-budget identity, the perturbative self-arrest residual, and the critical event-count exponents.  Four statements have explicit high overlaps with prior work, since a closely related continuum object or one-particle input appeared in 2025--2026 work: the Markov-switching Robin equation of Colantoni~\cite{Colantoni26} (Conjecture~\ref{an10}), the scalar vorticity/odd-diffusion exclusion of De Carlo, Gabrielli, and Gon\c calves~\cite{DeCarloGabrielliGoncalves25} (Conjecture~\ref{an11}), the critical-percolation random-walk scaling limit of Dankovic, Markering, Miller, and Yuan~\cite{DankovicMMY26} (Conjecture~\ref{an13}), and the finite-reservoir Wentzell theorem of Franco, Franco, and Gon\c calves~\cite{FrancoFrancoGoncalves26} (Conjecture~\ref{an15}); for these the novel content is the exact microscopic derivation and the specific interior/two-sided/multi-species structure, not the limiting object itself.

Throughout, $\eta$ is an exclusion configuration on the discrete torus $\mathbb T_N$ or on $\mathbb R$, $\rho$ the limiting density, and time is diffusively scaled unless stated otherwise.  Objects specific to a single conjecture are defined in its statement.

\begin{proposition}[Conservation, mobility budget, self-arrest residual, and critical counts]\label{an:reductions}
{\rm(i)} Each limiting equation displayed below conserves the relevant total mass (for multi-species models, each color mass): integrating the gain--loss or divergence form and interchanging dummy variables cancels the flux.  {\rm(ii)} For the fatigue ODE $\dot a=c(1-a)^p$ with $c=2\rho(1-\rho)>0$, the conductance reaches zero in finite time iff $p<1$, with $t_{\rm hit}=1/(c(1-p))$, while the integrated mobility $\int_0^\infty(1-a)^p\,dt=1/c$ is finite for every $p$.  {\rm(iii)} For the occupation-deepened trap system linearized about $\rho=\bar\rho$ with $b=0$, the first-order perturbation solves $\partial_tv=e^{-a\bar\rho t}\Delta v$, so $v(t)=e^{\tau(t)\Delta}v_0$ with $\tau(t)=(1-e^{-a\bar\rho t})/(a\bar\rho)$ and $v_\infty=e^{\Delta/(a\bar\rho)}v_0$, generally nonzero.  {\rm(iv)} A codimension-one reaction surface at generator rate $N^\theta$ contributes at order $N^{\theta-1}$, critical at $\theta=1$; and a membrane of step $N^a$, move rate $N^{-b}$, and slow conductance $\alpha/N$ has order-one Brownian motion, healing length, and slow activity per dwell simultaneously iff $b=2a$ and $a=\tfrac12$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
{\rm(i)} is the standard conservative-form cancellation.  {\rm(ii)} integrates $\dot a=c(1-a)^p$ directly: $(1-a)^{1-p}$ is linear in $t$ for $p\ne1$, giving finite $t_{\rm hit}$ iff $p<1$, and $\int(1-a)^p\,dt=\int_0^1 da/c=1/c$.  {\rm(iii)} solves the linear nonautonomous heat equation by the time change $\tau(t)=\int_0^te^{-a\bar\rho s}\,ds$.  {\rm(iv)} is the event-count balance: $N^{d-1}$ surface sites times rate $N^\theta$ times mass change $N^{-d}$ is $N^{\theta-1}$; and $N^2\cdot N^{-b}(N^a/N)^2=N^{2a-b}$, a dwell of $N^b$ diffuses $N^{b/2}$, and slow ringing per dwell is $\alpha N^{b-1}$, jointly order one exactly at $b=2a=1$.
\end{proof}

\section{Density-adaptive and refreshed exclusion hydrodynamics}

\begin{conjecture}[Density-adaptive L\'evy exclusion]\label{an1}
On $\mathbb T_N$ let $r_x^N(\eta)$ be the mean occupation in a block of radius $\ell_N$ with $\ell_N\to\infty$, $\ell_N/N\to0$, and $\log N/\sqrt{\ell_N}\to0$, and let $\alpha:[0,1]\to[\alpha_-,\alpha_+]\subset(0,2)$ be $C^1$.  A particle at $x$ jumps to a vacant $y$ at rate $N^{\alpha(r_x^N)}c(\alpha(r_x^N))|y-x|_N^{-1-\alpha(r_x^N)}$.  For smooth profiles bounded away from $0,1$ the empirical density converges to the conservative variable-order gain--loss equation
\[
\partial_t\rho(u)=\mathrm{PV}\!\int_{\mathbb T}\bigl[K_{\alpha(\rho(v))}(u-v)\rho(v)(1-\rho(u))-K_{\alpha(\rho(u))}(v-u)\rho(u)(1-\rho(v))\bigr]\,dv.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The spatial stable index is an endogenous local-density field, so the macroscopic operator has a state-dependent order; the stability condition $\log N/\sqrt{\ell_N}\to0$ is necessary because a vanishing block-density error otherwise creates an order-one multiplicative rate error through $N^{\alpha(r)}$.  A proof route establishes the replacement lemma for the source-dependent exponent with exponential control of the logarithmic amplification.  The nearest results are the variable-order fractional kinetics of Kolokoltsov and Troeva~\cite{KolokoltsovTroeva22} and the fractional porous-medium hydrodynamics of Cardoso, de Paula, and Gon\c calves~\cite{CardosoDePaula23}.  A first decisive theorem would be the case $\alpha_+<1$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the amplification diagnostic $\log N/\sqrt{\ell_N}$ decreased with $N$ and lower density gave longer accepted jumps.  A counterexample would be a surviving logarithmic renormalization or a different symmetrized operator.

\begin{conjecture}[Refreshing heavy traps: crossover trichotomy]\label{an2}
Start from a reversible heavy-trap exclusion model with static anomalous clock $\theta_N$ and index $\beta\in(0,1)$, refresh each trap at rate $q_N$ independently of the particles, and set $\lambda_N=q_N\theta_N$.  If $\lambda_N\to0$ the static fractional-kinetics limit persists; if $\lambda_N\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$ the hydrodynamics is governed by a model-dependent renewal/Bernstein symbol $\psi_\lambda(s)$ with $\psi_0(s)=cs^\beta$ and $\psi_\lambda(s)\sim m_\lambda s$ as $s\downarrow0$; if $\lambda_N\to\infty$ the limit is ordinary diffusion after effective-diffusivity renormalization.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Refreshing a trapped environment interpolates between anomalous and diffusive transport, but the critical symbol is model-dependent rather than universally tempered-stable; the theorem-sized problem is to identify $\psi_\lambda$ from the microscopic refreshed process.  A proof route computes the one-particle resolvent of the refreshed renewal clock.  The nearest results are static Bouchaud-trap fractional kinetics and dynamic-random-environment hydrodynamics.  A first decisive theorem would be the $\lambda\to0$ persistence.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a generic heavy waiting time interrupted by exponential refresh showed the truncated mean waiting time falling monotonically with refresh rate, supporting the crossover mechanism without a fixed symbol.  A counterexample would be a universal symbol independent of the refresh rule.

\begin{conjecture}[Critical sparse shortcuts add a teleportation operator]\label{an3}
Let nearest-neighbor SSEP run on $\mathbb T_N$ at rate $N^2$, and add $M_N$ macroscopic shortcut edges ringing at rate $\kappa$, with $M_N/N\to\lambda/2$ and endpoint-pair measure converging to uniform.  The empirical density converges to $\partial_t\rho=D\partial_{uu}\rho+\kappa\lambda(\bar\rho-\rho)$, with $\bar\rho=\int_{\mathbb T}\rho$; for a nonuniform endpoint kernel the nonlocal term becomes the corresponding conservative jump operator.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Each shortcut moves $O(N^{-1})$ mass and there are $O(N)$ of them, so their aggregate is an order-one nonlocal mean-field damping toward the spatial average, a Euclidean local-plus-teleportation hydrodynamic crossover.  A proof route uses the exact local-equilibrium cancellation $\rho(u)(1-\rho(v))-\rho(v)(1-\rho(u))=\rho(u)-\rho(v)$.  The nearest literature concerns random walks on small-world graphs and IPS on sparse graphs, not this local-plus-$O(N)$-shortcut limit.  A first decisive theorem would be the annealed rewiring case.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the first Fourier mode decayed at the predicted mean-field rate.  A counterexample would be a different damping coefficient or a non-mean-field limit.

\section{Renewal exclusion, fatigue, and boundary memory}

\begin{conjecture}[Crowding-renormalized successful-reset renewal exclusion]\label{an4}
Let a particle of age $a$ attempt jumps with hazard $\beta/(a+a_0)$, $0<\beta<1$, resetting its age only after a successful jump.  In dimension $d\ge2$, linearizing about a homogeneous equilibrium $\rho_*$, on the clock $t_{N,*}=N^{2/\gamma(\rho_*)}$ with $\gamma(\rho_*)=\beta(1-\rho_*)$ the density perturbation converges to the fractional diffusion $\partial_t^{\gamma(\rho_*)}u=D(\rho_*)\Delta u$; a genuinely nonconstant profile admits no single global polynomial clock, requiring a variable-order-in-time renewal kernel.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Because a jump resets the age only on success and a vacancy is seen with probability $1-\rho_*$, the successful-event hazard is thinned to $\beta(1-\rho_*)/(a+a_0)$, so the hard-core constraint changes the temporal universality exponent, not merely a diffusivity.  A proof route Markovizes the system with an empirical age measure and integrates the age out.  The nearest results are non-Markovian exclusion models and variable-order temporal CTRW equations.  A first decisive theorem would be the linearized fractional response at fixed $\rho_*$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, fitted tail exponents of the thinned-hazard proxy matched $\beta(1-\rho_*)$ at densities $0.1,0.4,0.7$ to $0.013$.  A counterexample would be restoration of the isolated exponent $\beta$ by decorrelation of the environment seen by old particles.

\begin{conjecture}[Activity-fatigued conductances]\label{an5}
Attach damage $a_b(t)\in[0,1]$ to each bond, exchanging symmetrically at rate $N^2(1-a_b)^p$, with $a_b$ increased by $N^{-2}$ at each successful crossing (a crossing budget of order $N^2$).  Writing $g(a)=(1-a)^p$, the damage field then evolves macroscopically as $\partial_ta=2g(a)\rho(1-\rho)$, this law derived from the increment rule rather than imposed.  The coupled hydrodynamic limit is $\partial_t\rho=\partial_u(g(a)\partial_u\rho)$, $\partial_ta=2g(a)\rho(1-\rho)$, with finite-time loss of ellipticity at $p<1$ but finite integrated mobility for every $p$, so some smooth nonconstant data retain nonconstant long-time limits.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Activity damages the medium it flows through, and the sharp $p=1$ transition governs finite-time loss of ellipticity while the finite total diffusive budget can freeze non-equilibrium profiles for a broader range of $p$.  A proof route proves finite-time hydrodynamics up to the first degeneracy, then controls the self-consistent damage field.  The nearest result is the history-dependent substrate exclusion of Schulz, Kolomeisky, and Frey~\cite{SchulzKolomeiskyFrey11}.  A first decisive theorem would be finite-time hydrodynamics up to degeneracy.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the exact fatigue ODE of Proposition~\ref{an:reductions} confirmed finite hitting iff $p<1$ and integrated mobility $1/(2\rho(1-\rho))$.  A counterexample would be complete homogenization for all nonconstant data.

\begin{conjecture}[Common heavy-tailed boundary clock: random Stieltjes boundary law]\label{an6}
Let a single heavy-tailed renewal process control all left-boundary updates, scaled so that $N^{-1}R_N(N^2t)\Rightarrow\kappa_LE_t^L$ with $E^L$ an inverse-$\gamma$-stable clock, and analogously on the right.  The bulk solves $\partial_t\rho=\partial_{uu}\rho$, but the boundary fluxes are singular random Stieltjes measures: in weak form $d\langle\rho_t,G\rangle=\langle\rho_t,G''\rangle dt+\kappa_LG(0)[\alpha-\rho_t(0)]dE_t^L+\kappa_RG(1)[\beta_R-\rho_t(1)]dE_t^R$, remaining random after averaging over the clocks.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A single shared heavy-tailed clock does not self-average---its inverse-stable limit is genuinely random---so the correct object is a random-measure-driven boundary law, not the deterministic fractional Robin condition of a naive law of large numbers.  A proof route proves joint convergence of the boundary counting process and the empirical field.  The nearest topics are inverse-stable time changes and fractional boundary PDE, whose ingredients are individually classical.  A first decisive theorem would be the one-sided clock.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the coefficient of variation of the single renewal clock stayed near $0.67$ and did not vanish, while averaging $36$ clocks drove it to $0.11$, the signature that forced the random-clock statement.  A counterexample would be a self-averaging deterministic boundary law from one shared clock.

\section{Catalysts, mixed clocks, and crossing budgets}

\begin{conjecture}[Codimension-one nonlinear catalyst transmission law]\label{an7}
Let $\Sigma_N$ approximate a smooth hypersurface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb T^d$ with bulk SSEP at rate $N^2$ and catalyst birth/death flips at generator rate $N^\theta$ with reaction $R(r)=b(r)(1-r)-d(r)r$.  The critical exponent is $\theta=1$, at which $\partial_t\rho=\Delta\rho$ off $\Sigma$ with continuous trace and derivative jump $[\partial_n\rho]_\Sigma=-R(\rho|_\Sigma)$; for $\theta<1$ the catalyst disappears and for $\theta>1$ a stable zero of $R$ pins the trace.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The lower-dimensional set carries no independent conserved density; it acts as a singular nonlinear reaction measure, a codimension-one transmission law.  A proof route is the surface event-count balance of Proposition~\ref{an:reductions} with a boundary replacement estimate.  The nearest result is the field-road bulk/surface SSEP of Alfaro, Mourragui, and Treton~\cite{AlfaroMourraguiTreton24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the linear-reaction case.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the catalyst contribution scaled as $N^{\theta-1}$, reproducing the $N^{-1/2},1,N^{1/2}$ regimes at $\theta=\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32$.  A counterexample would be a different critical exponent or a persistent independent surface density.

\begin{conjecture}[Mixed-clock two-species Maxwell--Stefan hydrodynamics]\label{an8}
Let species A use exponential attempt clocks and species B use i.i.d.\ heavy-tailed attempt clocks of index $\gamma\in(0,1)$, reset after every attempt.  Observed on time $N^{2/\gamma}$ with A's microscopic rate $N^{2-2/\gamma}$, both species stay hydrodynamically visible, and around a homogeneous composition the linearized law is the mixed-order Maxwell--Stefan system $s\,\widehat{\delta a}-\delta a_0=-k^2(D_*\widehat{\delta}\,)_A$, $s^\gamma\widehat{\delta b}-s^{\gamma-1}\delta b_0=-k^2(D_*\widehat{\delta}\,)_B$ with non-diagonal exclusion cross-diffusion $D_*$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The two species carry different temporal universality classes coupled by hard-core exclusion, so the relaxation modes are roots of a genuinely hybrid matrix dispersion relation, not one ordinary plus one independent fractional mode.  A proof route uses subexponential-tail stability of the attempt-reset clock under geometric blocking, which leaves the index $\gamma$ unchanged.  The nearest results are two-species exclusion cross-diffusion~\cite{Sasada09} and bidirectional non-Markovian exclusion.  A first decisive theorem would be the linearized dispersion relation.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, fitted successful-wait exponents stayed at $\gamma$ across vacancy probabilities and the clock-balance identity held to machine precision.  A counterexample would be a blocked-clock index shift or a diagonal decoupling.

\begin{conjecture}[Finite crossing-budget membrane: endogenous stopping-time transition]\label{an9}
Give a critical slow bond (microscopic rate $\alpha/N$) a budget $B_N=\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$ of successful exchanges, after which its rate is zero forever.  With unsigned local activity $A(r_-,r_+)=r_-(1-r_+)+r_+(1-r_-)$, the normalized success count satisfies $S_N(t)/N\to\alpha\int_0^tA(\rho(s,0^-),\rho(s,0^+))\,ds$, and the density obeys the critical Robin transmission law before the exhaustion time $\tau=\inf\{t:\alpha\int_0^tA\ge\kappa\}$ and reflecting conditions after, so the PDE changes type at an endogenous stopping time.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A cumulative successful-crossing capacity permanently switches a critical membrane, so the macroscopic boundary condition changes type at a stopping time generated by the integrated local activity---a genuinely endogenous phase transition.  A proof route enlarges the slow-bond replacement theory by the normalized success count and applies a continuous-mapping theorem for the hitting time.  The nearest machinery is the classical slow-bond Robin transition, which lacks the endogenous stopping mechanism.  A first decisive theorem is the joint law of large numbers up to exhaustion.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, mean exhaustion times concentrated on the predicted value with standard deviation shrinking as $N^{-1/2}$.  A counterexample would be a signed-current rather than unsigned-activity exhaustion law.

\section{Common noise, odd transport, and self-generated arrest}

\begin{conjecture}[Telegraph-modulated critical membrane]\label{an10}
Let a single two-state Markov chain $Z_t\in\{0,1\}$, converging on diffusive time to a finite-rate telegraph process, multiply a critical slow bond's rate, $\alpha Z_t/N$.  Conditional on $Z$, the density converges to the heat equation with time-dependent Robin coefficient $\alpha Z_t$, so the empirical density converges jointly with $Z$ to a random hydrodynamic limit; the fast-switch regime converges to the averaged Robin law.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A single finite-dimensional common noise survives a conservative hydrodynamic limit because there is no spatial averaging mechanism to replace $Z_t$ by its mean at order-one switching.  A proof route is a quenched hydrodynamic limit conditional on the telegraph path.  \emph{Priority.}  The continuum Markov-switching Robin equation is already established by Colantoni~\cite{Colantoni26}, so the novel content is only the exclusion derivation of that object and the fast-switch averaging; the statement has this high overlap with prior work.  A first decisive theorem would be the quenched limit at fixed switching rate.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a macroscopic gap proxy had substantial randomness at finite switching rate, averaging out only as switching accelerated.  A counterexample would be self-averaging of the common noise in the conservative limit.

\begin{conjecture}[Multi-species chiral-vorticity odd cross-diffusion]\label{an11}
Use at least two conserved colors plus vacancies, with symmetric color-vacancy exchanges and plaquette rotations at rates $c_\pm(\xi)=N^2c_0[1\pm\varepsilon\Phi(\mathcal N(\xi))]$ depending only on the rotation-invariant plaquette composition $\mathcal N(\xi)$, so grand-canonical product color measures are invariant.  The diffusive hydrodynamics is $\partial_tr_i=\nabla\cdot\sum_j[D^S_{ij}(r)\nabla r_j+D^O_{ij}(r)R\nabla r_j]$ with $R$ rotation by $\pi/2$ and a composition-dependent odd cross matrix $D^O$ that changes sign with $\varepsilon$ and affects individual density equations.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The genuinely new requirement is a density-changing odd \emph{cross} sector, $\nabla\cdot(D^O_{ij}(r)R\nabla r_j)=\nabla D^O_{ij}\cdot R\nabla r_j\ne0$, which needs composition dependence and cross-coupling, each color mass still conserved.  A proof route verifies the invariant product family, then computes the first nonzero odd cross Green--Kubo coefficient perturbatively.  \emph{Priority.}  The broad scalar odd/vorticity exclusion is already established by De Carlo, Gabrielli, and Gon\c calves~\cite{DeCarloGabrielliGoncalves25} (a scalar antisymmetric sector affects the current but not the density), and hard-core odd diffusion is known~\cite{Kalz22}; only the multi-species density-changing cross sector is claimed, a high overlap with prior work carried in the statement.  A first decisive theorem would be a nonzero odd cross coefficient at a symmetric composition.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a transverse species-1 current reversed sign with chirality while all color counts were exactly conserved.  A counterexample would be a vanishing density-changing odd cross sector for all admissible $\Phi$.

\begin{conjecture}[Perturbative self-generated arrest]\label{an12}
Attach trap depth $E_x(t)\ge0$ with symmetric bond rate $N^2\exp[-(E_x+E_{x+1})/2]$ and $dE_x/dt=a\eta_t(x)-bE_x$.  The finite-time limit is $\partial_t\rho=\partial_u(e^{-e}\partial_u\rho)$, $\partial_te=a\rho-be$; with $b=0$, linearizing about $\rho=\bar\rho$ gives residual $v_\infty=e^{\Delta/(a\bar\rho)}v_0$, so for small smooth mean-zero data the full nonlinear system converges to the nonconstant limit $\rho_\infty=\bar\rho+\epsilon e^{\Delta/(a\bar\rho)}v_0+O(\epsilon^2)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Occupation deepens the traps it sits in, and the finite total heat-time $\tau(\infty)=1/(a\bar\rho)$ freezes a residual nonconstant profile---a concrete, testable arrest expansion rather than a generic-arrest heuristic.  A proof route proves finite-time hydrodynamics with a positive conductance lower bound, then controls the nonlinear remainder in a weighted norm with finite time integral.  The nearest result is the history-dependent substrate exclusion of~\cite{SchulzKolomeiskyFrey11}.  A first decisive theorem is the finite-time coupled limit.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the conservative nonlinear PDE reproduced the linear residual fraction to four digits with mass error $10^{-16}$.  A counterexample would be complete relaxation despite the finite mobility budget.

\section{Critical geometry and moving membranes}

\begin{conjecture}[Critical-percolation exclusion transfer]\label{an13}
Let $(V_N,c_N,\mu_N)$ be the rescaled critical triangular-percolation graph sequence for which simple random walk converges quenched to the semigroup $P_t^\omega$ of CLE$_6$ Brownian motion on the limiting resistance space, with time normalization $a_N$.  Run SSEP on $V_N$ with the same conductances and time change.  If the initial color field converges to $\rho_0\mu^\omega$, then quenched $\pi_t^N\Rightarrow\rho_t\mu^\omega$ with $\rho_t=P_t^\omega\rho_0$, so exclusion produces no additional transport exponent beyond the one-particle normalization.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The conjecture transfers the one-particle scaling to the many-particle exclusion system on a critical random fractal where volume, resistance, and geometry are singular.  A proof route abstracts the transfer step: measured-Gromov/Dirichlet-form convergence of the walk plus exclusion local ergodicity in the same random geometry.  \emph{Priority.}  The one-particle scaling limit is now a theorem of Dankovic, Markering, Miller, and Yuan~\cite{DankovicMMY26}, so the remaining content is the exclusion-transfer step; the statement has this overlap with prior work.  A first decisive theorem would be local ergodicity uniform in critical bottlenecks.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, a random-walk proxy on the correct critical triangular model gave the expected mean-squared-displacement geometry.  A counterexample would be an additional slowdown exponent from exclusion correlations despite one-particle convergence.

\begin{conjecture}[Critically mobile slow membrane]\label{an14}
Let a distinguished slow bond of rate $\alpha/N$ move by microscopic distance $N^a$ at rate $N^{-b}$.  At the uniquely matched scaling $a=\tfrac12$, $b=1$ (step $\sqrt N$, move rate $N^{-1}$, conductance $\alpha/N$), the membrane path converges to Brownian motion and the density converges to a nontrivial random singular-interface heat flow conditional on that Brownian path; the membrane is not annealed away, and the exact moving-Robin generator is a sub-conjecture.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Three requirements---Brownian macroscopic motion, healing length equal to the next jump, and order-one critical slow activity per dwell---uniquely select the scaling, and at that scaling a random non-annealed interface survives the limit.  A proof route works in the moving-defect frame over dwell intervals with a Mosco-type convergence of random time-dependent forms.  The nearest result is the moving-defect SSEP of Chatterjee, Chatterjee, and Pradhan~\cite{ChatterjeeCP16}.  A first decisive theorem is tightness of the Brownian membrane with survival of the interface.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the rescaled membrane variance and slow-bond attempts per dwell both stayed order one across sizes.  A counterexample would be an annealed deterministic-membrane limit at the matched scaling.

\begin{conjecture}[Interior two-sided capacitor membrane]\label{an15}
Split a one-dimensional system into left and right SSEP bulks and an interior storage node of capacity $\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$, conserving total mass, with side-to-storage rates of order $N$.  The limit is $\mu_t=\rho_-du+\rho_+du+m(t)\delta_0$ with heat equations in the bulks, nonlinear vertex fluxes $F_\pm(r,m)=a_\pm r(1-m/\kappa)-b_\pm(m/\kappa)(1-r)$, boundary conditions $-\partial_{n_\pm}\rho_\pm=F_\pm$, and $\dot m=F_-+F_+$, conserving $\int\rho_-+\int\rho_++m$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
A single atomic storage state couples two macroscopic traces and mediates delayed conservative transfer between them, an interior two-sided capacitor.  A proof route couples the two bulk replacement estimates through the storage occupation.  \emph{Priority.}  Franco, Franco, and Gon\c calves~\cite{FrancoFrancoGoncalves26} prove finite-reservoir Wentzell boundary behaviour for exclusion; C15 differs in being interior, two-sided, conservative, and shared, but the conceptual distance is small, so the statement carries a high overlap with prior work.  A first decisive theorem would be the single-side reduction.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, total microscopic mass was conserved exactly and the stored macroscopic mass stayed order one across sizes.  A counterexample would be a vanishing or non-shared storage variable in the limit.


\part{Fixed-traffic circulation laws for nonequilibrium Markov chains}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 22 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The four conjectures below concern a controlled family of finite-state continuous-time Markov chains---fixed-traffic circulation rays---in which the stationary law, every undirected stationary edge traffic, and every escape rate are held fixed while an irreversible stationary circulation of strength $\alpha$ is increased.  The ray therefore varies time-reversal asymmetry without touching the equilibrium landscape or the local activity.  Two conjectures concern visited-set statistics (Conjectures~\ref{ao1}, \ref{ao3}, \ref{ao4}) and one the spectral geometry of the generator (Conjecture~\ref{ao2}).  Each is a determinate law with a stated mechanism, a nearest-literature boundary, a first decisive theorem, and a route to disproof.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{ao:basic}: the endpoint spectral bounds, the exact even-analytic dependence of visited-set laws on $\alpha$, and an explicit high-precision counterexample showing that the natural stronger companion---whole-ray monotonicity of the fast real spectral edge---is \emph{false}, so only the endpoint bound survives there.  Conjecture~\ref{ao2} is the strongest of the four; its own stronger global-unimodality form is also false and is recorded as a control.  The visited-set laws are exact finite-state statements, tested here by exact augmented-chain propagation rather than trajectory sampling, but with the alternating-derivative hierarchy of Conjecture~\ref{ao1} checked only to finite order.

Let the state space be $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with stationary law $\pi>0$.  For each undirected edge fix a symmetric traffic $T_{ij}=T_{ji}>0$ and an antisymmetric divergence-free current $J_{ij}=-J_{ji}$, $\sum_jJ_{ij}=0$, with $|J_{ij}|<T_{ij}$.  The circulation ray has off-diagonal rates $L_{\alpha,ij}=(T_{ij}+\alpha J_{ij})/(2\pi_i)$, $0\le\alpha\le1$, and zero row sums; then $\pi$ is stationary, the undirected traffic $q_{ij}(\alpha)+q_{ji}(\alpha)=T_{ij}$ and the escape rate $r_i=\tfrac1{2\pi_i}\sum_jT_{ij}$ are $\alpha$-independent.  Writing $H_\alpha=-D^{1/2}L_\alpha D^{-1/2}$ with $D=\operatorname{diag}(\pi)$ and restricting off the stationary mode gives $G_\alpha=K+\alpha C$ with $K=K^\ast\succ0$ and $C^\ast=-C$.  Let $h(\alpha)=\max\{\Re\lambda:\lambda\in\sigma(-L_\alpha)\setminus\{0\}\}$ and $g(\alpha)=\min\{\Re\lambda:\lambda\in\sigma(-L_\alpha)\setminus\{0\}\}$ be the fast and slow real spectral edges.  Let $V_t=\{X_s:0\le s\le t\}$ be the visited set, $w_i^{(\gamma)}=\pi_i^\gamma/\sum_j\pi_j^\gamma$ escort weights, and $U_{\gamma,t}=\sum_iw_i^{(\gamma)}\mathbf 1_{\{\tau_i>t\}}$ the unexplored escort mass, with $x=\alpha^2$.

\begin{proposition}[Endpoint bounds, even dependence, and the failure of fast-edge ray monotonicity]\label{ao:basic}
For every ray, $\Re\lambda(G_\alpha)\in[\lambda_{\min}(K),\lambda_{\max}(K)]$, so $h(\alpha)\le h(0)=\lambda_{\max}(K)$ and $g(\alpha)\ge g(0)=\lambda_{\min}(K)$.  Under a stationary start, path reversal maps the law of $L_\alpha$ to that of $L_{-\alpha}$ and fixes every visited-set statistic, so $V_t^{(\alpha)}\overset d=V_t^{(-\alpha)}$ and all finite-state visited-set probabilities are even analytic functions of $\alpha$, whence $x=\alpha^2$ is the natural variable.  The endpoint bound does \emph{not} extend to whole-ray monotonicity of the fast edge: there is a bidirected six-state ray on which $h(\alpha)$ strictly increases over an interior interval by more than $0.6$, verified to $40$ digits, so the companion statement $h(\beta)\le h(\alpha)$ for $\alpha\le\beta$ is false.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For an eigenpair $G_\alpha v=\lambda v$, $\Re\lambda=v^\ast Kv/v^\ast v\in[\lambda_{\min}(K),\lambda_{\max}(K)]$ by the Rayleigh bound, and at $\alpha=0$, $G_0=K$ attains both ends; this gives the endpoint inequalities.  The adjoint identity $L_{-\alpha}=L_\alpha^\ast$ in $L^2(\pi)$ and the invariance of $V_t$ under time reversal give the equality in law and hence even analyticity in $\alpha$.  The counterexample is an explicit valid ray (positive rates for all $\alpha\in[0,1]$, $\pi$ stationary to machine precision) whose fast-edge curve, recomputed by high-precision eigenvalue evaluation on a refined grid, rises across an interior interval; the increase exceeds $0.6$ at $40$-digit precision, far above any conditioning artifact, so it is genuine.
\end{proof}

\section{Visited-set and spectral circulation laws}

\begin{conjecture}[Escort unexplored-mass alternating-derivative hierarchy]\label{ao1}
For every integer $k\ge1$, integer $r\ge0$, time $t\ge0$, and $0\le\gamma\le1$, with $x=\alpha^2$,
\[
(-1)^r\frac{d^r}{dx^r}\,\mathbb E_{\sqrt x}\!\bigl[U_{\gamma,t}^{\,k}\bigr]\ge0
\]
throughout the admissible physical interval.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Every moment of the unexplored escort mass is a positive combination of finite-target avoidance probabilities, and $x=\alpha^2$ is forced as the variable by the time-reversal even-analyticity of Proposition~\ref{ao:basic}; the conjecture asserts a complete alternating-derivative hierarchy in the squared circulation, unifying stationary-random-target avoidance ($\gamma=1$) with expected state-space exploration ($\gamma=0$).  A proof route seeks an operator Stieltjes representation in $x$, or a target-avoidance identity made positive by pairing a path with its reverse.  The nearest results are the nonreversible-chain hitting/variance improvements of Rey-Bellet and Spiliopoulos~\cite{ReyBelletSpiliopoulos16} and Huang and Mao~\cite{HuangMao17}.  A first decisive theorem would be the first moment at $\gamma\in\{0,1\}$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact augmented-chain propagation on chains of sizes three to six recorded thousands of alternating-difference inequalities with no violation beyond roundoff; the infinite hierarchy is checked only to finite order.  A counterexample would be a moment, order, and lag with the wrong derivative sign.

\begin{conjecture}[One-maximum principle for the slow spectral edge]\label{ao2}
The slow real spectral edge $g(\alpha)$ has at most one strict interior local maximum on $(0,1)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The endpoint bound $g(\alpha)\ge g(0)$ says irreversibility cannot push the slow edge below the reversible gap, but says nothing about the shape in between; the conjecture asserts a rigid one-maximum shape imposed by the Markov positivity cone, allowing a later shallow rebound but not a second interior peak.  A proof route studies branch collisions of the symmetric-plus-skew pencil $K+\alpha C$ under the constraint that not every such pencil is a positive generator.  The nearest results are the affinity/winding eigenvalue-localization bounds of Kolchinsky, Ohga, and Ito~\cite{KOI24}.  A first decisive theorem would be the birth--death-plus-one-shortcut case.  The stronger global-unimodality form of this conjecture is \emph{false}, an eight-state ray realizing an interior maximum followed by a shallow minimum and an endpoint rebound, which is retained as a control.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, no ray among thousands of general and stressed families showed two interior maxima of $g$.  A counterexample would be a ray with two strict interior maxima of the slow edge.

\begin{conjecture}[Unicyclic range stochastic acceleration]\label{ao3}
For every bidirected chain whose undirected support is connected of cycle rank one, with $X_0\sim\pi$ and $R_t=|V_t|$: for every $m$, $t\ge0$, and $0\le\alpha\le\beta\le1$,
\[
\Pr_\beta(R_t\ge m)\ge\Pr_\alpha(R_t\ge m).
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
On a single-cycle support the whole finite-time range distribution is stochastically accelerated by circulation, first-order stochastic dominance along the ray that implies expected-range improvement and, at $m=n$, acceleration of cover time.  A proof route uses the unique-cycle decomposition, coupling excursions into attached trees to a biased cycle traversal.  The nearest results are the nonreversible mixing improvements of Chen and Hwang~\cite{ChenHwang13} and Hua and Chen~\cite{HuaChen22}; the unicyclic restriction is substantive, the same range ordering being false on general fixed-traffic graphs and retained as a control.  A first decisive theorem would be expected-range monotonicity.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact augmented-chain propagation on unicyclic families recorded thousands of stochastic-order inequalities with no violation beyond roundoff; an earlier apparent violation was traced to comparing probabilities at $\alpha$-dependent times rather than a fixed lag and vanishes under the correct fixed-time comparison.  A counterexample would be a unicyclic ray with a genuinely non-monotone range tail.

\begin{conjecture}[Pure-cycle stationary-mass coverage acceleration]\label{ao4}
For a simple-cycle support with $X_0\sim\pi$ and $M_t=\pi(V_t)$: for every $z\in[0,1]$, $t\ge0$, and $0\le\alpha\le\beta\le1$,
\[
\Pr_\beta(M_t\ge z)\ge\Pr_\alpha(M_t\ge z).
\]
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
On a simple cycle the visited set is a contiguous arc and the divergence-free current is one-dimensional, so the fixed-traffic deformation is unusually rigid; the conjecture asserts stochastic acceleration of the stationary mass of the visited set, which for nonuniform $\pi$ is strictly more than the range acceleration of Conjecture~\ref{ao3}.  A proof route reduces to a two-boundary arc-growth process whose clockwise and counterclockwise rates change oppositely under circulation at fixed total activity.  The nearest result is the circulant maximum-entropy mixing-time extremality of Avrachenkov, Cottatellucci, Maggi, and Mao~\cite{ACMM13}, whose homogeneous case is adjacent and attributed.  A first decisive theorem would be the homogeneous cycle.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact augmented-chain propagation on nonuniform cycles recorded tens of thousands of stochastic-order inequalities with no violation, cross-checked against Gillespie simulation.  A counterexample would be a cycle and mass threshold with a non-monotone coverage tail.


\part{Cross-shadow universality}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 24 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The five conjectures below share a single principle.  In each, two limiting observables are read off the \emph{same} discrete randomness, often with no literal separation of the input coordinates, and are nevertheless conjectured to decouple because they probe distinct resolution, frequency, or representation-theoretic sectors.  We call this \emph{cross-shadow universality}: an Archimedean or edge shadow and an arithmetic or bulk shadow of one random object become asymptotically independent even though each is a function of all of the input.  They fall in five settings.  A random-matrix setting (Conjecture~\ref{ap1}) couples the real microscopic spectrum of a symmetric integer Wigner matrix to its fixed-odd-prime Smith cokernel.  An arithmetic setting (Conjecture~\ref{ap2}) asks a bounded-alphabet random determinant to obey random-integer multiplicative laws in the growing-dimension regime.  An integrable-probability setting (Conjecture~\ref{ap3}) separates the modular charge of a Plancherel partition from its Airy edge.  A representation-theoretic setting (Conjecture~\ref{ap4}) asserts that the exponentially large unstable Fourier spectrum of a symmetric-group word measure cannot beat its best stable mode.  A local--global setting (Conjecture~\ref{ap5}) factorizes the real and fixed-prime root processes of a random Littlewood polynomial.  Each is a determinate law with a stated mechanism, a nearest-literature boundary, a first decisive theorem, and a route to disproof.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}: the nonsingular determinant--cokernel identity, the exact Parseval identity that makes the word-measure chi-square canonical, the $p$-adic unit-root property of Littlewood polynomials, the summable fixed-prime singularity tilt, and Rostam's core normalization.  The marginals in every case are mature theorems; what is proposed as new is in each case the joint law, for which no antecedent was found.  These are asymptotic-independence statements, so the accompanying finite-size diagnostics can only exclude gross obstructions: a small observed correlation is compatible with either a finite-size effect or genuine slow-decaying dependence, and no such computation certifies independence.  Two statements are flagged as beginning with odd primes only: the $p=2$ paired-cokernel structure of Conjecture~\ref{ap1} and the collapsed reduction $+1\equiv-1$ of Conjecture~\ref{ap5} are exceptional and are deferred to secondary statements.

\begin{proposition}[Cross-shadow anchor identities]\label{ap:basic}
{\rm(i)} For an integral matrix $A_n$ with $\det A_n\ne0$, the cokernel $\Z^n/A_n\Z^n$ is finite of order $|\det A_n|$, so the Archimedean size and the total arithmetic size coincide and cannot factor; the conjectured factorization is therefore of \emph{local} shadows only.  {\rm(ii)} For a conjugation-invariant word measure $\mu_{w,N}$ on $S_N$ with uniform reference $U_N$,
\[
\chi^2(\mu_{w,N}\Vert U_N)=\sum_{\rho\in\widehat{S_N},\,\rho\ne\mathbf 1}|\E_w\chi_\rho|^2,
\qquad \E_w\chi_\rho=\E[\chi_\rho(w(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_r))],
\]
an exact Parseval identity over the nontrivial irreducibles.  {\rm(iii)} Every root in $\Q_p$ of a Littlewood polynomial $F_n(X)=\sum_{j=0}^n\varepsilon_jX^j$, $\varepsilon_j=\pm1$, is a $p$-adic unit.  {\rm(iv)} The fixed-prime singularity probability of a balanced random matrix over $\mathbb F_p$ is $c_p=1-\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})=1/p+O(p^{-2})$, so the tilt $c_p-1/p$ is summable over primes.  {\rm(v)} For a fixed $e$-core, $t^{-1/2}|\operatorname{core}_e(\lambda_t)|$ and $(4/\pi)\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{Ros}}$ differ only by the deterministic factor $\pi/4$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
{\rm(i)} The Smith normal form writes $A_n=U\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n)V$ with $U,V\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\Z)$, so $\Z^n/A_n\Z^n\cong\bigoplus_i\Z/d_i$ has order $\prod_i|d_i|=|\det A_n|$.  {\rm(ii)} Writing $f=\mathrm d\mu_{w,N}/\mathrm dU_N=N!\,\mu_{w,N}$, the class functions carry the orthonormal basis $\{\chi_\rho\}$ under $\langle a,b\rangle=\E_{U_N}[a\bar b]$; expanding $f-1=\sum_\rho c_\rho\chi_\rho$ gives $c_\rho=\E_{U_N}[f\bar\chi_\rho]=\E_w\bar\chi_\rho$ for $\rho\ne\mathbf1$ and $c_{\mathbf1}=0$, and Parseval gives $\chi^2(\mu\Vert U)=\lVert f-1\rVert^2=\sum_{\rho\ne\mathbf1}|\E_w\chi_\rho|^2$.  {\rm(iii)} If $|x|_p<1$ then $|F_n(x)|_p=|\varepsilon_0|_p=1$ since every higher term lies in $p\Z_p$, so $F_n(x)\ne0$; if $|x|_p>1$ the leading term $\varepsilon_nx^n$ strictly dominates the rest in $|\cdot|_p$, so again $F_n(x)\ne0$; hence any root has $|x|_p=1$.  {\rm(iv)} Expanding $\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})=1-p^{-1}-p^{-2}+O(p^{-3})$ near its dominant terms gives $c_p=p^{-1}+O(p^{-2})$, and $\sum_p(c_p-1/p)<\infty$.  {\rm(v)} is Rostam's definition of the normalized core statistic.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Local spectral--Smith factorization]\label{ap1}
Let $A_n$ be a symmetric integral Wigner matrix with independent upper-triangular entries: off-diagonal entries have a fixed integer law $\xi$ with $\E\xi=0$, $\E\xi^2=\sigma^2>0$, enough moments for edge universality, and a fixed anti-concentration bound modulo every odd prime; diagonal entries are centered with the remaining Wigner hypotheses.  Let $\mathcal E_n$ be the rescaled real upper-edge process of $A_n/(\sigma\sqrt n)$ and, for an odd prime $p$, let $C_{n,p}=(\operatorname{coker} A_n[p^\infty],\delta_{n,p})$ be the $p$-primary cokernel with its symmetric discriminant pairing.  Then for every fixed finite set $P$ of odd primes,
\[
\bigl(\mathcal E_n,(C_{n,p})_{p\in P}\bigr)\Longrightarrow \mathcal E_{\mathrm{GOE}}\otimes\bigotimes_{p\in P}\mu_p^{\mathrm{sym}},
\]
with $\mu_p^{\mathrm{sym}}$ the universal paired-cokernel law, and the same product limit holds with any fixed finite collection of microscopic bulk and edge spectral windows in place of $\mathcal E_n$.  The $p=2$ analogue, with the correct $2$-adic paired state space, is a secondary statement.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The real microscopic spectrum is governed by resolvents at scale $n^{-1}$ in the bulk and $n^{-2/3}$ at the edge, while a fixed $p$-primary cokernel is governed by congruence rank and lifting through bounded powers of $p$; both are functions of the same entries, and the conjecture is resolution separation without input separation.  Global quantities cannot factor, since $|\det A_n|=|\operatorname{coker} A_n|$ on nonsingularity by Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}(i); the claim is about the local shadows.  The nearest results are the paired-cokernel universality of Hodges~\cite{Hodges24} and the quantitative symmetric-cokernel universality of Shen~\cite{ShenCok26} on one side, and real Wigner edge and bulk universality on the other; no joint theorem couples the two shadows of one integral matrix.  A first decisive theorem would be, for one odd prime and one three-point ensemble, $(n^{2/3}(\lambda_{\max}-2),\dim_{\mathbb F_p}\ker(A_n\bmod p))\Rightarrow\mathrm{TW}_1\otimes\nu_p$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, symmetric $\{-1,0,1\}$ matrices show odd-prime edge/nullity correlations small and unstable in sign, while $p=2$ retains a persistent finite-size correlation, the reason the statement begins with odd primes.  A counterexample would be a structured family of almost-singular real eigenvectors whose arithmetic also raises modular rank, a coupling channel neither marginal theory sees.

\begin{conjecture}[Random-integer multiplicative universality of determinants]\label{ap2}
Let $B_n$ have i.i.d.\ Bernoulli-$\tfrac12$ entries in $\{0,1\}$ and set $D_n=|\det B_n|$, conditioned on $D_n\ge3$.  Then
\[
\frac{\omega(D_n)-\log\log D_n}{\sqrt{\log\log D_n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\]
and simultaneously the ranked normalized logarithms of the prime factors converge in the ranked simplex,
\[
\left(\frac{\log Q_{1,n}}{\log D_n},\frac{\log Q_{2,n}}{\log D_n},\dots\right)\Rightarrow PD(1),
\]
so the normalized logarithm of the largest prime factor converges to the largest component of a Poisson--Dirichlet $PD(1)$ partition.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
For each fixed prime, reduction modulo $p$ turns $B_n$ into a balanced matrix, so $\Pr(p\mid D_n)\to c_p=1/p+O(p^{-2})$; the local tilt $c_p-1/p$ is summable by Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}(iv), so it may shift bounded centering constants but should vanish on the Erd\H os--Kac and Poisson--Dirichlet scales.  This is a dimension-driven arithmetic universality: the input alphabet is fixed forever while the determinant acquires $n^2$ variables and degree $n$, unlike classical Erd\H os--Kac results that fix a polynomial and enlarge the input box.  The $\{0,1\}$ alphabet is essential; a $\pm1$ determinant carries a deterministic power-of-two divisor incompatible with random-integer statistics.  The nearest results are finite-field singularity universality of Maples~\cite{Maples13} and the non-square theorem of Bary-Soroker and Kozma~\cite{BSK20}, with the magnitude theory of Tao--Vu and Nguyen--Vu~\cite{TaoVu06,NguyenVu14}; no Erd\H os--Kac or Poisson--Dirichlet law for a bounded-alphabet random determinant was found.  A first decisive theorem would be a central limit theorem for $\sum_{p\le e^{cn}}\mathbf 1_{p\mid D_n}$ for some fixed $c>0$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact determinant factorizations give $\omega(D_n)$ of order $\log\log D_n$ with a bounded excess, and a largest-prime fraction drifting toward the Golomb--Dickman value $0.62433\ldots$, though the factorable sizes are tiny.  A counterexample would be a systematic excess of medium primes leaving the normal law intact while destroying $PD(1)$, or the reverse.

\begin{conjecture}[Plancherel modular-charge/Airy factorization]\label{ap3}
Let $\lambda_t$ have poissonized Plancherel measure with parameter $t$, fix $e\ge2$, and let $X^{(e)}(\lambda_t)$ be the $e$-abacus charge vector in the root lattice, with Rostam's normalization $Y_t^{(e)}=e\sqrt{\pi/2}\,t^{-1/4}X^{(e)}(\lambda_t)$.  Let $\mathcal A_t$ be the Plancherel upper-edge process.  Then
\[
\bigl(Y_t^{(e)},\mathcal A_t\bigr)\Longrightarrow G_e\otimes\mathcal A_{\mathrm{GUE}},
\]
with $G_e$ Rostam's Gaussian charge limit and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{GUE}}$ the Airy$_2$ edge; consequently, with $\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{Ros}}$ Rostam's Gamma-sum law,
\[
\left(\frac{\pi}{4\sqrt t}\,|\operatorname{core}_e(\lambda_t)|,\;t^{-1/6}(\lambda_{t,1}-2\sqrt t)\right)\Longrightarrow\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{Ros}}\otimes F_2 ,
\]
with $F_2$ the Tracy--Widom GUE distribution and the deterministic $\pi/4$ scaling of Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}(v).
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The Plancherel partition is a discrete-Bessel determinantal process, and the two observables probe different sectors of it: the Airy statistic lives at the turning point of the limit shape, while the $e$-core charge is a periodic residue imbalance accumulated across the occupied Fermi sea, neither a compactly supported local statistic nor a smooth linear statistic.  The mechanism is frequency-sector separation of a high-frequency modular bulk observable from a turning-point edge observable.  The nearest results are Johansson's Airy edge asymptotics~\cite{Johansson01} and Rostam's explicit core-size law~\cite{Rostam23}; no joint distribution or independence statement was found, and the generic independence of smooth linear statistics from the edge does not apply because the $e$-core is built from periodic residue classes and a quadratic charge.  A first decisive theorem would be the $e=2$ scalar case, joint convergence of the normalized $2$-abacus charge and the longest row to $G\otimes F_2$, via a Fredholm determinant with a periodic charge twist and an edge projector.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact RSK sampling of poissonized Plancherel partitions gives core/edge correlations that fluctuate around zero and shrink from $t=400$ to $t=900$, with the $\pi/4$ normalization reproduced.  A counterexample would be a persistent nonzero covariance, or zero covariance with higher-order dependence, distinguishing periodic modular statistics from smooth bulk ones.

\begin{conjecture}[Stable-spectrum saturation of word measures]\label{ap4}
Let $w\in F_r$ have primitive abelianization in $\Z^r$ but be non-primitive in $F_r$, and let $\mu_{w,N}$ be the word measure it induces on $S_N$ by evaluating $w$ at $r$ independent uniform permutations.  With $\lambda[N]=(N-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\dots)$ and $\chi_{\lambda[N]}$ the stable irreducible character, set
\[
\beta_{\mathrm{st}}(w)=\inf_{\lambda\ne\varnothing}\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{-\log|\E_w\chi_{\lambda[N]}|}{\log N},\qquad -\log0=+\infty .
\]
Then
\[
\chi^2(\mu_{w,N}\Vert U_N)=N^{-2\beta_{\mathrm{st}}(w)+o(1)}\quad\text{and}\quad
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu_{w,N}\Vert U_N)=N^{-2\beta_{\mathrm{st}}(w)+o(1)} ,
\]
so the aggregate contribution of all unstable irreducible representations cannot improve the polynomial exponent of non-uniformity beyond the best stable Fourier mode.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The exact Parseval identity of Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}(ii) makes the chi-square the squared $\ell^2$ norm of the full nontrivial Fourier spectrum, so the conjecture is a genuine global saturation principle rather than a statement about finitely many stable observables: an exponentially large unstable spectrum does not collectively beat the best stable mode.  The nearest results are the word-measure and stable-invariant theory of Hanany--Puder and Puder--Shomroni~\cite{HananyPuder20,PuderShomroni26a,PuderShomroni26b}, which control fixed stable characters through primitivity-type invariants; no treatment of the KL or chi-square divergence of an $S_N$ word measure from uniform, or of the complete Fourier tail against the stable sector, was found.  A first decisive theorem would be, for $w=[x,y]x$, the matching bound $\chi^2,\ D_{\mathrm{KL}}=N^{-2+o(1)}$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact enumeration of $S_N^2$ for $w=[x,y]x$ through $N=6$ keeps $N^2\chi^2$ and $N^2D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ of order one, consistent with the exponent $2$, with the Parseval identity confirmed exactly.  A counterexample would be a family of unstable irreducibles collectively contributing more chi-square mass than every stable character, or KL and chi-square with different exponents through rare density-ratio spikes, either defining a new asymptotic invariant of words.  If the emerging stable theory identifies $\beta_{\mathrm{st}}(w)$ with the stable primitivity rank, the exponent becomes $2s\pi(w)$; that identification is deliberately kept separate.

\begin{conjecture}[Adelic root-process factorization]\label{ap5}
Let $F_n(X)=\sum_{j=0}^n\varepsilon_jX^j$ with independent signs $\varepsilon_j=\pm1$.  Let $\mathcal R_n=\sum_{r:\,F_n(r)=0}\delta_{n(|r|-1)}$ be the real-root process near the unit circle, and for an odd prime $p$ let $\mathcal Z_{p,n}=\sum_{\alpha\in\Q_p:\,F_n(\alpha)=0}m_\alpha\,\delta_\alpha$ be the $p$-adic root process on $\Z_p^\times$ (every $\Q_p$ root is a unit by Proposition~\ref{ap:basic}(iii)).  Then for every fixed finite set $P$ of odd primes,
\[
\bigl(\mathcal R_n,(\mathcal Z_{p,n})_{p\in P}\bigr)\Longrightarrow\nu_\infty\otimes\bigotimes_{p\in P}\nu_p ,
\]
with $\nu_\infty$ the limiting real microscopic root process and $\nu_p$ the universal $p$-adic root process for the Littlewood law.  The prime $2$ is excluded, since modulo $2$ one has $+1\equiv-1$ and the reduction loses all coefficient randomness.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
For an odd prime the residues do distinguish $+1$ from $-1$, so the $p$-adic observer can in principle reconstruct the whole sign sequence: there is no literal decomposition into independent real and $p$-adic digits, and the mechanism is adelic mode orthogonality.  The real process near $\pm1$ is controlled by approximately Gaussian evaluation and derivative modes at Archimedean scale, while fixed-prime roots are governed by congruence evaluation and Hensel lifting; each is a low-complexity nonlinear functional of the same high-dimensional sign vector, and the overlap of their informative modes is conjectured to vanish.  The nearest results are Michelen's real microscopic root process~\cite{Michelen21} and the non-Archimedean mean, correlation, and universality theory of Shmueli, Caruso, and Shen~\cite{Shmueli23,Caruso22,ShenPadic26}, whose expected $\Q_p$ root count is $(p-1)/(p+1)$; no joint Archimedean/$p$-adic root theorem for a single random coefficient sequence was found.  A first decisive theorem would be $(\mathcal R_n,S_{p,n})\Rightarrow\nu_\infty\otimes\sigma_p$ for the count $S_{p,n}$ of simple roots modulo $p$, each of which Hensel-lifts uniquely.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the expected $p$-adic root count approaches $(p-1)/(p+1)$ and the real-near-unit and simple-root-mod-$p$ counts show only small, slowly decaying correlations.  A counterexample would be a surviving coupling at $x=\pm1$, where a real root near $1$ and the event $F_n(1)\equiv0\pmod p$ share the evaluation $F_n(1)$; the correct theorem might then require conditioning on finitely many shared evaluation modes.



\part{Entropy and rare-event laws for random algebraic and topological structures}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Added to the deposit: 29 August 2026.}\par\medskip

The five conjectures below place deep algebraic and topological invariants---matrix-polynomial spectra, matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials, Khovanov homology, Jacobian lattices of hyperbolic surfaces, and Heegaard Floer homology---on canonical random ensembles and assert entropy, threshold, and rare-event laws for them.  They fall in five settings.  A random-matrix setting (Conjecture~\ref{aq1}) matches the zeros of a random matrix polynomial at a tropical breakpoint to a two-coefficient pencil in a double-scaling regime.  A matroid setting (Conjecture~\ref{aq2}) locates the transition from subextensive to extensive Kazhdan--Lusztig complexity of the random graphic matroid exactly at the Erd\H os--R\'enyi giant-cycle threshold.  A categorified-invariant setting (Conjecture~\ref{aq3}) asserts a deterministic convex free energy for the Khovanov bigrading of random braid closures.  A random-surface setting (Conjecture~\ref{aq4}) transfers the Weil--Petersson short-geodesic rare-event law to the first minimum of the Jacobian lattice through a two-sided thin-handle equivalence.  A three-manifold setting (Conjecture~\ref{aq5}) asserts that the Heegaard Floer rank of a random Heegaard splitting grows at exactly the homological torsion rate, with no excess exponential entropy.  Each is a determinate law with a stated mechanism, a nearest-literature boundary, a first decisive theorem, and a route to disproof.  The proved layer is Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}: the two-face tropical reduction and its spherical-ensemble pencil law, the block multiplicativity of matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials with the triviality of forests, the convexity and linear boundedness of the Khovanov free energy at finite length, the $\varepsilon^2/4$ short-geodesic tail with its collar-capacity normalization, and the Floer--homology lower bound $\operatorname{rank}\widehat{HF}\ge|H_1|$ on rational homology spheres.  The statements are asymptotic laws for invariants whose exact computation is infeasible at scale, so the accompanying diagnostics test exact finite calibrations, decategorified proxies, and reduced models rather than the laws themselves; where a proxy does not reach the hard mechanism, in particular the homological cancellations of Conjectures~\ref{aq3} and~\ref{aq5}, that gap is recorded where it occurs.

\begin{proposition}[Anchor identities and reductions]\label{aq:basic}
{\rm(i)} Let $P_{\beta,N}(z)=\sum_{k=0}^d e^{\beta a_k}z^kG_{k,N}$ with $G_{k,N}$ independent complex Ginibre matrices of entry variance $1/N$, let $x_*$ be a tropical breakpoint of $\Phi(x)=\max_k(a_k+kx)$ attained exactly by $r<s$, put $m=s-r$ and $\delta=\min_{k\ne r,s}(\Phi(x_*)-(a_k+kx_*))>0$.  After the rescaling $z=e^{\beta x_*}\zeta$ and removal of the common scalar factor, every inactive coefficient carries the factor $e^{-\beta\Delta_k}\le e^{-\beta\delta}$, and the zeros of the dominant pencil $G_{r,N}+\zeta^mG_{s,N}$ are exactly the $m$-th roots of the eigenvalues of $-G_{s,N}^{-1}G_{r,N}$: the $m$-th-root lift of the complex spherical ensemble.  {\rm(ii)} Matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials are multiplicative under direct sums, the cycle matroid of a graph is the direct sum of the cycle matroids of its blocks, every Boolean matroid has $P\equiv1$, and hence every forest has $P_{M(G)}\equiv1$; the cycle $C_k$ contributes the uniform matroid $U_{k-1,k}$.  {\rm(iii)} For any link diagram with $c$ crossings on $m$ strands, $\log Z(u,v)=\log\sum_{i,j}\dim_{\mathbb F_2}Kh^{i,j}\,e^{ui+vj}$ is convex in $(u,v)$ and bounded by $C(c+m)(1+|u|+|v|)$, so along a random braid word of length $n$ with bounded generators, $n^{-1}\log Z_n(u,v)$ is convex and uniformly bounded on compacta.  {\rm(iv)} With the Weil--Petersson short-geodesic intensity $\lambda(\ell)=\tfrac{e^\ell+e^{-\ell}-2}{2\ell}$, the Poisson mean is $\Lambda(\varepsilon)=\int_0^\varepsilon\lambda=\tfrac{\varepsilon^2}4+O(\varepsilon^4)$, so $\varepsilon^{-2}\Pr(\ell_{\mathrm{ns}}(X_g)\le\varepsilon)\to\tfrac14$ in the limit $g\to\infty$ then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$; and the collar capacity satisfies $\pi\,\mathrm{cap}(\ell)/\ell\to1$ as $\ell\downarrow0$.  {\rm(v)} For a rational homology sphere $Y$, $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\widehat{HF}(Y)\ge|H_1(Y;\Z)|$, so the excess Floer entropy $E=\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\widehat{HF}(Y)-\log|H_1(Y;\Z)|$ is nonnegative.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
{\rm(i)} Dividing $P_{\beta,N}(e^{\beta x_*}\zeta)$ by $e^{\beta\Phi(x_*)}$ gives coefficient $e^{\beta(a_k+kx_*-\Phi(x_*))}=e^{-\beta\Delta_k}$ at $\zeta^k$, with $\Delta_r=\Delta_s=0$ and $\Delta_k\ge\delta$ otherwise.  Since $G_{s,N}$ is almost surely invertible, $\det(G_{r,N}+\zeta^mG_{s,N})=\det(G_{s,N})\prod_i(\zeta^m-\lambda_i)$ with $\lambda_i$ the eigenvalues of $-G_{s,N}^{-1}G_{r,N}$; the eigenvalues of $G_{s,N}^{-1}G_{r,N}$ form the complex spherical ensemble~\cite{Krishnapur09}, which is invariant under rotation, so the zeros are its $m$-th-root lift.  {\rm(ii)} Multiplicativity and $P_{B_n}\equiv1$ are proved by Elias, Proudfoot, and Wakefield~\cite{EPW16}; a bridge is a coloop, so a forest's cycle matroid is Boolean, and the block decomposition of the cycle matroid is classical.  {\rm(iii)} $Z$ is a finite sum of exponentials with nonnegative integer weights, so $\log Z$ is convex by H\"older; the cube of resolutions has $2^c$ vertices, each carrying at most $c+m$ circles, so $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}Kh\le2^{2c+m}$ while $|i|\le c$ and $|j|\le2c+m+c$, giving the linear bound; a word of length $n$ in fixed generators has $c\le Cn$ crossings.  {\rm(iv)} $\lambda(\ell)=\sum_{k\ge1}\ell^{2k-1}/(2k)!$, so $\Lambda(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k\ge1}\varepsilon^{2k}/(2k\,(2k)!)=\tfrac{\varepsilon^2}4+\tfrac{\varepsilon^4}{96}+\cdots$; by Mirzakhani and Petri~\cite{MirzakhaniPetri19} the number of primitive closed geodesics of length at most $\varepsilon$ converges to a Poisson variable of mean $\Lambda(\varepsilon)$ and the short ones are simple and nonseparating asymptotically almost surely, so $\Pr(\ell_{\mathrm{ns}}\le\varepsilon)\to1-e^{-\Lambda(\varepsilon)}$; the collar of a geodesic of length $\ell$ has modulus $\pi/\ell+O(1)$, whence $\pi\,\mathrm{cap}(\ell)/\ell\to1$.  {\rm(v)} $\widehat{HF}(Y)$ splits over the $|H_1(Y;\Z)|$ $\mathrm{Spin}^c$ structures, and each summand has Euler characteristic $\pm1$~\cite{OzsvathSzabo04}, hence is nonzero over $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Double-scaling tropical shadowing]\label{aq1}
In the setting of Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}(i), suppose $\beta_N\delta/\log N\to\infty$.  Then on every compact annular sector $K\subset\mathbb C^\times$ contained in one branch of the $m$-th-root map and of angular width strictly less than $2\pi/m$, after removing a boundary layer whose limiting intensity vanishes, the zeros of the full matrix polynomial in $K$ can be matched to the zeros of $G_{r,N}+\zeta^mG_{s,N}$ so that the maximal matching displacement is $o_{\Pp}(N^{-1/2})$.  Consequently, after microscopic unfolding, the selected zero point process has the same local weak limit as the corresponding single-branch lift of the complex spherical ensemble.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
At fixed $N$ the limit $\beta\to\infty$ is a perturbative reduction to the two-face pencil, but in the joint regime the exponentially small inactive coefficients compete with the $N^{-1/2}$ microscopic spacing and the nonnormal condition numbers of the pencil, and the conjecture asserts that the tropical combinatorics still selects the local law; the matching formulation is primary, and pointwise convergence of correlation densities is a consequence only under additional uniform-integrability and density hypotheses.  The nearest results are the tropical localization of matrix-polynomial eigenvalues of Noferini, Sharify, and Tisseur~\cite{NoferiniST15} and Akian, Gaubert, and Sharify~\cite{AkianGS17}, which bound moduli but carry no microscopic law, and the spherical-ensemble limit of Krishnapur~\cite{Krishnapur09}.  A first decisive theorem would be the two-coefficient case $d=1$ at a single breakpoint, or any joint regime $\beta_N=c\log N$ with $c$ large.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, at profile $(-2,0,-1,0)$ the $\sqrt N$-scaled optimal matching displacement fell from $0.095$ to $0.009$ across $N=4$ to $20$ at $\beta=2\log N$ and stalled near $0.4$ at $\beta=0.75\log N$, locating the double-scaling threshold.  A counterexample would be a breakpoint and regime with $\beta_N\delta/\log N\to\infty$ whose matching displacement fails to be $o(N^{-1/2})$, and the crossover $\beta_N\delta\asymp c\log N$ with its possible critical kernels is the sharper open boundary.

\begin{conjecture}[Kazhdan--Lusztig entropy percolation]\label{aq2}
Let $G_n\sim G(n,c/n)$, let $M(G_n)$ be its cycle matroid, $P_{M(G_n)}(t)$ its matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial, and $H_n(c)=n^{-1}\log P_{M(G_n)}(1)$.  There is a deterministic $H_{\mathrm{KL}}\colon(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ such that $H_n(c)\to H_{\mathrm{KL}}(c)$ in probability for every fixed $c\ne1$, with $H_{\mathrm{KL}}(c)=0$ for $0<c<1$ and $H_{\mathrm{KL}}(c)>0$ for $c>1$; and at criticality $H_n(1)\to0$ in probability.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The Erd\H os--R\'enyi giant-cycle transition at $c=1$ is asserted to be simultaneously the transition from subextensive to extensive intersection-cohomology complexity of the random graphic matroid: by Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}(ii) forests contribute nothing and the carrier of entropy is the cycle-connected material, with the cycle calibration $k^{-1}\log P_{U_{k-1,k}}(1)\to\log3$ showing that sparse degree-two cyclic blocks already carry positive entropy density.  A proof of the critical clause requires a quantitative upper bound on $\log P_M(1)$ in terms of the size of the critical cyclic core, and a supercritical lower bound should use genuine direct-sum blocks or a proved comparison inequality rather than monotonicity under arbitrary minors, which is not available.  The nearest results are the matroid Kazhdan--Lusztig theory of Elias, Proudfoot, and Wakefield~\cite{EPW16}, the uniform-matroid formulas of Gedeon, Proudfoot, and Young~\cite{GedeonPY17}, and the deletion inequality of Braden and Vysogorets~\cite{BradenVysogorets20}.  A first decisive theorem would be the subcritical clause, where only bounded unicyclic complexity survives, or a lower bound for the giant cycle-connected core.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, an independent implementation of the defining recursion reproduced the closed cycle formula exactly through $k=25$ and the entropy sequence rising toward $\log3$.  A counterexample would be a supercritical density with subextensive Kazhdan--Lusztig complexity, or extensive complexity below the threshold.

\begin{conjecture}[Khovanov free energy of random braid closures]\label{aq3}
Fix $m\ge3$ and a finitely supported probability measure $\mu$ on the braid group $B_m$ whose induced walk is aperiodic on the symmetric-group quotient and whose support generates a subgroup whose image in $B_m/Z(B_m)$, acting on the $m$-punctured disc, is a nonelementary subgroup of its mapping class group.  Let $\beta_n=X_1\cdots X_n$ with $X_i$ i.i.d.\ $\mu$, let $L_n=\widehat{\beta_n}$ be the oriented closure, and with normalized oriented Khovanov bigradings over $\mathbb F_2$ set $Z_n(u,v)=\sum_{i,j}\dim_{\mathbb F_2}Kh^{i,j}(L_n;\mathbb F_2)\,e^{ui+vj}$.
