For every fixed $(u,v)\in\R^2$ there is a deterministic finite $F_\mu(u,v)$ with $n^{-1}\log Z_n(u,v)\to F_\mu(u,v)$ almost surely and in $L^1$, and $F_\mu$ is convex; in particular $n^{-1}\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}Kh(L_n;\mathbb F_2)\to F_\mu(0,0)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Finite-length convexity and linear boundedness are Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}(iii); the conjectural content is the deterministic limit itself, since closure and passage to homology destroy the subadditivity available at the chain level, so no Kingman-type argument applies directly, and differentiability of $F_\mu$, a large-deviation principle for the bigrading, and a variational characterization are separate later questions rather than hypotheses.  The nearest results are the categorified Jones polynomial of Khovanov~\cite{Khovanov00}, the Lyapunov theory of Alexander polynomials of random positive braids of Dunfield and Tiozzo~\cite{DunfieldTiozzo25}, and the polynomial-time algorithm for Khovanov homology of three-braid closures of Kelomaki and Sch\"utz~\cite{KelomakiSchutz26}, which makes direct testing at $m=3$ feasible.  A first decisive theorem would be the existence of the limit at $(u,v)=(0,0)$ for one nondegenerate walk on $B_3$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the decategorified reduced-Burau proxy at $t=-1$ gave a stable positive determinant exponent near $0.08$ on three-strand walks, a scale check that does not test the homological cancellation itself, the recorded gap.  A counterexample would be almost-sure oscillation of $n^{-1}\log\operatorname{rank}Kh$ between distinct limit points for a nondegenerate walk.

\begin{conjecture}[Two-sided thin-handle Hodge rare-event equivalence]\label{aq4}
Let $X_g$ be a closed genus-$g$ hyperbolic surface sampled from normalized Weil--Petersson volume, equip $H^1(X_g;\Z)$ with the Hodge $L^2$ norm, let $m_1(J(X_g))$ be the first successive minimum of the Jacobian lattice, and let $\ell_{\mathrm{ns}}(X_g)$ be the length of the shortest primitive nonseparating simple closed geodesic.  For every $\eta>0$,
\[
\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\ \lim_{g\to\infty}\ \Pp\!\left(\left|\frac{\pi\,m_1(J(X_g))^2}{\ell_{\mathrm{ns}}(X_g)}-1\right|>\eta\ \middle|\ \min\{\pi\,m_1(J(X_g))^2,\ \ell_{\mathrm{ns}}(X_g)\}\le\varepsilon\right)=0 .
\]
Consequently, with the short-geodesic law of Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}(iv), $\varepsilon^{-2}\Pp(\pi\,m_1(J(X_g))^2\le\varepsilon)\to\tfrac14$ in the same sequential limit.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
The two-sided conditioning is essential: conditioning only on a short geodesic controls the Hodge minimum when a thin handle is already known to exist but cannot exclude an anomalously short Hodge vector on a surface with no short geodesic, so the one-sided form does not imply the unconditional tail, while the displayed form asserts that whenever either quantity is anomalously small the same unique thin handle explains both, and then the $\varepsilon^2/4$ constant transfers.  The capacity normalization $\pi\,\mathrm{cap}(\ell)/\ell\to1$ fixes the factor $\pi$.  The nearest results are the Jacobian successive-minimum bounds from short geodesics of Muetzel~\cite{Muetzel12} and the Poisson length statistics of Mirzakhani and Petri~\cite{MirzakhaniPetri19}; the deterministic direction, that a short nonseparating geodesic forces a short Hodge vector, follows from the collar estimate, and the stochastic converse is the new content.  A first decisive theorem would be the one-sided conditional ratio law given $\ell_{\mathrm{ns}}\le\varepsilon$.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, the intensity integral and the collar capacity reproduced the constants $\tfrac14$ and $1$ to five decimals.  A counterexample would be a positive-probability family of Hodge-thin surfaces with no correspondingly thin handle; extensions to higher successive minima must condition on homological independence of the short curves, since bounding pairs make geometric disjointness insufficient.

\begin{conjecture}[Floer cancellation saturation for random Heegaard splittings]\label{aq5}
Fix $g\ge2$ and a finitely supported probability measure $\mu$ on the mapping class group of the closed genus-$g$ surface whose support generates it as a semigroup.  Let $\phi_n=X_1\cdots X_n$ with $X_i$ i.i.d.\ $\mu$, let $Y_n=H_g\cup_{\phi_n}H_g$ be the random Heegaard splitting, and let $Q_n=\{b_1(Y_n)=0\}$.  Define the excess Floer entropy $E_n=\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\widehat{HF}(Y_n)-\log|H_1(Y_n;\Z)|\ge0$.  Conditional on $Q_n$, $E_n/n\to0$ in probability; equivalently, whenever the homological torsion exponent $\alpha_\mu=\lim_n n^{-1}\log|H_1(Y_n;\Z)|$ exists in probability on $Q_n$, the Heegaard Floer rank satisfies $n^{-1}\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\widehat{HF}(Y_n)\to\alpha_\mu$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Significance.}
Nonnegativity of $E_n$ on $Q_n$ is Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}(v), and the conjecture asserts that the Heegaard Floer differential cancels every additional exponential contribution, so that the Floer rank grows at exactly the homological torsion rate; this is compatible with random splittings failing to be L-spaces, since $\operatorname{rank}\widehat{HF}/|H_1|$ may still diverge subexponentially, and the true subexponential scale of $E_n$ is the natural second question.  The nearest results are the random Heegaard splittings of Maher~\cite{Maher10}, the random-three-manifold model of Dunfield and Thurston~\cite{DunfieldThurston06} in which $b_1(Y_n)=0$ holds asymptotically almost surely so the conditioning is benign, and the non-L-space expectation for random splittings recorded in the problem literature~\cite{AFW3MG}.  A first decisive theorem would be any subexponential upper bound on $E_n$ for one nondegenerate walk, or the identity for a solvable subfamily.  In tests on the corpus described in the stress-test section, exact integral symplectic transvection walks reproduced a positive homological exponent near $0.19$, a calibration of the abelian shadow only, which cannot witness Floer cancellation, the recorded gap.  A counterexample would be a walk with $E_n\ge cn$ on $Q_n$ with positive probability, and such an excess exponent would itself be a new Floer-theoretic dynamical invariant.



\part*{Stress tests and independent recomputation}
\addcontentsline{toc}{part}{Stress tests and independent recomputation}\label{sec:stress}

Each statement was tested three ways: against the literature, against
computation well beyond its original range, and against an independent
reimplementation.

\emph{Layer 1: literature.}  Five independent searches combed OEIS,
arXiv, and the standard references for prior art, producing the novelty
labels and the attributions used throughout.  Each search
was run at neighbourhood depth: defining objects, derived sequences,
OEIS comments, and the abstracts and bodies of near-neighbour papers
read in full rather than skimmed from search summaries---the depth at
which, for instance, OEIS A088054's intersection comment
(Conjecture~\ref{c10}(ii)) and the second half of Lillie's abstract
(the primorial companion) are found, neither being visible in the
defining sequences or in a search snippet.  This layer also fixes two
attributions used above: the $k\ge1$ Stern list of
Conjecture~\ref{c14} is OEIS A060003 verbatim, with $1493$ the largest
known Stern prime, and the primorial-twin statement is Lillie's
\cite{Lillie}.

\emph{Layer 2: scripted refutation.}  Every
falsifiable-by-instance statement was pushed at least a decade past its
original bound: exception hunts across $(10^8,10^9]$ for
Conjectures~\ref{c15}, \ref{c14}, \ref{c17}, \ref{c13}; the uniformity
of Conjecture~\ref{c16} stressed on $d\le6000$; the statistical laws
re-tested at $4\times10^9$ (Conjectures~\ref{c21}, \ref{c25},
\ref{c18}, \ref{c19}, and~\ref{c20}, and the quintuplet calibration
count reported with Conjecture~\ref{c16}); the recovery clause of
Conjecture~\ref{c22} tested on fresh moduli $q\in(3000,6000]$.  No
statement moved.  The same layer settles one statement negatively: a
completeness list for Fibonacci--Lucas twins is destroyed by OEIS
A080327's catalogued index $148091$ (conditionally on the
probable-prime classifications of $F_{148091}$ and $L_{148091}$
alike, neither being a proven prime), which is why
Conjecture~\ref{c9} conjectures finiteness without a completeness
clause and carries that index as its calibration clause.

Each statement was also verified at large scale: the
Conjecture~\ref{c1} profile across $150$ shifts and the moment law for
its constants $C(d)$ (derived mean $2.7456$ and sd $1.6840$ against
measured $2.7434$ and $1.6726$); the cubic family moments and
uniformity of Conjecture~\ref{c2} ($294$ constants, $57$ count
profiles); the triplet and sexy-pair races of Conjectures~\ref{c3}
and~\ref{c7} at $10^9$ and the Stern lanes of Conjecture~\ref{c14} on
$2{,}500$ samples at $10^8$; the chain of Conjecture~\ref{c6} over five
decades to $10^7$; the null race of Conjecture~\ref{c8} at $10^7$; the
Fibonacci--Lucas joint scan to $p\le10^4$; factorial twins to $n=700$;
the CRT-exact factorization of Conjecture~\ref{c11} through a joint
period of $1.2\times10^8$, with the scan extended to $n=6000$; the
pinned average $G(H)$ of Conjecture~\ref{c12} computed exactly to
$H=3000$; the boundary trichotomy of Conjecture~\ref{c13} with two new
lanes counted at $10^6$; the least-summand law of
Conjecture~\ref{c15} on $2{,}000$ samples; the covariance kernels of
Conjectures~\ref{c16}(ii) and~\ref{c24}(ii) evaluated over $870$ and
$1{,}225$ pairs, with the moving-window randomization of
Conjecture~\ref{c16}(ii) over $2000$ windows (empirical correlation
matrix matching the predicted kernel entrywise at $0.86$); the
orientation-resolved twin-member profile of Conjecture~\ref{c17} on
$150$ samples; the race autocorrelation and running-maximum
measurements of Conjecture~\ref{c18} at $10^9$ against simulated
nulls; the singular-series waiting-time clause of
Conjecture~\ref{c19}(iii) (regression coefficient $-0.466$ against the
predicted $-\tfrac12$); the stratified experiment of
Conjecture~\ref{c22} on $80$ moduli; the multibase quotient tests of
Conjecture~\ref{c23} on $664{,}577$ primes; and the weighted drift and
internal null lane of Conjecture~\ref{c25} on $400$ fresh samples,
together with the cousin-race predictions of the contamination
calculus, Conjecture~\ref{c21}(v), at $10^9$ (leadership log-densities
$0.99$ and $0.92$ on the predicted sides).  In each case the
prediction was derived before the corresponding data were taken.

\emph{Layer 3: independent replication.}  Constants were recomputed
from their definitions, and sequences recounted, by implementations
sharing no code with the primary computation and working from the bare
statements alone.  All recomputed constants landed inside the stated
truncation error, and all recounts agreed.  The same layer reproduced
the Fibonacci deficit recorded at Conjecture~\ref{c9} and the ordering
anomaly of Remark~\ref{r:c22}, confirming that both are properties of
the primes rather than of a single implementation.

One methodological conclusion is worth recording.  The mathematical
failure modes in this subject are not statistical but \emph{algebraic}:
factorizations and congruence collapses living on density-zero or
positive-density-but-structured subsequences---the cubes obstructing
$n=p+k^3$ (Theorem~\ref{t:cube}), the composite-$k$ factorization of
$D_k$ (Conjecture~\ref{c4}(i)), the $k=4$ parity branch of
Conjecture~\ref{c5}, the inadmissible naive chain of
Conjecture~\ref{c6}.  Probabilistic sanity checks, however extensive,
integrate over density and cannot see such families; only structural
tests---testing a claimed exception census on special subsequences, for
instance---find them.  A verification that only re-runs an existing
count at a larger bound is blind to every one of them.

\emph{Part IV.}  The Part IV verification programme follows the same standard.  The rank formula of Proposition~\ref{u:rank} was checked against direct linear algebra over $\Fq_2$, $\Fq_3$, and $\Fq_5$ on eighteen thousand random pairs of a graph and an element before the proof was written.  The irreducibility claim of Conjecture~\ref{u1} was verified by exact factorization over $\Z$ for all $996$ connected graphs on at most seven vertices.  The recovery statements of Conjectures~\ref{u2}, \ref{u9}, and~\ref{u10} were tested on every known collision class of $C_G$: the $119$ classes among the $1252$ graphs on at most seven vertices, a randomized eight-vertex corpus, the unique class among all $3159$ trees on fourteen vertices, refound independently by exhaustive search, and the first unicyclic collision at ten vertices, with $Q_G$, $\gamma$, and $i$ agreeing in every class.  The rigidity statements were scanned exhaustively on at most seven vertices, with six thousand random eight-vertex graphs added for Conjecture~\ref{u3} and the scan for Conjecture~\ref{u5} restricted to graphs with at least four edges, and the class-restricted statements were tested on six-thousand-graph random holdouts for each of Conjectures~\ref{u6}, \ref{u7}, and~\ref{u8}, spanning $2747$, $3192$, and $5598$ distinct binary specializations respectively, together with all $656$ binary classes of ten-vertex unicyclic graphs for Conjecture~\ref{u7}.  The log-concavity and support statements of Conjectures~\ref{u11} to~\ref{u15} were verified on the full atlas of graphs on at most seven vertices and twenty-five hundred random graphs on eight to ten vertices, with the eight-vertex counterexample to the second-order slice strengthening reconfirmed by the independent implementation.  The tree programme of Conjectures~\ref{u16} to~\ref{u20} was verified exhaustively over all trees through fourteen vertices, for Conjectures~\ref{u17} and~\ref{u18} with $q\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ through twelve vertices, $q\in\{2,3\}$ at thirteen, and $q=2$ at fourteen, and the sharpness failure at $(n,q)=(4,2)$ recorded at Conjecture~\ref{u17} was found in this verification rather than assumed.  A seven-vertex pair refutes Conjecture~\ref{u7}, below the ten-to-thirteen-vertex range of those holdouts.  An exhaustive rescan locates it as the unique violating class among trees and connected unicyclic graphs through nine vertices, and the tree case was reverified exhaustively through fourteen vertices.

\emph{Part V.}  The Part V verification programme follows the same standard, on an independently generated corpus of all $87$ unlabelled posets on at most five points, over $\Fq_2$ and $\Fq_3$ fully and $\Fq_5$ to dimension six, cross-checked against the deposited enumerators.  The calibration identity of Proposition~\ref{v:calib} held with no exception.  The determination statements were tested on every adjoint-collision class: the adjoint-to-Kirillov determination of Conjecture~\ref{v1} held across $64$ classes, and the lower-central factor vector, $\dim\operatorname{Der}$, and $\dim\operatorname{Cent}$ of Conjectures~\ref{v2}, \ref{v4}, and~\ref{v6} were constant on every class.  The characteristic statements of Conjectures~\ref{v7} and~\ref{v8} were confirmed by agreement of the attained adjoint-rank and Kirillov-rank sets across $\Fq_2$, $\Fq_3$, and $\Fq_5$ in every case, the two-field rigidity of Conjecture~\ref{v9} forced equality at $q=5$ across $16$ three-field collision classes, and the adjoint field monotonicity of Conjecture~\ref{v10} held as first-order dominance in all $221$ field-pair tests while its likelihood-ratio strengthening failed.  The centre-one statements were tested on all $43$ centre-one records, where the Kirillov enumerator determined the adjoint enumerator, $R_{P,q}$ had nonnegative integer coefficients, and $R_{P,q}$ had interval support and was unimodal throughout this corpus, with log-concavity failing four times.  The unimodality was subsequently refuted by a seven-point poset outside the corpus, and Conjecture~\ref{v14} is recorded as resolved false.  The forest statements were tested on the forest class, where the Kirillov enumerator determined the adjoint enumerator across $44$ forest-collision classes, the Kirillov support filled every even rank up to $b_K$, the even-rank sequence was unimodal, and the bound $b_K\le 2b_A$ held everywhere while the unrestricted bound failed fourteen times off the forest class.  The unitriangular strict log-concavity of Conjecture~\ref{v19} was confirmed for $\mathrm{ut}_4$, $\mathrm{ut}_5$, and $\mathrm{ut}_6$ over $\Fq_2$, for $\mathrm{ut}_4$ and $\mathrm{ut}_5$ over $\Fq_3$, and for $\mathrm{ut}_4$ over $\Fq_5$, and the incidence anticorrelation of Conjecture~\ref{v20} gave negative covariance on every nonabelian poset and exactly zero on all sixteen abelian ones.  Two statements were not independently recomputed: the cohomology recoveries of Conjectures~\ref{v3} and~\ref{v5} rest on the deposited computation of $H^2$ and $H^3$ (ordinary) and $H^1$, $H^2$, and $H^3$ (adjoint), our reverification having not recomputed Lie-algebra cohomology.  Three statements, Conjectures~\ref{v3}, \ref{v5}, and~\ref{v9}, are supported only by the restricted tests recorded with each, and their general forms should not be read as carrying evidence comparable to the other conjectures.  Two further statements, Conjectures~\ref{v11} and~\ref{v14}, are false as stated and are recorded as resolved false with the seven-point counterexamples given in their resolutions.

\emph{Part VI.}  The Part VI verification programme follows the same standard, on an arithmetic cache of every integer through $20{,}000{,}000$ with segmented exact scans and an odd-only prime-neighbour sieve to $4\times10^9$, cross-checked by an independent deterministic Miller--Rabin implementation sharing no code with the primary scans.  The compass frequencies of Conjectures~\ref{w1} to~\ref{w6} were measured over the polygonal centres through $4\times10^9$, the local-sieve model of Conjecture~\ref{w1} correlating with the order-level bias at $0.896$ across $3\le s\le100$ and every promoted direction replicated on a holdout above $10^9$.  The radical order-pattern laws of Conjectures~\ref{w7} and~\ref{w8} were computed exactly through $10^9$, the chi-square against uniformity rising from $0.45$ at length four to about $2.1\times10^7$ at length five and the pattern ratio settling at $13.31$, with the length-four and length-five cell counts reproduced by a second implementation.  Proposition~\ref{w:raddens} now proves existence of every fixed-length conditional density, leaving nonuniformity open at each length at least five.  Proposition~\ref{w:trihex} proves that triangular and hexagonal centres have identical residue laws and local compass frequencies at every finite sieve depth.  The order constants of Conjectures~\ref{w9} to~\ref{w13} were measured over $2\times10^7$ triples across seven disjoint blocks, and the five-term totient barrier of Conjecture~\ref{w11}, since resolved false by G.~Martin's theorem, showed no run below $4\times10^9$ in an exact segmented scan, while its abundancy analogue fell within the same scan to an increasing five-term run at $n=36{,}721{,}681$.  The shock statements of Conjectures~\ref{w14} to~\ref{w19} were checked over millions of steps per family against the exact jump identities of Proposition~\ref{w:jump}, the lag-one covariances negative in all $22$ tested families.  Proposition~\ref{w:shock} now proves Conjectures~\ref{w14} to~\ref{w16} outright, with explicit six-prime witnesses reaching $J_{3,n}=-20$, $J_{4,n}=-30$, and $J_{3,n}=+21$, beyond every scanned extreme, and Conjecture~\ref{w19} follows from the same identities through the multivariate Erd\H{o}s--Kac theorem of~\cite{ELS22}.  Proposition~\ref{w:cov53} evaluates the truncated lag-one covariance of the central-binomial slice at exactly $-\tfrac53$ for every cutoff at least $3$, confirmed numerically to five decimals at $2\times10^6$, the full covariance standing at $-1.47$ and drifting toward the constant.  Proposition~\ref{w:k2slope} now proves the $k=2$ case of Conjecture~\ref{w18}.  The boundary law of Conjecture~\ref{w20} matched its truncated Euler sum at correlation $0.998$ across the $39$ gaps with at least $500$ samples, with block-level correlations from $0.986$ to $0.997$.  Six of the twenty state a bias as a numerical band rather than a derived constant, and Conjectures~\ref{w6} and~\ref{w17} extrapolate in a parameter rather than the index, so their general forms should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part VII.}  The Part VII verification programme rests on exact integer computation throughout: truncated integer power series for the Chern-class evaluation, gcd--lcm inclusion-exclusion for the Milnor--Orlik formula, $\mathbf F_2$ Gaussian elimination for induced clique-complex homology with exact fraction-free Routh--Hurwitz determinants, and signed-orbit counting for the exterior actions, every calibration reproduced by a second implementation sharing no code with the primary scans, which recovered the quintic $-200$, the K3 value $24$, the Poincar\'e-sphere $0$, the empty-graph strand $6z^2+8z^3+3z^4$, and the $-I_4$ profile $(1,0,6,0,1)$.  The Euler laws of Conjectures~\ref{x1} to~\ref{x5} were tested on the complete configuration census through dimension $30$, the merges numbering $1{,}568{,}731$, the ladder exact through $n=200$, and the gcd law reverified independently through dimension $26$.  The cap extrema of Conjectures~\ref{x6} and~\ref{x7} are complete exact-cap censuses through caps $50$ and $40$ with the $A=12$ transition value $222$ reverified, and the scale laws of Conjectures~\ref{x9} and~\ref{x10} cover $52{,}593$ tuples at scales through $10$, with independent random rechecks one scale beyond.  The strand laws of Conjectures~\ref{x11} to~\ref{x15} were tested on $34{,}867$ graphs, exhaustive over labeled graphs through six vertices with $250$ deterministic holdouts at each order seven to ten, giving $50{,}454$ strands, and reverified independently on an exhaustive labeled corpus through five vertices.  The monodromy laws of Conjectures~\ref{x16} to~\ref{x20} cover all $57{,}758$ orientation-preserving signed cycle types through dimension $21$, with every type through dimension $11$ and the minimum $160$ at dimension $12$ reverified independently against Proposition~\ref{x:orbit}.  Six adversarial controls are retained in place, each refuting a tempting strengthening.  Two of the twenty, the limit clause of Conjecture~\ref{x1} and Conjecture~\ref{x19}, assert limits, and Conjectures~\ref{x4} and~\ref{x8} lie close to classical methods, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.  Since deposit, Conjectures~\ref{x1} and~\ref{x2} have been resolved true and Conjecture~\ref{x19} resolved false, the Landau floor of Proposition~\ref{x:landau} fixing the compression exponent at $2$ while the deposited minima respect the floor with room to spare.  Proposition~\ref{x:ehrhart} now identifies every scale sequence as a sum of interior Ehrhart counts of $N-1$ integral weighted hypersimplices, proving Conjecture~\ref{x9} and the convexity clause of Conjecture~\ref{x10}, with an independent exact stress of $24{,}950{,}000$ scale inequalities on $25{,}000$ random tuples finding no violation of the surviving log-concavity clause.  Proposition~\ref{x:qladder} proves all three ladder clauses with the sharpening $8-Q_{n+1}/Q_n\sim4/n$, and its exact recurrence reproduces the deposited ladder through $n=200$.  Proposition~\ref{x:merge} proves every normalised merge inequality by a positive coefficient identity, independently checked through dimension $18$.

\emph{Part VIII.}  The Part VIII verification programme is exact wherever its statements are: integer Chern-coefficient evaluation for the ambient products, integer expansion of G\"ottsche's product, exact age histograms, exact subset-sum functionals with rational arithmetic, and $\mathbf F_2$ homology of matroid independence complexes with exact rational Routh tests, every calibration reproduced by a second implementation sharing no code with the primary scans, which recovered the quintic, K3, and tetraquadric values, the $\operatorname{Hilb}^2(\mathrm{K3})$ Betti row $(1,23,276,23,1)$, and the moment identities of Proposition~\ref{y:mom} in exact rational arithmetic.  The dominance and refinement laws of Conjectures~\ref{y1} to~\ref{y4} were tested on $42{,}691$ moves, $42{,}861$ splits, and $24{,}680$ disjoint split squares through dimension $22$, reverified independently through dimension $18$ with the four dimension-five violations of the unqualified Conjecture~\ref{y4} reproduced exactly.  The profile laws of Conjectures~\ref{y5} to~\ref{y8} rest on $179{,}200$, $53{,}070$, and $48{,}384$ exact inequalities for $b\le30$ and $n\le80$, with the complete kurtosis phase diagram of Conjecture~\ref{y7} reverified independently through $n=50$.  The age laws of Conjectures~\ref{y9} to~\ref{y12} combine an exact census of $450{,}999$ admissible weight multisets with $r\le60$, reverified on $58{,}393$ multisets with $r\le40$, with seeded Monte Carlo in four regimes whose lattice-corrected Kolmogorov distances $0.0398$ to $0.0162$ were independently recomputed as $0.0344$ and $0.0178$.  The entropy laws of Conjectures~\ref{y13} to~\ref{y16} were tested on $16{,}200$ random and $48{,}512$ exact integer spectra, the $222$ equality cases all two-valued, with an independent exhaustive recount through $d=7$ finding $122$ two-valued equality cases.  Propositions~\ref{y:upper} and~\ref{y:lower} now prove Conjectures~\ref{y15} and~\ref{y16}.  The former matroid sample did not contain the two graphic certificates now built into the exact checker.  Proposition~\ref{y:k33} refutes Conjectures~\ref{y17}, \ref{y18}, and~\ref{y20}, while Proposition~\ref{y:rhombus} refutes Conjecture~\ref{y19}.  The limit clauses of Conjectures~\ref{y3} and~\ref{y7} and the random-model statements of Conjectures~\ref{y10} to~\ref{y12} are recorded where they occur, and Conjecture~\ref{y9} carries an attribution, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part IX.}  The Part IX verification programme is exact wherever its statements are: tubings enumerated exhaustively with integer $f$-to-$h$ conversion, $\mathbf F_2$ homology of flag complexes by integer rank, sector functionals by deterministic convolution over exactly enumerated sectors, and boundary maps assembled as integer matrices, while root locations, Mahler measures, and pseudodeterminants are floating-point spectral computations, every calibration reproduced by a second implementation sharing no code with the primary scans, which recovered the Narayana and Eulerian endpoint $h$-polynomials, the matrix-tree value $\operatorname{pdet}=5^4$ for the complete graph on five vertices, and both identities of Proposition~\ref{z:logsine}, the sine product exactly and the moment integral to $10^{-6}$.  The toric laws of Conjectures~\ref{z1} to~\ref{z5} were tested on $878$ deposited root sets, $3{,}621$ connected deletions, $3{,}956$ edge additions with minimum Mahler increment $0.0263$ and exact integer tail margins, and $1{,}857$ tree tests, reverified independently on all $771$ labelled connected graphs through five vertices, $2{,}971$ deletions, $3{,}227$ edge additions, and every labelled tree through six vertices.  The McKay laws of Conjectures~\ref{z6} to~\ref{z10} were tested on $3{,}135$ deposited profiles, $2{,}905$ of them at $d\ge5$, reverified by an independent exhaustive census of $379$ distinct-weight profiles at $p\in\{7,11,13\}$ that reproduced the two repeated-weight controls and the two-crest $\beta_3$ control exactly.  The torsion laws of Conjectures~\ref{z11}, \ref{z12}, and~\ref{z15} rest on $40{,}932$, $6{,}822$, and $20{,}466$ admissible deposited triples with extreme curvatures $0.0079$, $0.0770$, and $-0.0076$, reverified independently at five $(p,d)$ pairs with the $s=-2$ control curvature $+0.4980$ reproduced to six decimals over the exactly verified centering identity; the parabola of Conjecture~\ref{z13} matched four exact dynamic-programming regimes with central root-mean-square errors $0.027$ to $0.038$, and the decoupling of Conjecture~\ref{z14} was checked on three seeded ensembles of up to $60{,}480$ character samples whose empirical correlations below $5\times10^{-16}$ reproduce the exact zero forced by the involution, the informative diagnostics being the variances and fourth moments, which moved toward Gaussian values.  The entropy laws of Conjectures~\ref{z16} to~\ref{z20} were tested on a corpus of $130$ spheres and $225$ stellar pairs supplying $262$, $392$, $130$, $900$, and $450$ comparisons in statement order, with minimum log-concavity margins $51.8$ and $17.8$ and minimum stellar increment $1.42$, reverified independently through dimension four.  The iterated-limit clause of Conjecture~\ref{z13} and the random-model clause of Conjecture~\ref{z14} are recorded where they occur, and Conjectures~\ref{z1}, \ref{z5}, \ref{z8}, \ref{z13}, and~\ref{z14} are close to prior work, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part X.}  The Part X verification programme is exact wherever its statements are: characteristic-two and finite-field cohomology by exact elimination, integral torsion by Smith normal form through dimension nine, and every $\chi_y$-coefficient, signature, merge inequality, ratio, and gcd in exact integer or rational arithmetic, while characteristic-zero ranks beyond dimension nine are dual large-prime proxies and the root, Mahler, and radius laws are floating-point spectral checks, every calibration reproduced by a second implementation sharing no code with the primary scans, which recomputed the $\chi_y$-profiles from the scaled Hirzebruch series with the signature recovered as $\chi_{y=1}$ and reproduced the K3 profile $(2,20,2)$, the quintic profile, and the dimension-two signature $16$.  The support obstructions of Proposition~\ref{aa:support} were checked independently: the deposited profile admits at most one unused coordinate through $n=120$, the rescaling criterion was confirmed on all $1{,}073$ spanning supports through six coordinates with no exception, and the retained coefficient control was recomputed in exact rational arithmetic, its two profiles separated exactly by the vanishing Pfaffian.  Proposition~\ref{aa:coverage} now pins the subcritical side of the sparse threshold at every fixed $c<2$ by a second-moment coverage argument.  The flux laws of Conjectures~\ref{aa1} to~\ref{aa8} rest on $144$ dense trials, $960$ sparse trials, $2{,}800$ finite-field samples, eight explicit witnesses, and complete-flux scans for $4\le n\le13$ with sixteen exact Smith trials, reverified independently with $71$ of $72$ dense hits, all eight witnesses, exhaustive support minimality at $n=5,6$, sparse transition rates $0/36$, $5/36$, $34/36$ at $c=1,4,10$, the characteristic-three excesses $2$, $4$, $28$ at $n=11,12,13$, the exact torsion staircase through $n=9$, and twelve universal-coefficient torsion counts with an order-four factor confirming the non-elementary control.  Proposition~\ref{aa:flux} was then checked against those scans from scratch: an independent brute-force computation of the integral cohomology, using no part of the normal form, reproduced its predictions in every degree at $p=2,3,5$ through $n=13$, and at $n=15$ in degree nine returned rational rank $3003$, $911$ even invariant factors, and exactly one divisible by four, the summand $\Z/4$ refuting Conjecture~\ref{aa7}.  The profile laws of Conjectures~\ref{aa9} to~\ref{aa15} rest on $680$ configurations with $7{,}124$, $110{,}777$, $47{,}433$, and $6{,}540$ exact and $369$, $4{,}267$, and $2{,}102$ numerical deposited tests through dimension $14$, reverified independently with matching configuration and inequality counts, zero violations, and the smallest root separation $1.276\times10^{-3}$ reproduced to six decimals.  The signature laws of Conjectures~\ref{aa16} to~\ref{aa20} rest on $8{,}190$ configurations, $302{,}130$ and $80{,}294$ exact merge tests, $29$ exact ratios through $n=60$, and all thirteen even-dimensional gcds, reverified independently in full, including the $n=14$ spike and $R_{58}=26.55045876$.  The random models of Conjectures~\ref{aa1}, \ref{aa2}, \ref{aa4}, and~\ref{aa8}, the beyond-computation statement of Conjecture~\ref{aa5}, the numerical evidence of Conjectures~\ref{aa12}, \ref{aa14}, and~\ref{aa15}, and the attributions of Conjectures~\ref{aa8}, \ref{aa13}, and~\ref{aa19} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.  Since deposit, Conjecture~\ref{aa19} has been resolved true by the proof of Proposition~\ref{aa:quad}, whose generating function and recurrence are certified by exact symbolic identities and cross-checked against the exact signature ladder through $n=60$; a further exact scan through $n=10{,}000$, redundant given the proof, confirmed what it guarantees.  The block generalization of Proposition~\ref{aa:blocks} was verified by exact extraction against the Hirzebruch signatures at fourteen block-repetition pairs through dimension $14$, with the saddle constants $\Lambda_4$ and $\Lambda_6$ matched to ten digits and sixteen blocks at five exact ratios each showing no violation of the open monotonicity question.

\emph{Part XI.}  The Part XI spectral scans are floating-point eigensolver checks, on exhaustively generated corpora: all trees through twelve vertices at nine R\'enyi orders, all unicyclic graphs and all connected bipartite graphs through seven vertices with holdouts through thirty vertices, and every eligible local move on each corpus member, giving $8{,}775$ path and $8{,}775$ star comparisons with smallest margins $2.23\times10^{-4}$ and $4.72\times10^{-4}$, $86{,}982$ leaf-pair, $70{,}126$ subdivision, and $15{,}385$ leaf-compression comparisons with smallest margins $1.66\times10^{-3}$, $6.12\times10^{-2}$, and $9.31\times10^{-4}$, and $6{,}230$ unicyclic, $168{,}168$ tree-extension, $10{,}884$ general-extension, $465$ bipartite-minimum, $5{,}322$ biclique-window, and $2{,}245$ cycle-maximum comparisons, with zero violations on the asserted ranges.  A second implementation sharing no code with the deposited scans rebuilt both entropy functionals from scratch and reproduced zero violations in $3{,}031$ comparisons each for the path and star laws through eleven vertices, $14{,}252$ leaf-pair and $11{,}249$ subdivision comparisons, all tree extensions through ten vertices, $7{,}672$ general-extension window comparisons, and exhaustive unicyclic and bipartite scans through seven vertices, and reproduced the deposited boundary controls to the digit: the leaf-move excess $7.65\times10^{-7}$ and the unicyclic excess $6.62\times10^{-4}$ at order $0.1$, the order-five and order-ten subdivision decreases $1.00\times10^{-2}$ and $2.02\times10^{-3}$, and the order-ten pendant decrease $2.32\times10^{-2}$; the same verification found the exact four-vertex min-entropy tie now recorded in Conjecture~\ref{ab5}.  The carry programme is exact integer arithmetic throughout, valuations computed from Legendre digit sums: the exact block-mean formula of Proposition~\ref{ab:carry} was verified exhaustively for $p=3$ through $k=8$, $p=5$ through $k=6$, and $p=7$ through $k=5$, and the deposited diagnostics at two million integers, marginal means and variances tracking the chain law, all pairwise correlations among $p\in\{3,5,7,11\}$ below $0.08$, covariances below $0.24$, modular discrepancies below $10^{-3}$ at moduli two and three, mixed third and fourth cumulants of order one, and multiplier correlations below $0.11$ at half a million integers, were reproduced by an independent run at one million integers with variance slopes $0.4766$, $0.3400$, $0.3146$, and $0.2774$ against the limits $1/2$, $3/8$, $1/3$, and $3/10$ for $p=3,5,7,11$, correlations below $0.04$, modulus-two discrepancy $2.5\times10^{-3}$, multiplier-three correlations below $0.04$, and Landau-ratio variance slopes $0.339$ and $0.332$ at $p=7,11$ with cross-correlation $-0.016$.  The nine carry statements are limit laws, Conjecture~\ref{ab20} is a programme statement, and the attributions of Conjectures~\ref{ab1} and~\ref{ab12} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part XII.}  The Part XII graph and spectral scans are floating-point checks.  The subdivision programme was calibrated on degree and spectral moments of iterated barycentric refinements: the deposited scans run seven refinement depths in dimension two and a tetrahedral Hodge probe in dimension three, and the independent recomputation, a from-scratch implementation of subdivision as the order complex of the face poset, reproduces the supercritical moment ratio $2.675$ against the predicted $16/6$ at depth seven from three different starting complexes including a non-manifold book, the two-dimensional Hodge pattern with degree-one maxima doubling and top-degree maxima converging to six, and the three-dimensional probe maxima $75.0645$, $15.7366$, and $7.8794$ to the deposited digits; the tail counts of Conjecture~\ref{ac4} are uninformative at reachable depth, and that statement rests on mechanism alone.  The spanning-tree programme is exact arithmetic on closed formulas cross-checked against direct pseudoinverse and matrix-tree computation to $1.1\times10^{-13}$: the deposited scans cover the connected atlas through seven vertices, all complete multipartite partitions through twenty-four, family optimization through $n=10^7$, and seeded edge-toggle climbs through twelve vertices; the independent recomputation reproduces the atlas maximizers and the bridgeless cycle minimum, reproduces the seventeen-vertex bipartite crossover values $8.315588550473$ and $8.350120011590$ to twelve digits, extends the exhaustive multipartite check to all $89{,}133$ partitions at $n=45$, adds all theta graphs through forty vertices and one hundred eighty-three structured and random bridgeless graphs with zero violations, runs core-density, periphery-matching, and two-core adversaries at thirty and forty vertices, all falling below the split optimum, and finds hill climbs from random starts at twelve and sixteen vertices landing exactly on the split value, with the family scales $r^*/\sqrt{n/\log n}=0.92$ and deficit ratio $1.14$ at $n=10^7$ drifting toward one.  Within the split family the scale is now derived, a promotion: at $r=c\sqrt{n/\log n}$ the deficit is $((c+1/c)/2+o(1))\sqrt{n\log n}$, uniquely minimized at $c=1$, so the family clauses hold and the content is the global reduction.  The cyclic programme is genuine cyclic convolution throughout: the deposited scans use fast-Fourier convolution at three primes, and the independent recomputation, with its own transform code, puts discrete Gaussians on the doubling floor to $10^{-6}$ at two primes and four widths, reproduces the full extra half-log-two penalty of the separated-bump control, holds the fixed-$m$ floor across six families and a three-hundred-draw adversarial mixture search with minimum excess zero, matches the wrap-crossover total variation at machine roundoff for Gaussian inputs and at $4.6\times10^{-7}$ falling to $1.0\times10^{-9}$ for a lazy-walk input at up to $9{,}604{,}801$ convolutions with entropy defects matching the heat-kernel target to five decimals, and holds the uniform monotonicity margin nonnegative through one thousand summands at $p=2{,}000{,}003$ and wrap ratio $2.5\times10^{-8}$.  The graphon programme's deposited simulations are row-signature resolution proxies and are recorded as such, not as measurements of sampled-graph entropy; the independent recomputation adds an exact enumeration of the threshold-graphon law through seven vertices, whose support sizes $46$, $332$, $2{,}874$, and $29{,}024$ match the labeled threshold-graph counts exactly and whose linear entropy correction $-0.60$ per vertex confirms the negative control of Proposition~\ref{ac:threshold}.  Conjectures~\ref{ac4}, \ref{ac5}, and~\ref{ac19} are deposited on mechanism with their evidence gaps on record, and the attributions of Conjectures~\ref{ac3} and~\ref{ac14} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part XIII.}  The Part XIII flux and torsion scans are exact arithmetic throughout.  The deposited computation ran sixty dense degree-five sign trials and sparse sweeps at $n=9,10$, exact torsion profiles through $n=11$, exact Gopakumar--Vafa invariants through degree sixty on all five merge edges with $495$ conifold-fraction Yukawa tests and the raw-instanton adversarial control failing at every grid point, a $1{,}900$-comparison mirror-map scan through dimension nine, and the insertion-power enumeration through $m=4$, a signed sum over $76{,}545$ regular families.  The independent recomputation, sharing no code with it, reproduced the degree-five saturation on twenty-four fresh trials at $n=9,10$; rebuilt the complete-flux torsion from exact modular and rational ranks through $n=12$ at $p=2,3,5$, confirming interval support, shifted duality, and strict log-concavity on every nonzero profile, including $1,10,44,10,1$ at $n=11$ and $1,11,54,54,11,1$ at $n=12$, with totals $T_2=1,2,10,20,66,132$ and $T_3=1,2$, and verified the closed-form two-primary expression to strict growth through $n=200$; recomputed the torsion profiles from the normal form of Proposition~\ref{aa:flux}, finding interval support exactly $2p+1$ to $n-2p+2$ and no log-concavity failure for every prime $p\le23$ through $n=150$, and strict growth of $T_p$ for every $p\le11$ over the same range; reimplemented the full hypergeometric mirror computation from scratch, matching the five known degree-one invariants $2875$, $1280$, $1053$, $720$, $512$ exactly, finding zero log-convexity or amplification violations through degree twenty-four, evaluating the five conifold constants to sixty digits as $1/q_c=1980.146$, $641.778$, $458.890$, $269.607$, $159.255$ with strict ordering along every edge, and passing the normalized Yukawa comparison at nineteen fractions per edge; verified the five Chern floors of Proposition~\ref{ad:merge} analytically; ran an independent $588$-comparison mirror-map contraction scan in dimensions three to five with zero violations; and reran the deposited insertion enumeration with all coefficients matching.  Conjectures~\ref{ad13} to~\ref{ad19} assert laws, the attributions of Remark~\ref{ad:kraines} and Conjectures~\ref{ad10} and~\ref{ad19} are recorded where they occur, and the raw-instanton control of Conjecture~\ref{ad9} is retained in place, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part XIV.}  The Part XIV verification programme is exact throughout: integer Chern-class series for every complete-intersection Euler characteristic, the thirteen published Betti tables of $\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1$ reverified file by file against the primary dataset, and integer convolution for every hypersurface Hodge vector, all comparisons in exact rational arithmetic, the calibrations recovering the quintic $-200$, the K3 profile $(1,19,1)$, and the quintic-threefold profile $(1,101,101,1)$.  The convexity laws of Conjectures~\ref{ae1} to~\ref{ae6} were tested on the exhaustive grid of dimensions through ten, codimensions through four, and degrees through seven, $482{,}150$ comparisons, and on an adversarial extension of $424{,}357$ further comparisons with dimensions through sixteen and degrees through sixty, with no failure.  The tables behind Conjectures~\ref{ae7} to~\ref{ae11} were pinned by the antidiagonal identity of Proposition~\ref{ae:strand} in every internal degree, with projective dimensions, quadric counts, and the canonical counts $(a-1)(b-1)$ all matching; the forty-eight nonlinear and one hundred two pre-mode linear triples were strictly log-concave, the eight defects locked as stated, and the eight rational-normal-scroll tables at $a=1$, outside the stated range, were defect-free with empty nonlinear rows, consistent with Conjecture~\ref{ae10} from the boundary.  The dispersion laws of Conjectures~\ref{ae12} to~\ref{ae15} were tested on the grid of dimensions through thirty and degrees through sixty, $88{,}334$ comparisons, and on an extension through dimension eighty-three and degree eighty, $195{,}234$ further comparisons, with no failure, the coordinatewise overshoot control at dimension twelve and the cubic--quartic coincidence reproduced exactly, and the total-variation distances falling to $2\times10^{-3}$ by degree three hundred.  The small-corpus caveats of Conjectures~\ref{ae7} to~\ref{ae11} and the beyond-any-finite-check statements of Conjectures~\ref{ae12} to~\ref{ae15} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.

\emph{Part XV.}  The Part XV verification programme is exact throughout and independent of the deposited candidate scans: fresh enumerators for square-lattice walks, bridges, and $d$-dimensional counts, agreeing with the deposited data files entry by entry wherever they overlap, with every inequality checked in integer arithmetic and both coupling laws certified by exact integer maximum flows via Strassen's theorem.  The curvature law of Conjecture~\ref{af1} was checked against the published counts through $n=79$, largest ratio $\rho_{77}=0.99977583$; the joint laws of Conjectures~\ref{af2} and~\ref{af5} to~\ref{af12} on complete enumerations through $n=21$, with $c_{21}=2{,}408{,}806{,}028$ walks at the top length and five exact joint tables per length; the bridge laws of Conjectures~\ref{af3} and~\ref{af4} through $n=23$, $b_{23}=862{,}447{,}881$, extending the deposited range by seven lengths; and the dimension laws of Conjectures~\ref{af14} and~\ref{af15} in exact rational arithmetic across $2\le d\le10$, through $n=14$ at $d\le3$, smallest survival gap $6.3\times10^{-4}$ and smallest moment gap $1.8\times10^{-4}$.  The calibration propositions were verified both symbolically and against the enumerations: the four bridge diagonals and both corner minors at every length through $n=23$, the survival polynomials against eleven dimensions with the axis-grouping expansion overdetermined by three data points, and the monotonicity numerators expanded with every coefficient nonnegative.  All four negative controls reproduce exactly: the endpoint-coordinate quadrant violation at $n=3$, the radial-law crossings between adjacent dimensions, the bridge equalities $b_2^2-b_1b_3=b_4^2-b_3b_5=2$, and the oscillating curvature roots, which run $2.40,1.88,1.80,2.15,2.14,1.82,2.48$ from $n=4$ before settling near $2.0$ through $n=19$.  The attribution and consolidation notes of Conjectures~\ref{af1} and~\ref{af13} are recorded where they occur.

\emph{Part XVI.}  The Part XVI verification programme replaced the deposited sanity probes by optimizer-level computation throughout.  The skewness law of Conjecture~\ref{ag1} was checked with exact tilted-cumulant perturbation theory, Drazin-inverse formulas with no finite differences, across rings of up to twelve states, affinities $0.25\le F\le12$, and chords $0.002\le g\le64$, all $420$ ratios exceeding one and increasing, the smallest $1.0000739$ at the smallest chord, after finite-difference artifacts at ten states were exposed and eliminated.  The frontier laws of Conjectures~\ref{ag2} to~\ref{ag6} were tested by multistart global optimization over full antisymmetric couplings, not random sampling: recruitment stayed ordered on six spectra including near-degenerate and widely split ones, the two-mode support held with off-block leakage below $2\times10^{-5}$, the frontier arcs accelerated with a slope reset at recruitment and hit the trace ceiling at finite budget to $10^{-6}$, no dense coupling beat the pair envelope for the frequency in adversarial maximization across four spectra and five budgets per spectrum, and adversarial minimization of the eigenvalue separation at $99.5$ percent of the predicted cheapest cost left separations above $10^{-2}$ while the predicted pair coalesces to machine precision.  The envelope correspondence of Proposition~\ref{ag:env} holds to $3.6\times10^{-15}$ on the qubit, the qutrit optimizer of Conjecture~\ref{ag7} aligned with the accessibility-restricted prediction to cosine $1.0000$, and the basin law of Proposition~\ref{ag:basin} reproduced the exact $\eps/\kappa_{\mathrm{eig}}$ measure within sampling error at every tested distance from the exceptional point, with the scaled condition number matching $\sqrt{h_c/2}$ to three digits.  The four optimizer-level negative findings, the failure of exceptional-point pinning on rings of four and five states, the infinite-budget escape of the three-state frontier, the vacuity of the entangling-resonance criterion on nondegenerate products, and the orbit-range obstruction that voids the tangent-rank capacity principle, exhibited on a generic qutrit whose slow coordinate ranges over $[0.18,0.51]$ and never vanishes, are recorded in the part preamble as the controls that fixed its scope.

\emph{Part XVII.}  The Part XVII verification programme combined exact orthant-probability computation, process-level simulation, exhaustive enumeration, and high-precision arithmetic, with every optimizer-level claim adjudicated against integration noise by paired Monte Carlo on common random samples.  The staircase of Conjecture~\ref{ah1} was mapped by exact orthant sums, the three-active, four-active, and full-simplex phases of the five-variable family separated at scales near $0.15$ and $0.6$, unrestricted eighteen-parameter optimization at scale $0.35$ converging to the four-active configuration with paired-Monte-Carlo margin $+3.4\times10^{-3}\pm1.5\times10^{-5}$ over the simplex on one hundred million common samples, and two earlier apparent exceedances at the same scales exposed as noise by the same adjudicator.  The closure ratios of Conjecture~\ref{ah2} rose monotonically to $1.000000$ on random geometries and to $0.998$ on the equilateral one; the elasticity of Conjecture~\ref{ah3} never exceeded $0.334$ over eighty-three geometries, twelve scales each, and degenerate shapes, against the conjectured bound one half and the proved pairwise constant $0.1472$; and the curvature of Conjecture~\ref{ah4} was driven to machine zero exactly on collinear configurations by exact polar quadrature, with the expansion residual converging to the exact $q$ like $\sqrt t$.  The thinning formulas were tested on genuine moving-maximum processes of twelve million steps, the Bernoulli response matching to ratios $0.95$ to $0.99$ and the systematic resonance reproducing $\theta\,\E R_m$ at every modulus including the exact one-third resonance; the occupancy censuses enumerated $6437$ canonical sets of size at most six through diameter eighteen and $3312$ of size at most seven through diameter fourteen, found ten collisions, every one a homometric pair, verified Bloom's pair occupancy-equivalent at every modulus, and separated the homometric pair $\{0,1,3,8,10,14\}$, $\{0,1,7,9,11,14\}$ by occupancy at modulus five.  The angular-topology laws were tested with an independent $\mathbb F_2$ Vietoris--Rips implementation: the Hausdorff distance of top-$k$ angular samples tracked the two-term rate within factors $0.55$ to $1.22$ across $k=50$ to $3200$, the ring diagrams showed a single dominant loop with death $0.3123$ against the analytic $0.3118$ and bottleneck error falling from $0.115$ to $0.049$, and the leakage crossover switched recovery exactly across ratio one, bottleneck error $0.075$ to $0.090$ below against $0.143$ to $0.156$ above.  The tomography dichotomy held to $4.5\times10^{-16}$ at the integer power against $2.0\times10^{-3}$ at the fractional one, with effective ranks three against fifteen at tolerance $10^{-12}$ and oscillating-witness ratios falling from $0.70$ to $0.048$; the identifiability threshold showed a fifty-solution continuum one measurement below the count, forty-digit Newton polishing collapsed a spurious ten-fold multiplicity at a near-degenerate instance into the single truth, exposed the two genuine second mixtures at three atoms, and dissolved both one measurement higher.  The design ladder was verified in fifty-digit arithmetic with sup-error slopes $-1.001$, $-2.002$, $-3.004$, $-4.004$ for deterministic, two-point, and the exact rational three-point and four-point ladder laws, the Fr\'echet shape bias fell from $+0.0396$ to $+0.0017$ under honest Poissonization at three hundred thousand blocks, and the cancellation cusp doubled the tail-error slope from $-0.845$ to $-1.600$ with the critical window tracking $n^{-\beta/(\alpha+4\beta)}$ at constant ratio $0.500$ across six decades.

\emph{Part XVIII.}  The Part XVIII verification programme was built on an independent implementation stack: Vietoris--Rips persistence in degree one by boundary-matrix reduction of the full two-skeleton over the two-element field, exact bottleneck distances by threshold search with augmenting matchings, exact two-Wasserstein matchings with diagonal slots, a one-dimensional Mapper with breadth-first nerve construction, interval tracking for rectangle-decomposable fiber fields, and adaptive time refinement for vineyard events.  The regular-polygon ratio formula was reproduced to $10^{-15}$ through $n=12$; fifteen hundred random circle configurations per $n$ with local optimization at $n=4$ to $10$ never exceeded the regular value, the closest competitor reaching $0.9988$ of it, while the unrestricted planar control search exceeded the hexagon at the factor $1.052$, fixing the circle hypothesis of Conjecture~\ref{ai1} and refuting the deposited planar claim.  The greedy saturation ratio ran $1.990$, $2.014$, $2.032$, $2.000$ at $m=24$ to $128$ on the circle against the analytic bar and $1.955$ to $2.019$ on the ellipse, and the projection threshold fit $m^*=5.92\log q+1.00$ across $q=4$ to $256$ with maximum residual $1.4$, the $q=64$ transition rising from $0.00$ at $m=14$ through $0.45$ at $m=24$ to $0.92$ at $m=44$.  A true alternating-minimization Fr\'echet mean over five hundred diagrams per prevalence tracked the flat shrinkage law at ratios $0.98$ to $1.02$ across prevalences $0.1$ to $0.9$, margin shrinkage to three noise scales leaving the deviation at the $0.02$ sampling floor, and the grouping-swap frequency ran $0$, $0$, $0.0027$, $0.0103$, $0.0307$ at noise scales $0.15$ to $0.60$ under margin one, the observed logarithms decaying faster than $\gamma^2/4\sigma^2$.  The Mapper phase calculus was confronted with four hundred phases per scale: empirical survival matched the proved kernel to three decimals at overlaps $0.30$ and $0.45$, a first candidate kernel with onset at $\ell/h=\alpha$ being refuted by the same phase data before the span criterion fixed the onset at one; two-cycle additivity held within $0.0055$ over twenty-eight scales spanning both kinks, the curve passing value one exactly at the smaller span; and the discretized dither estimator at mesh $10^{-3}$ showed bias between $-1.7\times10^{-4}$ and $-4\times10^{-5}$ with variance ratio $1.000$ to $s^2/12$ at all three cover resolutions.  One-direction tracking reconstructed one hundred sixteen of one hundred twenty random rectangle modules exactly, with zero corner error among successes, the four failures diagnosed as artifacts of the greedy tracker at coincidental crossings, none a collision of fiber fields; corner displacement stayed below $0.48$ of the three-direction metric over thirty perturbed pairs with median $0.26$, the empirical profile Lipschitz constant stayed below $22.1$, and the near-maximal slope fraction never fell below $0.017$.  Kernel distance ran two-sidedly against transport in $[0.90,2.75]$ over eight hundred separated pairs, with sketch deviation halving at each fourfold frequency increase from $0.10$ at $M=16$ to $0.0087$ at $M=1024$; sixty adversarial collision searches at the Whitney count kept the evaluation gap above $2.0\times10^{-2}$ with full-rank Jacobians throughout; exact-moment multistart inversion found a unique diagram at $2m$, $3m$, and $4m$ moments for $m=2$ and $m=3$ across one hundred fifty starts each; and exact vineyard counts at $n=6$ to $14$ grew at log-log exponent $2.36$ against the local slope $2.45$ of $n^2\log n$, twenty to thirty times below the quartic count.

\emph{Part XX.}  The Part XX verification programme evaluates two exact closed forms independently of the source computation.  The DOZZ modulus of Conjecture~\ref{ak1} was recomputed from the Barnes integral representation of $\Upsilon_b$ by a real-integrand quadrature sharing no code with the deposited scan, reducing the spectral curvature to the three surviving modulus factors of Proposition~\ref{ak:basic}: over $b\in\{0.5,0.8,1,1.3\}$, external charges filling $Q/3\le a<Q/2$, and momenta from $P=0.15$ to $3.5$, every discrete second derivative of $\log M_a$ was strictly negative, the least negative maximum being about $-5.6$.  Both boundary controls reproduced: the sub-chamber charge $a=0.55$ at $b=1$ gave a positive maximum curvature near $+1.78$, and the full three-charge Hessian of $\log|C_1|$ at $(1.3,1.3,1.3)$ carried a large positive eigenvalue, of order two hundred against two negative eigenvalues near $-54$, so the one-dimensional interior-chamber statement is the surviving one.  The Brownian-annulus density of Conjecture~\ref{ak2} was rebuilt by numerically inverting the exact Mellin transform of $\log X_\tau$ and multiplying by the exact Dedekind-eta factor, with the second logarithmic-modulus derivative of the product evaluated on a grid $\tau\in[0.02,30]$ for boundary ratios $x$ from $0.05$ to $20$: the maximum curvature stayed negative across this moderate range, from about $-0.43$ to $-0.58$, with the $x\mapsto1/x$ symmetry to the evaluated precision; but extending the range exposes the large-boundary-ratio tail, where the curvature turns positive---$+0.380$ at $x=e^5$, $\tau=0.30$, tending to the positive limit $\mathcal C_\infty(0.30)=0.9746$---so Conjecture~\ref{ak2} is resolved false, its deposited scan having reached only the moderate ratios.  The DOZZ law of Conjecture~\ref{ak1} remains checkable but unproved, a rigorous proof requiring continuous rather than gridwise curvature control.


\emph{Part XXI.}  The Part XXI diagnostics are reduced-model, exact-anchor, and prerequisite-scaling checks, never evaluations of the singular laws themselves.  Independent recomputation confirmed the exact anchors of Proposition~\ref{al:anchors}: the three-vortex collapse condition holds exactly for $\Gamma=(1,1,-\tfrac12)$ and integration of the planar system from a vanishing-angular-impulse configuration contracted the core to about $2.4\%$ of its initial diameter while the spectator-to-core scale separation amplified; the Fourier-reduced degenerate-shear generator returned enhanced-dissipation exponents $0.32$, $0.53$, $0.63$ for bracket depths $m=1,2,3$ against $m/(m+2)=0.33,0.50,0.60$; the homogeneity-reduced generalized-SQG neck ODE reproduced $d(t)\sim(T-t)^{1/\beta}$ to three digits with $d\,\kappa_{\max}$ of order one; and the scale-invariant Frenet pair of a modulated helix was dilation-invariant in total curvature to relative error $5\times10^{-15}$.  For the two-dimensional Euler laws a pseudo-spectral run showed the bulk enstrophy quantiles moving far more slowly than the pointwise gradient and a strong negative correlation between $\log\max|\nabla\omega|$ and the near-maximal-gradient area; for the exact-Beltrami controls the ABC field annihilated the Lamb vector to root-mean-square about $10^{-14}$ of a Taylor--Green comparison.  Every conjecture in the part is, several as conditional on an unproven Type-I singularity, and the attributions of Conjectures~\ref{al5}, \ref{al8}, and~\ref{al14} and the elevated novelty caveat of Conjecture~\ref{al11} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.


\emph{Part XXII.}  The Part XXII metric-geometry statements are continuum-limit laws; the diagnostics are algebraic anchors and finite Liouville first-passage-percolation or mated-CRT surrogates whose finite-size biases are reported rather than hidden, and the field-theory statements are tested in the exact global-block limit only.  Independent recomputation confirmed the algebraic layer of Proposition~\ref{am:triangle}: the exponents $p_\gamma=d_\gamma/2$, $H_\gamma=2/d_\gamma$, $\alpha_\gamma=1+2/d_\gamma$ satisfy $p_\gamma=1/H_\gamma=1/(\alpha_\gamma-1)$ and reduce to $2,\tfrac12,\tfrac32$ at $d_\gamma=4$, and the affine star spectrum hits $s_1=d_\gamma$, $s_3=2$, and $5-k$ at the Brownian point.  For the field-theory laws an independent evaluation of the exact global $SL(2)$ sphere block gave strictly positive discrete likelihood-ratio slopes (Conjecture~\ref{am9}); exact-$\Upsilon_b$ DOZZ quadrature at $b=1$ combined with the global block gave negative four-point curvature throughout the interior chamber and positive curvature at the excluded charge $a=0.55$ (Conjecture~\ref{am10}); the global torus-descendant proxy gave negative thermal log-ratio slopes (Conjecture~\ref{am11}); and a five-point coupled DOZZ/global-block proxy had negative-definite finite-difference Hessians (Conjecture~\ref{am12}).  Every conjecture in the part is, the field-theory statements with their descendant contributions tested only in the global-block limit, and the attributions of Conjectures~\ref{am1} and~\ref{am5} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.


\emph{Part XXIII.}  The Part XXIII statements are hydrodynamic scaling limits; the diagnostics test event-count scalings, conservation, reduced linearizations, and exact ODE reductions only.  Independent recomputation confirmed the reductions of Proposition~\ref{an:reductions}: the fatigue ODE has finite hitting time iff $p<1$ and integrated mobility $1/(2\rho(1-\rho))$ for every $p$; the occupation-trap linearization has explicit residual $v_\infty=e^{\Delta/(a\bar\rho)}v_0$, matched by the conservative nonlinear finite-difference solver to four digits with mass error $10^{-16}$; the crowding-thinned successful-reset hazard has tail exponent $\beta(1-\rho)$, fitted to $0.013$ at densities $0.1,0.4,0.7$; the codimension-one catalyst contribution scales as $N^{\theta-1}$, reproducing the subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes at $\theta=\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32$; the matched moving-membrane scaling keeps the rescaled membrane variance and slow-bond attempts per dwell order one; and the crossing-budget exhaustion time concentrates on its predicted value with $N^{-1/2}$ fluctuations.  The single shared boundary clock had coefficient of variation near $0.67$ that did not vanish, forcing the random-clock form of Conjecture~\ref{an6}, and the odd cross-current of Conjecture~\ref{an11} reversed with chirality while all color masses were conserved.  Every conjecture in the part is, and the high overlaps with prior work of Conjectures~\ref{an10}, \ref{an11}, \ref{an13}, and~\ref{an15} against~\cite{Colantoni26,DeCarloGabrielliGoncalves25,DankovicMMY26,FrancoFrancoGoncalves26} are recorded where they occur, so those statements should be read with the corresponding caution.


\emph{Part XXIV.}  The Part XXIV visited-set statements are exact finite-state laws tested by exact augmented-chain $(X_t,V_t)$ propagation with the sparse matrix exponential, not by trajectory sampling.  Independent recomputation confirmed the proved layer of Proposition~\ref{ao:basic}: the ray invariants (stationarity, traffic, and escape rates constant to $10^{-15}$), the endpoint spectral bounds, and the even-analytic dependence of visited-set laws on $\alpha$.  The alternating-derivative hierarchy of Conjecture~\ref{ao1} was checked over moments one to four, difference orders one to four, escort exponents $\gamma\in\{0,\tfrac12,1\}$, and several lags on chains of sizes three to six with no violation beyond roundoff; the unicyclic range dominance of Conjecture~\ref{ao3} and the cycle coverage dominance of Conjecture~\ref{ao4} were checked exhaustively over range and mass thresholds with no violation, the latter cross-checked against Gillespie simulation, after an earlier apparent violation was traced to comparing probabilities at $\alpha$-dependent times and eliminated by a fixed-time comparison; and no ray among thousands of general and stressed families exhibited two interior maxima of the slow edge (Conjecture~\ref{ao2}).  The refuted companions are retained as controls: a fresh high-precision search reproduced a bidirected six-state ray on which the fast edge $h(\alpha)$ strictly increases by more than $0.6$ at $40$-digit precision, refuting whole-ray fast-edge monotonicity, and an eight-state ray realizes an interior maximum of the slow edge followed by a shallow minimum and endpoint rebound, refuting its global unimodality.  Conjecture~\ref{ao1} is checked only to finite derivative order and Conjecture~\ref{ao2} is the part's strongest statement.

\emph{Part XXV.}  The Part XXV statements are asymptotic-independence and universality laws, so their diagnostics can only exclude gross finite-size obstructions and cannot certify independence; the exact identities of Proposition~\ref{ap:basic} are, however, checkable outright.  Independent recomputation, sharing no code with the source diagnostics, confirmed the marginal anchors and the exact identities: the $\{0,1\}$ singularity probability over $\mathbb F_p$ approaches $c_p=1-\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$ with the summable tilt $c_p-1/p=O(p^{-2})$; the exact Parseval identity $\chi^2(\mu_{w,N}\Vert U_N)=\sum_{\rho\ne\mathbf1}|\E_w\chi_\rho|^2$ was verified against a from-scratch enumeration of $S_N^2$ for $w=[x,y]x$ through $N=6$, whose $N^2\chi^2$ and $N^2D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ stay of order one, consistent with the exponent two; the $p$-adic root count of a Littlewood polynomial approaches $(p-1)/(p+1)$; and Rostam's $\pi/4$ core normalization was reproduced from exact RSK sampling of poissonized Plancherel partitions.  The cross observables behaved as the independence conjectures require: odd-prime spectral-edge and cokernel-nullity correlations were small and sign-unstable while the $p=2$ correlation persisted, Plancherel core and edge correlations fluctuated around zero and shrank with $t$, and real-near-unit and simple-root-modulo-$p$ correlations were small and slowly decaying, the last the weakest decorrelation and Conjecture~\ref{ap5} correspondingly the least confident.  These are falsification diagnostics, not proofs, and the finite-size correlations are consistent with either transient constraints or genuine slow-decaying dependence.

\emph{Part XXVI.}  The Part XXVI statements are asymptotic laws for invariants whose exact computation is infeasible at scale, so the diagnostics test exact finite calibrations and reduced models, not the laws themselves.  Independent recomputation, sharing no code with the source diagnostics, confirmed every proved anchor of Proposition~\ref{aq:basic}: a from-scratch implementation of the defining Kazhdan--Lusztig recursion reproduced the closed cycle formula $P_{U_{k-1,k}}(1)=\sum_i\binom ki\binom{k-i-2}i/(i+1)$ exactly for $3\le k\le25$, with $k^{-1}\log P_{U_{k-1,k}}(1)$ rising toward $\log3$; the Mirzakhani--Petri intensity integrates to $\Lambda(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/4+\varepsilon^4/96+\cdots$, giving the tail constant $\tfrac14$ to five decimals, and the collar normalization $\pi\,\mathrm{cap}(\ell)/\ell\to1$ reproduced; the tropical matching experiment at profile $(-2,0,-1,0)$ gave $\sqrt N$-scaled displacements falling from $0.095$ to $0.009$ across $N=4$ to $20$ at $\beta=2\log N$ and stalling near $0.4$ at $\beta=0.75\log N$, locating the double-scaling threshold; and the decategorified proxies, the reduced-Burau determinant exponent near $0.08$ on three-strand walks and the integral symplectic transvection homology exponent near $0.19$, reproduced their calibration scales.  The recorded gaps stand: the Burau and symplectic proxies test decategorified shadows only and cannot witness the homological cancellations of Conjectures~\ref{aq3} and~\ref{aq5}, and no finite computation reaches the Weil--Petersson or double-scaling limits themselves.
